title: ThinkReset: Learnable Intermediate Interface Construction for Bounded-Context Long-Horizon Reasoning
summary: This research introduces "ThinkReset," a method to address issues like context overflow and redundancy accumulation in long chain-of-thought reasoning within bounded context windows. It focuses on improving how AI systems manage and utilize their context/memory.

title: TAPR: Enhancing LLM Performance with a Task-Aware Prompt Rewriter
summary: This work introduces TAPR (Task-Aware Prompt Rewriter), an AI model designed to reformulate user prompts into task-optimized versions to enhance Large Language Model performance. It focuses on a specific AI model's capability.

title: Empowering Cross-Domain Sequential Recommendation with Hybrid Tokenization and Serial-Parallel Decoding

title: An Ontology-Guided, Deduplication-Aware Extraction Layer for Knowledge Graph Construction from Heterogeneous Documents
summary: This paper introduces an ontology-guided, deduplication-aware extraction layer for building knowledge graphs from heterogeneous documents using large language models. It presents a method to improve the consistency and accuracy of information extraction.

title: How Hard Does It Think? Analyzing Step-Aware Reasoning Energy in LLM Chain-of-Thought Trajectories
summary: This research analyzes the step-aware reasoning energy in LLM chain-of-thought trajectories to understand computational effort allocation within the models. It contributes to the interpretability of LLM reasoning processes.

title: Reasoning in Real World Clinical Care: Why Large Language Models Are Not Yet Safe for Autonomous Clinical Decision Support
summary: This paper analyzes the application of Large Language Models (LLMs) in clinical care, discussing their current capabilities and raising concerns about their safety for autonomous clinical decision support.

title: ViSAGE: Constructing Self-Correcting Memories for Long-Form Video Understanding

title: Library Reachability in LSR-Synth: How Anti-Memorization Design Changes the Measurement of Symbolic Discovery
summary: This research explores how anti-memorization design in LSR-Synth alters the measurement of symbolic discovery, aiming to differentiate true discovery from recall in scientific equation benchmarks.

summary: This paper presents a validity audit of several agent-safety benchmarks (R-Judge, InjecAgent, AgentHarm, AgentDojo) to evaluate their consistency in measuring agent safety.

title: SciToolAgent-Evo: An Ontology-Aware Self-Evolving Agent for Open-World Scientific Tool Acquisition
summary: SciToolAgent-Evo describes an ontology-aware, self-evolving Large Language Model agent designed for acquiring and utilizing specialized computational tools in open-world scientific workflows.

title: EarlyDx: An Admission-Anchored Benchmark for Open-Ended Generation of Evidence-Supported ED-Encounter Diagnoses
summary: EarlyDx introduces a new benchmark for evaluating the open-ended generation of evidence-supported diagnoses during emergency department encounters, addressing limitations of existing diagnostic prediction benchmarks.

title: Best Friends, Not Forever: Evaluating Long-Horizon Persona Collapse and Behavioral Drift in AI Companions
summary: This research evaluates long-term issues like 'persona collapse' and 'behavioral drift' in AI companions, examining how these affect stable roles and shared histories in repeated social interactions.

title: Fragility of Value under Imperfect Alignment
summary: This paper discusses the 'fragility of value' in AI safety, highlighting concerns that optimizing for imperfect proxies of human values under imperfect alignment could lead to catastrophic outcomes.

title: Identifying Informative Environments for Cognition Parameter Inference via Bayesian Experimental Design
summary: This study explores how to identify informative environments for inferring cognition parameters using Bayesian experimental design, aiming to improve computational cognitive modeling.

summary: NeSyFS introduces a neuro-symbolic fast-slow thinking framework for Large Language Model agents to operate effectively under partial observability in various applications like self-reflection and scientific discovery.

title: MerchantBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Long-Term Coherence in E-Commerce Operations
summary: MerchantBench introduces a new benchmark for evaluating the long-term coherence of Large Language Model agents in e-commerce operations, focusing on sustained purposeful behavior over extended periods.

title: Scaling Scientific Discovery Environments for Turn-Level Agentic RL
summary: This research focuses on scaling scientific discovery environments for turn-level Agentic Reinforcement Learning, enabling Large Language Model agents to conduct long-horizon scientific analysis.

title: MMShopBench: A Real-Log Benchmark for Multimodal, Multi-Turn Shopping Agents
summary: MMShopBench is a new real-log benchmark for multimodal, multi-turn shopping agents, designed to evaluate AI assistants in complex online shopping scenarios involving images and dialogue.

title: Evidence-Grounded Constraint Checking in Construction Documents
summary: This paper presents an evidence-grounded pipeline for constraint checking in professional construction documents, extracting facts and executing rules to analyze text, geometry, and revisions.

title: On the Generalization of Steering Vectors for Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness
summary: This study investigates the generalization of steering vectors to ensure the faithfulness of chain-of-thought reasoning in Large Language Models, which is important for AI safety and interpretability.

title: A Generalized-Bayes Perspective on Counterfactual Explanations: Posterior-Based Decision-Making and Evaluation
summary: This paper provides a Generalized-Bayes perspective on counterfactual explanations, exploring their theoretical basis for enhancing the interpretability of machine learning models.

title: Harnessing the Wisdom of LLM Crowds through Complementarity-Driven Iterative Collaboration
summary: This research explores a method for coordinating multiple Large Language Models through complementarity-driven iterative collaboration to overcome individual model limitations in enterprise settings.

title: CAGE: Certified Authorization under Typed-Return Uncertainty for Tool-Using Agents
summary: CAGE proposes a system for certified authorization for tool-using Large Language Model agents, addressing reliability and safety challenges under typed-return uncertainty during runtime.

title: MirrorCraft: Paired Evaluation under Hidden Rule Changes in Minecraft
summary: MirrorCraft introduces a paired evaluation method for LLM-based agents in Minecraft, designed to test their adaptability under hidden rule changes rather than fixed game mechanics.

title: Don't Mix Rewards, Mix Policies: Policy Decomposition and Optimization for Multi-Reward RL
summary: This research proposes a policy decomposition and optimization method for multi-reward reinforcement learning to enable Large Language Models to adapt their behavior to different human values and use cases.

title: Tool Specifications Matter: Uncovering and Mitigating Safety Risks in AI Agents
summary: This paper examines how external tools used by AI agents can introduce and exacerbate safety risks, noting that large language models (LLMs) become less safe when deployed as agents.

title: MAGA: Multi-Platform Self-Fusion of GUI Agents via Structured Action Distillation
summary: This research introduces 'MAGA', a method for multi-platform self-fusion of GUI agents, aiming to consolidate specialized domain-specific GUI agents for broader deployment and improved user experience.

title: Beyond Component Testing: Validating Agentic AI Systems
summary: This article discusses the need for new validation practices for agentic AI systems, which involve multi-step trajectories with planning, tool use, memory, and adaptation, going beyond traditional component testing.

title: ModelEquivBench: Certifying Multi-Relational Evaluation of LLM-Generated Optimization Models
summary: This work introduces 'ModelEquivBench', a benchmark for certifying multi-relational evaluation of optimization models generated by large language models, addressing limitations of current evaluation methods.

title: Beyond Retrieval: Analytic Memory for Multimodal Agents
summary: This paper proposes 'Analytic Memory' for multimodal agents, which supports not only retrieving relevant information but also computing over accumulated observations, extending beyond traditional retrieval memory.

title: Self-Play Meets Skill Evolution: Self-Evolving Search Agents that Pose, Solve, and Remember
summary: This paper presents 'Self-Evolving Search Agents' that can pose, solve, and remember problems, using external skill memories to preserve procedural experience and shape future practice in self-play systems.

title: AMTFV: Agentic Mathematical Tool-Flow Verification for LLM Self-Correction
summary: This research introduces 'AMTFV' (Agentic Mathematical Tool-Flow Verification) as a method for LLM self-correction, enhancing the reliability of mathematical problem-solving by verifying candidate answers through tool-flow.

title: LEMUR: Learning to Align with Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning from Preference Feedback
summary: This paper introduces 'LEMUR', a system for learning to align AI systems using multi-objective reinforcement learning from preference feedback, addressing the challenge of multiple competing objectives in real-world decision-making.

title: AgentHPOBench: A Benchmark For Evaluating LLM Agents as Sequential Hyperparameter Optimizers
summary: This research introduces 'AgentHPOBench', a new benchmark specifically designed for evaluating large language model agents as sequential hyperparameter optimizers, assessing their ability to conduct experiments.

title: ExtractBench: A Benchmark for Schema-Guided Enterprise Document Extraction
summary: This paper introduces 'ExtractBench', a new benchmark for schema-guided enterprise document extraction, which evaluates agents' ability to faithfully extract information based on user-defined schemas.

title: Scaffolding Critical Engagement with GenAI: Transforming Ethnic Minority Preparatory Students' Collaborative Discourse in Prompt Engineering Tasks
summary: This paper explores how scaffolding can encourage critical engagement with Generative AI among ethnic minority students in prompt engineering, addressing potential benefits for educational equity and risks of cognitive laziness.

title: Topology-Aware Data Movement for Disaggregated GPU Inference
summary: This research investigates topology-aware data movement strategies for disaggregated GPU inference in data centers, aiming to solve networking problems arising from transferring large KV caches between separate GPU pools for LLMs.

title: The Asymmetric Effects of Knowledge Distillation on Bias in Small Language Models
summary: This study demonstrates that knowledge distillation in small instruction-tuned language models can have asymmetric effects on bias, showing improvements in context-following for biased baselines when using a Gemma-2-9B teacher.

title: The Formalism Trap: Are LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluators Blinded by Consensus Mimicry under Social Load?
summary: This paper introduces the 'Agentic Formalism Trap' and 'Evaluative Dissonance Index', critiquing how LLM-as-a-Judge systems may prioritize procedural adherence over semantic truth under adversarial conditions.

title: Seeing Differently: Modeling Interpretive Perspectives in Computational Creativity using a Four-World Framework
summary: This paper proposes a 'Four-World Framework' for modeling interpretive perspectives in computational creativity, arguing that artistic meaning is perspective-dependent and current evaluation frameworks are too objective.

title: Looks Right, Works Right: A Project-Level Benchmark for Multi-Screen Mobile App Generation
summary: This research introduces a 'Project-Level Benchmark' for multi-screen mobile app generation, highlighting the limitations of current design-to-code models in creating complete, buildable mobile products.

title: ConnectED: A Curriculum-Aligned AI System for Vietnamese Instructional Lesson Planning and Student Learning
summary: This paper presents 'ConnectED', a human-centered AI system built on VietEduQwen that supports the full instructional lifecycle in Vietnamese education, linking lesson design, student learning, and feedback.

title: Why It Hurts: Identifying the Drivers of Negative Thoughts in Emotional Support Conversations
summary: This research investigates the use of large language models (LLMs) in emotional support tasks, focusing on identifying the drivers of negative thoughts in conversations for effective negative thought reframing.

title: COSI-Lab: Conference Living Lab for Modeling Multi-Perspective Multimodal Social Intention
summary: This paper introduces 'COSI-Lab', a multimodal, multi-sensor dataset collected during an interdisciplinary scientific workshop, designed for modeling multi-perspective multimodal social intention.

title: Unanticipated Effects of Generative AI on Expertise Pathways and Performance Perception in System Administration
summary: This study investigates the profound impacts of generative AI on professional expertise and performance perceptions within system administration, highlighting shifts in practice beyond immediate productivity gains.

title: HenTwin: A Multimodal Digital Twin Framework for Longitudinal Biological State Monitoring in Laying Hens
summary: HenTwin is introduced as a multimodal digital twin framework with a five-layer IoT architecture designed for formalizing and monitoring the biological state of laying hen flocks.

title: Evaluating Federated Pre-Training: On the Reliability of Downstream Fine-Tuning and Intrinsic Evaluation
summary: This paper examines the challenges of evaluating federated pre-training, focusing on the reliability of downstream fine-tuning and intrinsic evaluation methods given varying client participation and data availability.

title: Sensitivity Analysis of GRU, LSTM and Transformer Encoder in Classification of Automated Driving Systems
summary: This research conducts a sensitivity analysis of GRU, LSTM, and Transformer Encoder models for classifying automated driving systems, aiming to improve independent monitoring for safety.

title: Guarantees on Dynamical System Distinguishability for LLM Token Generation
summary: This theoretical work provides guarantees on the distinguishability of dynamical systems used to model and compare token generation trajectories of large language models.

title: LAWFUL: Law-Aligned Witness for Faithful Use of Latents
summary: The LAWFUL framework investigates whether neural networks learn governing laws as structured knowledge and if their internal computations faithfully use these representations, addressing key interpretability gaps.

title: MPP-GNN: Subject-Adaptive Community Detection for fMRI-Based Alzheimer's Disease Classification
summary: MPP-GNN is proposed as a subject-adaptive graph neural network method for community detection in fMRI data, demonstrating potential for classifying brain disorders like Alzheimer's disease.

title: Metaphor-Induced Algorithmic Steering: Cross-Domain Procedural Transfer in LLM Code Generation
summary: This paper explores how metaphors in natural language can lead to unintended 'algorithmic steering' and unwanted behaviors in large language models during code generation, impacting cross-domain procedural transfer.

title: LARA: Lightweight Adapters in the Residual Stream for Composable Adaptation and Alignment
summary: LARA (Lightweight Additive Residual Adaptation) is presented as a method for efficient adaptation of frozen models by operating in their residual stream, offering a lightweight alternative to methods like LoRA.

title: Hierarchical Copula-Gumbel-Top-\texorpdfstring{$K$}{K} Routing: Two-Sided Dependence Control for Frozen Mixture-of-Experts at Fixed Per-Token Routing Laws
summary: This research introduces Hierarchical Copula-Gumbel-Top-K Routing, a method for controlling two-sided dependence in the routing choices of Mixture-of-Experts models at fixed per-token routing laws.

summary: This article synthesizes technological advancements for detecting and managing cognitive impairment in older adults, addressing trends, challenges, and future directions for this critical health challenge.

title: SEDR-Seq2P: A Lightweight Dilated Residual Sequence-to-Point Network for Multi-Task Industrial NILM
summary: SEDR-Seq2P is introduced as a lightweight dilated residual sequence-to-point network designed for multi-task industrial Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) to overcome challenges like measurement noise and concurrent machine operation.

title: Predicting Steel Fatigue Life from Micrographs Using Physics-Informed Deep Learning
summary: This work demonstrates predicting steel fatigue life from micrographs using physics-informed deep learning, offering an alternative to traditional time-consuming mechanical testing.

title: Mitigating Class-Tail Undercoverage in Medical Vision-Language Models under Clinical Shift
summary: This paper addresses mitigating class-tail undercoverage in medical vision-language models under clinical shift, ensuring more reliable and equitable performance across individual disease classes despite overall marginal coverage.

title: MMFGU: Multimodal Federated Graph Unlearning
summary: MMFGU (Multimodal Federated Graph Unlearning) is proposed as a method enabling collaborative training of graph models across diverse multimodal data while supporting efficient and fine-grained data unlearning requests.

title: Mirror Learning
summary: Mirror learning is presented as a novel framework for acquiring actionable policies from passive, third-person observations, expanding upon traditional imitation learning methods like behavior cloning.

title: TAGTorch: A PyTorch Library for Geometry, Topology, and Symmetry-Aware Machine Learning
summary: TAGTorch is introduced as a PyTorch library designed to facilitate geometry, topology, and symmetry-aware machine learning, enabling researchers to integrate these structural properties into neural network applications.

title: Feature Interaction Modeling for Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Neural Operators
summary: This research embeds feature interaction modules into physics-informed neural networks and neural operators to enhance their expressiveness for solving partial differential equations.

title: Representations from Pretrained Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials as Coarse Coordinates for Material Generation and Evaluation
summary: This paper explores using representations from pre-trained machine-learning interatomic potentials as coarse coordinates for generative inorganic crystal structure design and evaluation.

title: Distilling Knowledge from Large Language Models into Lightweight Reinforcement Learning Agents for Autonomous Cyber Operations
summary: This research details a method for distilling knowledge from large language models into lightweight reinforcement learning agents, enabling them to perform autonomous cyber operations effectively.

title: Hypergradient-based Bilevel Reinforcement Learning with Improved Sample Complexity
summary: This paper introduces a hypergradient-based approach to bilevel reinforcement learning (RL), a framework used for problems like meta-learning and RL from human feedback, aiming to improve sample complexity. It focuses on the theoretical and algorithmic aspects of this advanced RL method.

title: An analysis of machine learning approaches for enhancing decision-making in complex discrete choice tasks
summary: This analysis explores how machine learning approaches can enhance decision-making in complex discrete choice tasks, particularly for policy-making. It focuses on using data-driven methods to improve preference elicitation beyond traditional parametric models.

title: Reflection or Re-Generation? Why LLM Revision Fails Where Human Revision Succeeds
summary: This paper investigates why large language model (LLM) revision often fails compared to human revision, introducing the Human-LLM Reflection Framework (HRF). It aims to clarify whether LLM reflection capabilities truly resemble human reasoning and revision processes.

title: Gated Q-learning: Add Off-Policy Bias to Taste
summary: This research introduces Gated Q-learning, a new method designed to address the long-standing challenge of managing off-policy bias in Q-learning for sample-efficient reinforcement learning. It explores an alternative to the binary choice of eliminating bias at the cost of truncated eligibility traces.

title: Learning Optimal Dynamic Matching via Graph Neural Networks
summary: This paper develops a value-based reinforcement learning framework using Graph Neural Networks to solve the problem of optimal dynamic matching in evolving weighted graphs. The research aims to balance immediate matching value against potential future opportunities.

title: Latent Lie-Poisson Neural Networks (LLPNNs): Discovering the motion of Lie-Poisson systems through observable data and latent dynamics
summary: This paper introduces Latent Lie-Poisson Neural Networks (LLPNNs), a new type of structure-preserving neural network designed to discover the motion of Lie-Poisson systems from observable data and latent dynamics. These networks are crucial for long-term prediction of Hamiltonian systems in various scientific domains.

title: FairDiffuseVQVAE: Sampling-Time Fairness in Tabular Diffusion via Conditional Refinement of Vector-Quantized Latents
summary: This paper introduces FairDiffuseVQVAE, a novel method that enhances tabular diffusion models by incorporating sampling-time fairness through conditional refinement of vector-quantized latents. The goal is to mitigate downstream classifier bias in synthetic tabular data generation.

title: Shapley-Value-Based Feature Attribution for Data Masking
summary: This study proposes a novel framework that adapts the Shapley-value-based feature attribution approach for data masking to address data privacy concerns. The method aims to enhance privacy protections in scenarios involving widespread access to personal data.

title: Overcoming the Weakest-Link Effect in LLM-Driven Program Optimization via Heterogeneous Edit Recombination
summary: This paper addresses the weakest-link effect in large language model (LLM)-driven program optimization by proposing a method of heterogeneous edit recombination. The research aims to improve LLMs' ability to solve complex scientific problems represented as programs.

title: Mining Verdict Boundaries for Neural Network Verification
summary: This research focuses on mining verdict boundaries to enhance the Branch and Bound (BaB) procedure for complete neural network verification. It aims to improve the adaptive partitioning and verification of subproblems in complex neural network verification tasks.

title: Efficient LLM Adversarial Training via Low-Rank Defense and Circuit-Guided Surrogates
summary: This paper proposes methods for efficient large language model (LLM) adversarial training using low-rank defense and circuit-guided surrogates to reduce computational costs. The research aims to make adversarial training a more feasible defense against adversarial attacks at scale.

title: Beyond Feature and Structure Alignment: Learning Transferable Propagation Knowledge for Graph Foundation Models
summary: This research explores learning transferable propagation knowledge to enhance Graph Foundation Models (GFMs), enabling knowledge transfer across diverse domains. It aims to improve GFMs' ability to generalize to unseen graphs beyond traditional in-domain graph learning methods.

title: Dynamics-aware identification of governing equations from sparse and noisy data
summary: This paper introduces a dynamics-aware identification method to recover governing equations from sparse and noisy data, addressing the unreliability of derivative estimates in SINDy and PDE-FIND. The research aims to improve the accuracy of identifying ordinary and partial differential equations.

title: DFSC: Error-Controlled Differentiable Mittag-Leffler Propagation for Fractional Scientific Machine Learning
summary: This paper introduces DFSC, an error-controlled differentiable Mittag-Leffler propagation method for fractional scientific machine learning, focusing on numerical operators that can be differentiated, batched, and composed with neural networks. It addresses the need for efficient and accurate computation of fractional evolution.

title: Learning Lookahead Lemmas for Neural Network Verification
summary: This paper introduces an inprocessing framework for neural network verification driven by the lookahead procedure, which learns new lemmas over unstable ReLU phases. The method aims to improve state-of-the-art neural network verifiers that typically use branch-and-bound.

title: Autonomous Repair for Multi-Agent Systems via Monte-Carlo Tree Search
summary: This paper proposes an autonomous repair mechanism for multi-agent systems using Monte-Carlo Tree Search to locate and correct agent mistakes. The goal is to reduce manual failure attribution and refinement in complex multi-agent tasks.

title: Benchmarking Frontier Large Language Models Against Official Crash Database Coding Using Police Crash Narratives
summary: This study benchmarks six frontier large language models (LLMs) by comparing their performance in reproducing official crash database coding from police crash narratives. The research aims to evaluate how well LLMs can supplement labor-intensive manual review processes for crash data.

title: Federated Foundation Models Fine-Tuning with Heterogeneous Compressed Clients
summary: This research addresses the resource-asymmetry challenge in federated learning of foundation models by proposing a fine-tuning method with heterogeneous compressed clients. The goal is to enable institutions with valuable domain-specific data to participate despite limitations in hosting large models.

title: DASH-OPD: Discrepancy-Aware Switching with Hysteresis for On-Policy Distillation
summary: This paper introduces DASH-OPD, a discrepancy-aware switching method with hysteresis for on-policy distillation, designed to mitigate exposure bias in multi-turn agent scenarios. It aims to prevent early student errors from leading trajectories away from the teacher's domain.

title: What Is Missing in Surgical Risk Stratification and Outcome Prediction: A Scoping Review of End-to-End Machine Learning Approaches
summary: This scoping review examines the current landscape of end-to-end machine learning approaches for surgical risk stratification and outcome prediction. It identifies gaps in existing methods for early identification of high-risk patients to improve perioperative care.

title: PiDDM: Physics-Informed Differentiable Degradation Modeling for Lithium-Ion Battery State-of-Health Prediction
summary: This research introduces PiDDM, a physics-informed differentiable degradation model for accurately predicting the state-of-health of lithium-ion batteries. It addresses the limitations of purely data-driven models by incorporating physical principles.

title: StraightDP: Geometry-Aware Differential Privacy for Rectified-Flow Transformers
summary: This paper proposes StraightDP, a geometry-aware differential privacy method for rectified-flow transformers used in text-conditioned generative models. It aims to improve utility during differentially private training by analyzing the geometry of rectified flows.

title: Curriculum Matters: Data-Efficient Relational PFN Pretraining with Synthetic Data
summary: This research investigates data-efficient pretraining of Relational Prior-Data Fitted Networks (PFNs) using synthetic data, specifically exploring the effectiveness of different synthetic data generators. It studies their ability to approximate Bayesian inference over relational databases.

title: PluRel-to-RDB-PFN: Schema-Guided Synthetic Relational Pretraining
summary: This study examines whether PluRel, a general-purpose synthetic relational database generator, can be used for schema-guided pretraining of Relational Foundation Models. It addresses the challenge of tightly coupled data generation and model training in existing approaches.

title: HERO: History-Enriched Rollout Training for Long-Horizon Autoregressive Neural Operators
summary: This research introduces HERO, a History-Enriched Rollout Training method for long-horizon autoregressive neural operators. It aims to mitigate error accumulation when applying learned evolution operators recursively for time-dependent partial differential equations.

title: Implicit Machine Learning Force Fields Accelerate Molecular Dynamics Simulations
summary: This paper introduces Implicit Machine Learning Force Fields (I-MLFFs) which use self-consistent fixed-point equations to replace neural network layers. This method accelerates molecular dynamics simulations by enabling reuse of intermediate representations across timesteps.

title: MBDiff: Multi-view Behavior-aware Diffusion Model for Probabilistic Utility Data Imputation
summary: This paper introduces MBDiff, a Multi-view Behavior-aware Diffusion Model designed for probabilistic utility data imputation. The model addresses substantial missing values in utility consumption data collected by sensors and embedded devices.

title: SERUM: State Extraction and Refinement for User Modeling
summary: This paper presents SERUM, a multi-pass framework designed for State Extraction and Refinement for User Modeling in agentic assistants. SERUM extracts finite-state behavioral models from unstructured screen activity to enable proactive and personalized interactions.

title: SAF-OPD: Stable Advantage Fusion for On-Policy Distillation
summary: This research introduces SAF-OPD, a method for Stable Advantage Fusion for On-Policy Distillation in reinforcement learning. It aims to combine the benefits of verifiable rewards and on-policy distillation to improve token-level scoring and exploration.

title: Frugal Bayesian Optimization: Scalable Surrogates for Data- and Resource-Limited Discovery
summary: This study presents a compute-aware analysis of Bayesian Optimization, evaluating surrogate models based on both optimization performance and computational cost. It focuses on scalable surrogates for data- and resource-limited discovery in scientific applications.

title: Assessing the Generalization of Graph Neural Networks for Fault Location Across Increasing Distributed Energy Resource Penetration Levels
summary: This research assesses the generalization capabilities of Graph Neural Networks for fault location in distribution networks with increasing distributed energy resource penetration. It addresses how complex power flows complicate traditional fault location methods.

title: Sample Efficient Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning via Best Policy Identification
summary: This paper presents HBPI-UCRL, a model-based algorithm for sample-efficient hierarchical reinforcement learning that learns high-level and low-level policies simultaneously. The algorithm leverages multi-step transitions at the low level for efficiency.

title: Analysing User Reviews to Identify User Concerns Around Permissions in AI Apps
summary: This analysis identifies user concerns about permissions in AI applications by examining user reviews. It highlights the need for AI mobile app developers to adhere to security and privacy best practices.

title: Versatile On-device Adaptation at the Edge by Unifying Few-shot, Zero-shot, Continual, and In-context Learning
summary: This research explores versatile on-device adaptation for AI at the edge by unifying few-shot, zero-shot, continual, and in-context learning paradigms. It aims to enable smart edge devices to tailor applications to users or patients locally.

title: Cross-Resolution Semantic Learning for Graph Domain Adaptation
summary: This paper proposes a method for Cross-Resolution Semantic Learning for Graph Domain Adaptation. It addresses transferring predictive knowledge between labeled source graphs and unlabeled target graphs under distribution shift.

title: Exploring Block Anomaly Detection In HDFS Log Data Analysis
summary: This research explores block anomaly detection techniques specifically for HDFS log data analysis. It aims to improve the maintenance and reliability of distributed file systems through data-driven methods.

title: Simulation Code Generation for Fluid Systems using Large Language Models: Benchmarking Models and Prompting Strategies
summary: This study benchmarks large language models and prompting strategies for generating simulation code for fluid systems from natural language specifications. It explores the capability of LLMs to translate neutral graph representations into executable code.

title: Ranní výběr: Jak odhalit texty psané AI? A proč Musk tvrdí, že peníze za deset let skončí?
summary: This article discusses methods for detecting texts written by artificial intelligence, as AI-generated content becomes increasingly indistinguishable from human writing. It touches on the broader implications of AI's growing role in text creation.

title: Can LLMs Really Understand Item Difficulty Levels? Implications for Automated Item Generation Using LLMs
summary: This study investigates the ability of Large Language Models (LLMs) to understand and predict item difficulty levels for automated item generation. It examines LLM performance using items from a reading and writing assessment.

title: Imbalanced Data Clustering via Targeted Data Augmentation Using GMM and LLM
summary: This paper introduces a novel unsupervised data augmentation method for imbalanced data clustering in Natural Language Processing. The method integrates Gaussian Mixture Models and Large Language Models to improve the representation of minority topics.

title: Chain-of-Models: Cross-Model Auditing for Bias-Robust LLM Judges
summary: This paper introduces Chain-of-Models (CoM), an automated method to audit Large Language Model (LLM) judges for cognitive biases. It aims to provide a scalable way to measure and improve the bias-robustness of LLM judgments.

title: ZeroR@CHiPSAL 2026: Two-Stage Vision-Language Adaptation with Contrastive Learning for Nepali Meme Classification
summary: This paper presents a system for the CHiPSAL 2026 shared task, focusing on multimodal hate speech and sentiment detection in Nepali memes. The approach uses two-stage vision-language adaptation with contrastive learning.

title: Learning Stateful Predictive Knowledge From Experience
summary: This research explores how LLM agents can learn 'stateful predictive knowledge' from experience, moving beyond episodic hindsight to predictive foresight. It investigates improved learning paradigms for agentic systems.

title: TokenSwap: Benchmarking and Reducing the Modality Gap in Multimodal LLMs
summary: This paper introduces 'TokenSwap' for benchmarking and reducing the modality gap in Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs), which is a discrepancy in responses to semantically equivalent cross-modal inputs. The work aims to measure and improve MLLM consistency.

title: Are the Financial Reasoning from LLMs Credible? A Real World Test over Long-Horizon Statements
summary: This study evaluates the credibility of financial reasoning from Large Language Models (LLMs) through a real-world test over long-horizon statements. It aims to assess LLM capabilities in a domain where existing benchmarks are considered insufficient.

title: The Checking Problem: What must be true before AI ships in a regulated firm
summary: This paper investigates 'The Checking Problem,' analyzing why enterprise AI programs stall in regulated firms, particularly in financial services. It studies the mechanisms across various model families and tool configurations, focusing on real-world application challenges.

title: TELLER: Dual-Path Iterative Preference Optimization for Table Entity Linking
summary: This paper proposes 'TELLER,' a new method utilizing Dual-Path Iterative Preference Optimization for table entity linking. It aims to improve the matching of short cell mentions to knowledge-base entities by effectively using contextual evidence.

title: Self-Supervised Skill Optimization
summary: This research focuses on 'Self-Supervised Skill Optimization' for frozen Large Language Model (LLM) agents, providing reusable procedural guidance. It addresses the challenge of optimizing agent skills when ground-truth feedback is scarce.

title: Benchmarks Are Not Monolithic: Sample-Level Auditing and Orchestration for LLM Evaluation
summary: This paper introduces a dataset-centric meta-evaluation framework for LLM evaluation, arguing that benchmarks are not monolithic. It audits benchmark datasets at the sample level to reveal variations in individual demands.

title: Rolling With Resistance: Preference-Optimized LLM Counselors Can Trade Goal Persistence for Relational Attunement in Motivational Interviewing
summary: This study explores how preference-optimized LLM counselors can balance 'goal persistence' and 'relational attunement' in Motivational Interviewing (MI). It investigates the behavior of AI in a therapeutic application context.

title: Benchmarks Are Not Validation: A System-Level View of Financial LLM Applications
summary: This paper argues that traditional benchmarks are insufficient for validating complex financial LLM applications, advocating for a 'system-level view' of evaluation. It highlights the need for comprehensive assessment beyond model-centric scores.

title: TextCloak: Thwarting Unauthorized LLM Exploitation via RL-Driven Unlearnable Text
summary: This paper proposes 'TextCloak,' an RL-driven method using 'unlearnable text' to thwart unauthorized Large Language Model (LLM) exploitation and privacy leakage. It offers a defense mechanism against ethical concerns related to data usage.

title: Token-Level Diagnosis of Sycophancy in LLMs with Attribution-Guided Steering
summary: This research introduces a 'Token-Level Diagnosis' method with attribution-guided steering to identify 'sycophancy' in Large Language Models (LLMs). It aims to understand and mitigate models matching user beliefs over factual correctness, which impacts reliability.

title: FairFund-Bench: Evaluating Distributive Bias in LLM Resource Allocation
summary: This paper introduces 'FairFund-Bench,' a new benchmark designed to evaluate distributive bias in Large Language Model (LLM) resource allocation. It addresses concerns about biased allocations based on characteristics like race and gender.

title: BLADE: Boundary-Expanded and Layer-Adaptive Dynamic Exit for Efficient LLM Reasoning
summary: This paper proposes 'BLADE' (Boundary-Expanded and Layer-Adaptive Dynamic Exit) for efficient Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning. It aims to reduce wasted computation from long reasoning traces by implementing a dynamic exit strategy.

title: Mixture-of-Translators: Translating KV Caches Across Heterogeneous Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces 'Mixture-of-Translators' to enable translating Key-Value (KV) caches across heterogeneous Large Language Models (LLMs). This allows for reusing contextual memory elements between different model architectures, improving efficiency.

title: PARALLEL: A Prefrontal-Aligned Reinforcement inspired Approach for Language-Model Learning under Explicit Limits
summary: This paper proposes 'PARALLEL,' a prefrontal-aligned reinforcement-inspired approach for language-model learning. It aims to improve model adaptation by applying updates more selectively based on local update benefit rather than uniformly.

title: Tokenizer-Agnostic Engram Module
summary: This paper introduces a 'Tokenizer-Agnostic Engram Module' as an improvement to Deepseek's conditional memory module for Large Language Models. This enhancement makes the memory lookup mechanism independent of the specific tokenizer used.

title: Semantics of Subterfuge: Benchmarking Legal Deception Detection Against General-domain State-of-the-Art
summary: This paper focuses on 'Benchmarking Legal Deception Detection,' comparing NLP-based methods against general-domain state-of-the-art techniques. It aims to measure the effectiveness of data-driven approaches in critical applications like law enforcement.

title: Faster but Different: Diagnosing and Controlling Content Drift in Accelerated Multimodal Diffusion Language Models
summary: This paper diagnoses and controls content drift in accelerated multimodal diffusion language models (dMLLMs), showing how training-free acceleration can silently change generated content compared to unaccelerated outputs.

title: Can Zero-Shot LLMs Predict Child Malnutrition? A Fairness and Temporal Robustness Study
summary: This study evaluates the feasibility, fairness, and temporal robustness of zero-shot large language models (LLMs) in predicting child malnutrition, particularly in South Asia.

title: Authorship Verification of Transcribed German-Language Videos
summary: This work addresses authorship verification in digital text forensics, focusing on verifying authors of transcribed German-language videos, a challenging area with remaining issues.

title: Learning Latent Reasoning Traces for Scalar Reward Models End-to-End
summary: This research proposes learning latent reasoning traces for scalar reward models, aiming to improve alignment of large language models with human preferences, especially for complex or out-of-distribution tasks.

title: Detecting Experiential Intertextuality Across Migration Routes: Beyond Surface Similarity in French Narratives
summary: This study introduces and tackles the task of detecting experiential intertextuality in French narratives from migrants, aiming to identify parallel lived experiences across different migration routes beyond surface similarity.

title: Hy-MultiTurn: A Six-Dimensional Benchmark for Deep Multi-Turn Dialogue Understanding
summary: Hy-MultiTurn is introduced as a six-dimensional benchmark designed to evaluate deep multi-turn dialogue understanding, addressing challenges like remembering details, tracking revisions, and identifying referents in long interactions.

title: Knowing When to Quit: Diagnosing and Training LLMs to Abort Futile Reasoning
summary: This research diagnoses and explores methods to train large language models (LLMs) to abort "futile reasoning" on tasks beyond their capabilities, aiming to prevent the generation of plausible but incorrect derivations.

title: Small Is Enough: Per-User Style Rewriting of AI-Edited Text via LoRA Adapters
summary: InMyStyle is a privacy-first system that uses LoRA adapters to adapt small language models for per-user style rewriting of AI-edited text, generating training examples with local helper LLMs without explicit instruction prompts.

title: Data Turnstile: A Scalable Open Framework for Function-Calling Data Generation
summary: Data Turnstile is a scalable open framework designed for generating function-calling data, particularly to address the scarcity and noise of training data for small language models (SLMs) in tool-use tasks.

title: CalibratedRubric: Task-Adaptive Rubric Banks for Open-Ended LLM Evaluation
summary: CalibratedRubric proposes a method using task-adaptive rubric banks for more reliable evaluation of open-ended large language model (LLM) outputs, addressing the challenges of costly expert curation and limitations of existing automated pipelines.

title: Translation with Thought: Difficulty-Adaptive Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Domain Machine Translation
summary: Translation with Thought (TwT) is a resource-rational framework using reinforcement learning for multi-domain machine translation (MDMT), which learns to adapt reasoning effort based on linguistic complexity.

title: Cross-Lingual Transfer for Machine Translation in Turkic Languages
summary: This study characterizes cross-lingual transfer in machine translation among five closely related Turkic languages (Turkish, Azerbaijani, Uzbek, Kazakh, and Kyrgyz), which is central to low-resource machine translation.

title: Zero-Mem: Zero-Token Memory Operations for LLM Agents
summary: Zero-Mem introduces a method for zero-token memory operations for large language model (LLM) agents, aiming to reduce token and time costs associated with managing and retrieving information from memory.

title: PTP: Previous-Token Prediction based LLM Inversion for Near-Exact Prompt Reconstruction
summary: PTP introduces a Previous-Token Prediction-based method for LLM inversion to achieve near-exact prompt reconstruction, addressing the challenge of inferring prompts from observed model outputs.

title: Studying quantization trade-offs for efficient inference deployment in machine translation
summary: This study examines the trade-offs of quantization for efficient inference deployment of large language models in machine translation, evaluating its impact on latency and throughput while maintaining quality.

title: Know It, Act on It: Investigating Memory Utilization in LLM Personalization
summary: This research investigates memory utilization in large language model (LLM) personalization, exploring why agents may fail to act on relevant user preferences even when the information is present in their context.

title: Evidence-Type Competition: When Can Interventional Data Teach Language Models Causal Direction?
summary: This study investigates when interventional data can teach language models causal direction, examining the competition between observational correlation and causal effect in a controlled synthetic environment.

title: ARB: A Matched Authorship-Rewriting Benchmark Dataset for AI-Text Detector Evaluation
summary: ARB is a new matched authorship-rewriting benchmark dataset developed for evaluating AI-text detectors, focusing on performance when AI-generated text has been rewritten or paraphrased.

title: Sycophancy Undermines Epistemic Vigilance in Cooperative Vision-Language Tasks
summary: This study investigates how sycophancy in AI models undermines epistemic vigilance in cooperative vision-language tasks, preventing iterative belief updates and conflict repair similar to human conversation.

title: ResKV: Reconstructing Omitted Attention Contributions for Fixed-Budget KV Cache Compression
summary: ResKV introduces a method for reconstructing omitted attention contributions during fixed-budget KV cache compression, improving efficient long-context inference by preserving more information than existing eviction methods.

title: FriendBench: Benchmarking Dyadic Familiarity Inference in Humans and Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: Introduces FriendBench, a new benchmark for evaluating the ability of humans and multimodal large language models to infer dyadic familiarity from short video clips of conversations.

title: Evolving language compositionality in a frequency-structured meaning space
summary: This research investigates language evolution using an iterated learning model, showing how language compositionality can emerge through repeated transmission in a frequency-structured meaning space.

title: TokTier: Exact Stateful Tokenization for Agentic LLM Serving
summary: Introduces TokTier, a method for exact stateful tokenization designed for agentic LLM serving systems to improve efficiency by avoiding re-tokenization of full request text.

title: To Facilitate or not to Facilitate: Human and LLM Facilitator Tendencies in Online Discussions
summary: This study examines the tendencies of human and LLM facilitators in online discussions, addressing the question of when to automate facilitation in such platforms.

title: Measuring Cognitive Engagement in Collaborative Discourse with an Extended ICAP Framework: Comparing Human Annotation, In-Context Learning, and Reflective LLM Agents
summary: This study applies an extended ICAP framework to measure cognitive engagement in collaborative discourse, comparing human annotation, in-context learning, and reflective LLM agents.

title: ReLoop-UME: Recurrent Depth with Learnable Retrieval Registers for Universal Multimodal Embedding
summary: Introduces ReLoop-UME, a new model that uses recurrent depth and learnable retrieval registers to create universal multimodal embeddings, mapping heterogeneous inputs into a shared embedding space.

title: SCMA: Structure-Conditioned and Metal-Aware Flow Matching for CT Metal Artifact Reduction
summary: Presents SCMA, a new method utilizing structure-conditioned and metal-aware flow matching to reduce artifacts caused by metallic objects in X-ray CT images, improving diagnostic quality.

title: WaiT for the Signal: Simple Frequency-Aware Flow-Matching
summary: Introduces WaiT, a simple frequency-aware flow-matching method designed to improve the global coherence, local detail, and texture fidelity of high-resolution image generation models.

title: Do Medical Foundation Models Generalize on the African Brain?
summary: This research investigates whether medical foundation models for brain MRI analysis generalize effectively to African cohorts, evaluating their performance compared to non-African data.

title: Can Synthetic Data Overcome the Generalization Limits of AI-Based Flower and Pod Detection Across Cowpea Breeding Genotypes and Environments?
summary: This study explores whether synthetic data can improve the generalization of AI-based computer vision models for flower and pod detection in cowpea breeding across diverse genotypes and environments.

title: A Unified Benchmark of Deep Learning Models for Multi-task 3D Brain Tumor Segmentation from Magnetic Resonance Imaging
summary: Proposes a unified benchmark for objectively comparing deep learning models used in multi-task 3D brain tumor segmentation from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

title: Physics-Aligned Self-Supervised Learning for Scientific Imaging
summary: This research proposes physics-aligned self-supervised learning for scientific imaging, which adapts data augmentations to reflect the physical measurement processes and acquisition constraints of scientific modalities.

title: DiffAttack: Evasion Attacks Against Face Recognition via Latent Diffusion Models
summary: Introduces DiffAttack, a method that uses latent diffusion models to create evasion attacks against face recognition systems, exploiting vulnerabilities in their decision boundaries.

title: Automated classification method of COVID-19 cases from chest CT volumes using 2D and 3D hybrid CNN for anisotropic volumes
summary: Proposes an automated classification method for COVID-19 cases from chest CT volumes, utilizing a hybrid 2D and 3D Convolutional Neural Network designed for anisotropic volumes.

title: Retrieval-Driven Training-Free AI-Generated Video Attribution
summary: Introduces a retrieval-driven, training-free method for attributing AI-generated videos to their specific generative sources, addressing threats from realistic synthetic media.

title: Visual Distribution Anchoring for Efficient Prompt Tuning
summary: Proposes Visual Distribution Anchoring, a method for efficient prompt tuning that adapts vision-language models more effectively by mitigating overfitting and computational costs.

title: SafeNexus: Discovering and Steering Modality-Universal Safety Neurons in MLLMs
summary: Introduces SafeNexus, a method for discovering and steering modality-universal safety neurons within Multimodal Large Language Models to improve their safety performance and defenses.

title: RAID: Towards Robust AI-Generated Image Detection with Bit-Reversed Images
summary: Presents RAID, a new method utilizing bit-reversed images for robust detection of AI-generated images, aiming to mitigate potential risks associated with the misuse of fake images.

title: Classification of COVID-19 cases from chest CT volumes using hybrid model of 3D CNN and 3D MLP-Mixer
summary: This paper proposes an automated classification method for COVID-19 cases from chest CT volumes using an improved hybrid model combining 3D CNN and 3D MLP-Mixer.

title: Adjudicated Captioning: Multi-Agent Alignment Scoring and Consensus-Distilled Beam Arbitration for Strict Zero-Shot Image Captioning
summary: This research introduces a multi-agent alignment scoring and consensus-distilled beam arbitration method for strict zero-shot image captioning, which generates image descriptions without paired image-caption supervision. It relies on text-only corpora and frozen pretrained image-text scorers.

title: CAER: Conflict-Aware Evidence Routing with Dual Prefix Experts for Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: This paper proposes CAER, a method with dual prefix experts for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to improve multimodal understanding and generation by addressing hallucinations and inconsistencies when textual inputs conflict with visual evidence.

title: SULAND v2: A Refined RGB Dataset and Deep Learning Object Detection Benchmark for UAV/UGV-Based SUrface LANDmine Detection Under Domain Shift
summary: This introduces SULAND v2, a refined RGB dataset and deep learning object detection benchmark designed for UAV/UGV-based surface landmine detection, focusing on challenges posed by domain shift and limited cross-architecture benchmarking.

title: Evaluation-Verification Reward for Consistent Multi-Reference Image Editing
summary: This paper proposes an Evaluation-Verification Reward mechanism to enhance consistency in multi-reference image editing models, aiming to improve visual harmony and maintain consistency across references through reinforcement learning.

title: SAM+D: Parameter-Efficient Dimensional Lifting of SAM-Family Models via Depth-Routed LoRA and Depth Shifting
summary: This research introduces SAM+D, a parameter-efficient framework that adapts 2D SAM-family foundation models to 3D volumes using Depth-Routed LoRA and Depth Shifting, addressing challenges of processing inter-slice context.

title: ReMoE: Report-Guided Mixture-of-Experts for Multimodal OCT/OCTA Anomaly Detection
summary: This paper presents ReMoE, a Report-Guided Mixture-of-Experts framework for multimodal anomaly detection in retinal Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) and OCT Angiography (OCTA), aiming to identify deviations from normal patterns in healthcare.

title: Rethinking Detection Calibration: A Coordinate and Direction Perspective
summary: This research rethinks detection calibration, proposing a coordinate and direction perspective to improve the trustworthiness of deep learning object detectors by aligning confidence scores with accuracy and mitigating overconfident predictions.

title: Adaptive Emotional Video Captioning via Affective Heterogeneous Graph Reasoning and Multi-task Joint Learning
summary: This paper introduces an adaptive emotional video captioning method using affective heterogeneous graph reasoning and multi-task joint learning to generate descriptions with both factual correctness and affective expressiveness.

title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Spiking Point Cloud Models
summary: This research investigates parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods for Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) in point cloud analysis, aiming to provide energy-efficient solutions for resource-constrained devices and facilitate downstream task adaptation.

title: A Frozen Pixel-Space Diffusion Model Can Guide Itself with Its Own Samples
summary: This paper explores how a frozen pixel-space diffusion model can guide itself using its own samples to improve the generation of both global structure and local texture in high-dimensional image spaces.

title: SciFigPlag-Bench: A Benchmark for Provenance-Aware Scientific Figure Plagiarism Detection
summary: This introduces SciFigPlag-Bench, a benchmark for provenance-aware reasoning to detect plagiarism in scientific figures within scholarly documents, addressing an underexplored multimodal evaluation problem.

title: First Investigation of Deep Learning for Intraoperative Gauze Segmentation in Minimally Invasive Abdominal Surgery
summary: This paper presents the first investigation into using deep learning for intraoperative gauze segmentation in minimally invasive abdominal surgery, aiming to prevent complications from retained surgical gauze.

title: On the Efficacy of Self-Supervised Point Cloud Encoders for Efficient 3D Large Language Models
summary: This research examines the efficacy of self-supervised point cloud encoders in developing efficient 3D Large Language Models (3D-LLMs) for 3D understanding, aiming to lower the computational barriers for training such models.

title: Have I Seen You? Embedding Behavior Signals Synthetic Face Dataset Membership
summary: This research investigates whether synthetic face datasets generated by AI models embed behavioral signals that could reveal membership to their real source datasets, raising questions about privacy exposure in biometric recognition.

title: Progressive Decision-Making for Localizing Open-Ended AI-Generated Image Forgeries
summary: This paper proposes a progressive decision-making approach for localizing open-ended AI-generated image forgeries, addressing the challenge of detecting evolving manipulation patterns from generative models.

title: MoRAE: Flow-Friendly Self-Supervised Latents for Text-to-Motion Generation
summary: This paper introduces MoRAE, a method that uses flow-friendly self-supervised latents for text-to-motion generation, aiming to produce semantically correct, temporally coherent, and physically plausible motions.

title: Locally Consistent Transductive Information Maximization for Few-Shot Remote Sensing Scene Classification
summary: This research proposes Locally Consistent Transductive Information Maximization for few-shot remote sensing scene classification, which utilizes foundation models pre-trained on Earth-observation data and exploits collective statistical structure from unlabeled query sets.

title: UltraSAM3: A Concept-Driven Foundation Model for Universal Ultrasound Image Segmentation
summary: This paper introduces UltraSAM3, a concept-driven foundation model designed for universal ultrasound image segmentation, addressing the unique challenges of ultrasound images compared to other medical imaging modalities.

title: Domain-Division based Progressive Learning for Source-Free Domain Adaptation
summary: This research proposes a Domain-Division based Progressive Learning method for source-free domain adaptation, enabling effective adaptation to target data using only a source pre-trained model and an unlabeled target domain, addressing privacy and portability concerns.

title: Multi-Modal Object Re-Identification with Dual Semantic Guidance and Global-Local Mutual Modulation
summary: This paper introduces a Multi-Modal Object Re-Identification (ReID) method utilizing dual semantic guidance and global-local mutual modulation to leverage complementary information across modalities and improve performance.

title: Is It Time for the Renaissance of Salient Object Detection in the Era of MLLMs?
summary: This research investigates how multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can enhance salient object detection (SOD) through zero-shot capabilities, proposing a method to evaluate and refine SOD beyond conventional mask-based approaches.

title: CorrelationFlow: A Training-Free Geometric Approach for LiDAR Scene Flow Estimation
summary: This paper introduces CorrelationFlow, a novel training-free geometric method for LiDAR scene flow estimation, addressing limitations of existing feed-forward approaches in handling sparse and distant data.

title: When Model Priors Conflict with Visual Evidence: Mitigating Commonsense-Driven Hallucinations by Selective Prior Calibration
summary: This research explores and aims to mitigate commonsense-driven hallucinations in vision-language models, where a model's prior knowledge overrides visual evidence, suggesting selective prior calibration to address these errors.

title: TAVI-TEC: An AI-Based Tool for Procedural Planning of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation
summary: This item introduces TAVI-TEC, an AI-based tool designed to standardize and improve the efficiency of preprocedural planning for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation using computed tomography angiography data.

title: OsteoCAD: A Human-in-the-Loop Cloud-Edge Framework for Bone Tumor Segmentation
summary: This paper presents OsteoCAD, a human-in-the-loop cloud-edge framework for bone tumor segmentation, addressing challenges in deploying AI for medical image analysis due to limited computational resources and specialized expertise in healthcare.

title: Training-Free Entity-Level Few-Shot Segmentation of Remote Sensing Images with Advection Refinement
summary: This research proposes a training-free, entity-level few-shot segmentation method with advection refinement for remote sensing images, aiming to reduce training costs and improve prediction quality compared to existing cross-domain approaches.

title: FillGS: Filling Observation Gaps in 4D Gaussian Splatting via Viewpoint-Time Selection and Generative Refinement
summary: FillGS is introduced as a method to improve 4D Gaussian Splatting by filling observation gaps in dynamic scenes via viewpoint-time selection and generative refinement, addressing artifacts caused by limited viewpoint coverage.

title: CALM-AH: An ABAW11-Calibrated Multimodal Ensemble with Reliability-Gated Multi-Expert Consensus for Video-Level Ambivalence and Hesitancy Recognition
summary: CALM-AH is presented as an ABAW11-calibrated multimodal ensemble that uses reliability-gated multi-expert consensus to recognize video-level ambivalence and hesitancy based on language, voice, and facial cues.

title: DualDiT: A Conditional Dual-Output Diffusion Transformer for Joint OCT Image and Segmentation Mask Generation
summary: DualDiT is a new Conditional Dual-Output Diffusion Transformer developed for jointly generating realistic OCT medical images and their corresponding segmentation masks, helping to address the shortage of annotated data in medical imaging.

title: SatEdit: Mask-Conditioned Image Editing via VLM-Guided Segment Annotation
summary: SatEdit is introduced as a mask-conditioned satellite image editing framework that utilizes Vision-Language Model (VLM)-guided segment annotation to enable precise, object-level control in overhead imagery without costly supervised datasets.

title: VFAD: Variational Semantic Prompting Meets Frequency-Adaptive Representation Learning for Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection
summary: This research introduces VFAD, a novel approach that combines variational semantic prompting with frequency-adaptive representation learning for zero-shot anomaly detection, aiming to enhance the generalization capabilities of CLIP-based methods.

title: Dense Temporal Contrast Synthesis via Conditioned Latent Transport
summary: This paper describes a method for Dense Temporal Contrast Synthesis using Conditioned Latent Transport, aiming to reduce the reliance on gadolinium-based contrast agents in Dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI for breast cancer management.

title: OSEF: One-Step Evidence Fusion for Cross-Video Scene Procedure Planning
summary: OSEF is presented as a One-Step Evidence Fusion method for Cross-Video Scene Procedure Planning (CVSPP), enabling AI planners to effectively retrieve and use evidence from multiple candidate videos to solve start-goal queries.

title: Role-Break in Attention Heads: Understanding and Detecting Hallucinations in VLMs
summary: This research investigates the phenomenon of hallucinations in Vision-Language Models (VLMs), focusing on understanding and detecting these inconsistencies by analyzing 'role-break' in attention heads.

title: QR-Structured Thermal Triggers for Targeted Semantic Attacks on Infrared Vision-Language Models
summary: This paper investigates the robustness of Infrared Vision-Language Models (IR-VLMs) against QR-structured thermal triggers, exploring targeted semantic attacks and the stability of cross-modal alignment under perturbations.

title: Weight-Space Mixture-of-Experts for Implicit Neural Representation Classification
summary: This paper proposes a Weight-Space Mixture-of-Experts approach for Implicit Neural Representation (INR) Classification, addressing the challenge of classifying signals encoded in the high-dimensional weight space of INRs.

title: Lightweight Neural Networks for Affordance Segmentation: Enhancement of the Decoder Module
summary: This research focuses on enhancing the decoder module of lightweight neural networks for visual affordance segmentation, optimizing them for deployment on wearable robots despite the conflicting requirements of high abstraction and small model size.

title: Leveraging Transfer Learning with Class-Specific Decoders for Laparoscopic Segmentation
summary: This paper explores leveraging transfer learning with class-specific decoders for laparoscopic multi-organ segmentation, addressing the challenge of class imbalance and intricate anatomical feature learning in surgical data.

title: Advances, challenges, and opportunities for legged robots
summary: This article provides an assessment of the current capabilities, challenges, and future opportunities for legged robots, including humanoids and quadrupeds, covering their hardware, locomotion, and societal impact.

title: ST-WAM: Semantic-Temporal World Action Model for Robust Manipulation under Visual Distribution Shifts
summary: ST-WAM (Semantic-Temporal World Action Model) is introduced to enhance robust robot manipulation by better modeling robot actions and visual dynamics, addressing limitations of existing World Action Models under visual distribution shifts.

title: Receding-Horizon Next-Best-View Planner for Autonomous Leaf Surface Reconstruction
summary: This paper proposes a receding-horizon next-best-view planner for autonomous robotic reconstruction of plant leaf surfaces, optimizing view points under budget and computational constraints. This method aids in plant growth monitoring and yield estimation.

title: D-VLC: Decentralized Vision-Language Collaboration for Heterogeneous Embodied Multi-Robot Systems in Unknown Environments
summary: This research introduces a decentralized vision-language collaboration framework (D-VLC) for heterogeneous embodied multi-robot systems to improve efficiency in complex tasks in unknown environments. It moves beyond conventional rule-based methods for task execution.

title: Auto-JEPA: A Latent World Model of Continuous Intent for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: This paper introduces Auto-JEPA, a latent world model for end-to-end autonomous driving that focuses on predicting scene features relevant to future ego actions, rather than reconstructing the complete future world. This approach aims to improve planning for self-driving vehicles.

title: Outcome-Guided Distillation: A Teacher-Student Framework to Advance VLM Reasoning in Autonomous Driving
summary: This research proposes an outcome-guided distillation framework to enhance Vision-Language Model (VLM) reasoning in end-to-end autonomous driving, addressing the black-box nature and limitations in complex scenarios. It helps provide explicit reasoning for control actions in autonomous vehicles.

title: ActFovea: Runtime Safeguarding for VLA Policies via Spatiotemporal Visual-Action Consistency
summary: ActFovea is a plug-and-play safeguarding framework designed to ensure runtime robustness for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies in robotic manipulation by maintaining spatiotemporal visual-action consistency. It protects against disturbances that disrupt temporal alignment.

title: CLIFT: Turning Gemini Robotics On-Device into Humanoid Specialists via Non-Invasive Closed-Loop Iterative Fine-Tuning
summary: CLIFT presents a non-invasive closed-loop iterative fine-tuning method to adapt robot foundation models, specifically Gemini Robotics On-Device, into humanoid specialists. This approach aims to overcome limitations of proprietary models and allow adaptation to new tasks and embodiments.

title: Event-Based Upper-Body Humanoid Teleoperation Under Challenging Illumination
summary: This paper presents a real-time framework for upper-body human-to-humanoid motion imitation using neuromorphic event-based vision, addressing perceptual challenges of conventional sensors in high dynamic range scenes. This technology improves teleoperation capabilities under difficult lighting.

title: FBFM: A Training-Free Asynchronous Feedback Mechanism for Flow-Matching in World-Action Models Execution
summary: FBFM introduces a training-free asynchronous feedback mechanism for flow-matching in world-action model (WAM) execution to enhance long-horizon robot control reliability. This method improves real-time re-grounding by refreshing history with ground-truth data instead of recursive rollout.

title: BWM: A Low-Cost High-Fidelity World Simulator for Robot Learning
summary: BWM is a low-cost, high-fidelity world simulator developed to facilitate reliable robot learning by predicting action consequences on physical hardware, including risky outcomes. It aims to address the sim-to-real gap more effectively than existing physics simulators.

title: SAGP: Semantic Affordance-Guided Grasp Planning via Coarse-Zone VLM Reasoning
summary: SAGP proposes a semantic affordance-guided grasp planning method that uses coarse-zone VLM reasoning to generate functionally appropriate robot grasps. This approach overcomes limitations of geometry-based planners by considering semantic context for robotic manipulation.

title: AquaJEPA: Action-Conditioned Multimodal Predictive Representations for Underwater Robot Dynamics
summary: AquaJEPA is an action-conditioned joint-embedding predictive model that fuses multimodal sensor data for underwater robot dynamics. It enhances reliability by integrating an RGB camera, forward-looking sonar, and proprioception, adapting to varying water visibility and vehicle motion.

title: Automated Straight-line Sewing of Stretchable Fabrics with Different Lengths
summary: This research addresses the challenge of automating straight-line sewing of stretchable fabrics with different lengths by stretching the shorter fabric to match the longer one. The aim is to develop an automated sewing process that meets various precision requirements.

title: Temporal Policy: History-Initialized Action Generation for Robotic Learning from Demonstration
summary: This paper introduces Temporal Policy, a method for history-initialized action generation in robotic Learning from Demonstration, leveraging generative models to capture multimodal behaviors. It aims to improve robotic action learning by better utilizing historical data.

title: Homotopy-Aware Corridor Generation without Predefined Reference Paths
summary: This work proposes a reference-path-free framework for homotopy-aware corridor generation, essential for collision-free robotic motion planning. Unlike existing methods, it avoids predefined reference paths, allowing for exploration of a wider range of homotopy classes.

title: STAGE: STyle-controllable Action GEneration for personalized autonomous driving
summary: STAGE introduces a style-controllable action generation system for personalized autonomous driving, allowing autonomous systems to adapt to individual driver preferences and aggression levels. This aims to meet human expectations for customized driving styles.

title: TransGraspNet: Physically and Geometrically Consistent Manipulation of Transparent Labware
summary: TransGraspNet focuses on achieving physically and geometrically consistent manipulation of transparent laboratory glassware containing liquid, a safety-critical task. It optimizes robotic grasping by improving transparent object perception to prevent unstable grasps and spillage.

title: Safe Vision Language Action Models via Barrier Enhanced Flow Matching
summary: This article presents a modular inference framework that integrates Flow Matching generative models with formal Control Barrier Function (CBF) safety guarantees for Vision Language Action models. This approach modifies the denoising process to ensure safety, likely for robotic applications.

title: FibVLA: An Efficient Temporal Vision-Language-Action Model with Fibonacci Sampling
summary: FibVLA introduces an efficient temporal Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model that uses Fibonacci Sampling to enhance multimodal information cognition for embodied AI applications. This model aims to improve VLA's ability to infer physical-world actions by considering temporal dynamics.

title: HAM-VLN: Harnessing Hierarchical Agentic Memory for Zero-Shot Vision-and-Language Navigation
summary: HAM-VLN proposes using hierarchical agentic memory to improve zero-shot vision-and-language navigation for robots, allowing them to follow instructions in unseen environments. This training-free paradigm enables robots to query multimodal LLMs for observation understanding and action planning.

title: WCM: A World Critic Model for Vision-Language-Action Reinforcement Learning
summary: WCM introduces a World Critic Model designed to enhance Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models in reinforcement learning for robotic manipulation. This critic-based approach improves value estimation by operating on single-frame observations or VLM backbone latents.

title: RayViT: Ray-Conditioned Visual Representations for Viewpoint-Robust Imitation Learning
summary: This paper proposes RayViT, a Ray-conditioned Vision Transformer Encoder model, designed to achieve viewpoint-robust visual imitation learning for robots.

title: Balancing of Humanoid with Object Mass: Trade-off Analyses and Lifting Control
summary: This study analyzes and develops control approaches for humanoid robots to maintain balance while performing loco-manipulation tasks with an object.

title: Bootstrapping Self-Supervised Learning of Binary Classification Using Error Bounds: A Case Study on a Robotic Insertion Task
summary: This research applies bootstrapping self-supervised learning with error bounds to a robotic insertion task, aiming for rapid and reliable deployment in manufacturing.

title: GPA-RAM: Grasp-Pretraining Augmented Robotic Attention Mamba for Spatial Task Learning
summary: This paper introduces Grasp-Pretraining Augmentation (GPA), which incorporates grasp priors into imitation policies to improve fine-grained robotic manipulation for spatial tasks.

title: ASVSim (AirSim for Surface Vehicles): A High-Fidelity Simulation Framework for Autonomous Surface Vehicle Research
summary: ASVSim is introduced as a high-fidelity simulation framework for research and development of autonomous surface vehicles (USVs) in the transport industry.

title: Towards bridging the gap: Systematic sim-to-real transfer for diverse legged robots
summary: This work presents a systematic approach for sim-to-real transfer of controllers for diverse legged robots, aiming for robust locomotion and energy efficiency in real-world environments.

title: Vision-based Goal-Reaching Control for Mobile Robots Using a Hierarchical Learning Framework
summary: This paper proposes a novel hierarchical learning framework for vision-based goal-reaching control in mobile robots, integrating stereo visual pose estimation and constrained reinforcement learning.

title: Choose What to Manipulate: Revealing Data Scaling Laws in Bounding-Box Guided Policies for Semantic Manipulation
summary: This research explores bounding-box guided policies for semantic manipulation to improve robot performance in cluttered scenes, addressing limitations of diffusion-based policies.

title: Physics-Embedded Neural ODEs for Learning Antagonistic Pneumatic Artificial Muscle Dynamics
summary: This study focuses on using physics-embedded neural ODEs to model and control the complex, nonlinear dynamics of antagonistic pneumatic artificial muscles for soft robots.

title: DuetHOI: Language-Guided Bimanual Hand--Object Motion Generation with Articulation Planning and Contact Refinement
summary: DuetHOI is a model presented for language-guided bimanual hand-object motion generation, incorporating articulation planning and contact refinement.

title: Kinodynamic Motion Retargeting for Humanoid Locomotion via Multi-Contact Whole-Body Trajectory Optimization
summary: This paper introduces the KinoDynamic Motion Retargeting (KDMR) framework, a multi-contact whole-body trajectory optimization approach for humanoid locomotion.

title: The Open Motion Planning Library 2.0
summary: The Open Motion Planning Library (OMPL) 2.0 is released, continuing to provide a wide range of state-of-the-art sampling-based algorithms for motion planning in robotics.

title: Vehicle Prediction Model for Enhanced MPC Path Tracking in Formula Student Driverless
summary: This paper presents a vehicle prediction model designed to enhance Model Predictive Control (MPC) for path tracking in autonomous race cars, specifically in Formula Student Driverless.

title: Pushing the Performance Limits in Autonomous Racing: Continuous Stability-Aware Adaptive Velocity Planning in Formula Student Driverless
summary: This research focuses on continuous stability-aware adaptive velocity planning to improve performance and stability for autonomous race cars in competitive events like Formula Student Driverless.

title: RynnBrain 1.1: Towards More Capable and Generalizable Embodied Foundation Model
summary: RynnBrain 1.1 is introduced as a family of embodied foundation models, supporting embodied perception, spatial reasoning, localization, and planning at various scales.

title: Combining Large Language Models and Symbolic Reasoning for Multi-Robot Temporal Planning through Explainable Knowledge Bases
summary: PLANTOR is presented as a framework combining large language models and symbolic reasoning for multi-robot temporal planning through explainable knowledge bases derived from natural language.

title: Fast Feature Field ($\text{F}^3$): A Predictive Representation of Events
summary: This paper develops the Fast Feature Field (F3), a mathematical framework and algorithms for building predictive representations of data from event-based cameras.

title: AREA3D: Active Reconstruction Agent with Unified Feed-Forward 3D Perception and Vision-Language Guidance
summary: Describes an active 3D reconstruction agent that autonomously selects viewpoints using unified feed-forward 3D perception and vision-language guidance.

title: RAPiD: Reward-Guided Consistency Distillation of Diffusion Planners for Real-Time Autonomous Driving
summary: Introduces RAPiD, a reward-guided consistency distillation framework to improve diffusion-based trajectory planners for real-time autonomous driving by addressing latency bottlenecks.

title: Leveraging Image Generators to Address Data Scarcity: The Gen4Regen Dataset for Forest Regeneration Mapping
summary: Describes how image generators are used to create the Gen4Regen dataset to address data scarcity for forest regeneration mapping in sustainable forest management.
