summary: This study explores knowledge transfer between different sizes of Transformer models, specifically converting a 1.4B Pythia model to a 410M sibling. It characterizes how representations align strongly across sizes while parameters align weakly.

title: NOMADD: Numerical Optimization of Models Adapting to Data Drift
summary: This paper introduces NOMADD (Numerical Optimization of Models Adapting to Data Drift), a method designed to mitigate performance degradation in tabular models due to data drift and concept drift. It addresses changes in feature distributions or relationships over time.

title: Contrast-invariant deep ptychography neural networks
summary: This research addresses scaling inconsistencies in ptychography neural networks when generalizing out of distribution by introducing a factorization strategy. This method decouples learned object texture from measurement scaling, improving real-world viability.

title: Maglev: Sliding Recurrent Memory
summary: This paper introduces Maglev, a recurrent Transformer architecture featuring fixed-size memory that generalizes sliding-window attention. The architecture is designed to remain parallelizable during training.

title: GoT-CD: Graph-of-Thoughts Causal Discovery and the Fragility of Post-hoc Path-Specific Fairness Audits
summary: This research introduces GoT-CD (Graph-of-Thoughts Causal Discovery), a method for recovering directed structure from observational data. It explores its use in clinical settings for mechanism reasoning and discusses the fragility of post-hoc path-specific fairness audits.

title: Robust Counterfactual Policy Optimisation via Nondeterministic Causal Models
summary: This paper proposes a method for robust counterfactual policy optimization that utilizes nondeterministic causal models, addressing the limitations of traditional deterministic assumptions in sequential decision-making. It formalizes counterfactual policy optimization under these conditions.

title: AnchorKV: Anchor-Residual KV Cache Compression
summary: This paper introduces AnchorKV, a method for compressing the key-value (KV) cache, which is a primary memory bottleneck in long-context LLM inference. It aims to improve efficiency by addressing the limitations of existing eviction and quantization methods.

title: Bayesian Data Reweighting Improves Multimodal Retrieval for Knowledge-Based Visual Question Answering
summary: This research proposes using Bayesian data reweighting to improve multimodal retrieval systems for knowledge-based visual question answering. It aims to enhance the retrieval of external evidence for image-question pairs by addressing how unmatched query-document pairs are treated.

title: Federated generative event models for tokenized electronic health records
summary: This research evaluates federated training of tokenized generative event models (GEMs) across electronic health records from multiple institutions. It addresses limitations of siloed data and performance degradation in cross-site transfer for healthcare foundation models.

title: Sedentary Behavior Classification for Wearable Sensors with a CNN-BiLSTM Model
summary: This study uses a CNN-BiLSTM model to classify sedentary behavior from wearable sensor data, focusing on improving posture-based classification. It investigates the transferability of models trained on hip-worn data to wrist-worn accelerometers.

title: ATFlash: Per-RoPE-Wavelength Attention Windows for Compute/Memory-Efficient LLM Inference
summary: This paper introduces ATFlash, a method for compute/memory-efficient LLM inference using per-RoPE-wavelength attention windows. It optimizes attention scores by pruning query-key pairs based on rotary position embedding wavelength to improve efficiency.

title: Rubrics as Privileged Information for Open-Ended Generation
summary: This research extends on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) by using rubrics as "privileged information" to improve open-ended generation models. It leverages structural constraints from ground-truth answers in verifiable domains like math.

title: Schedule-Informed Temporal Fusion Forecasting of Hourly Airport Security-Checkpoint Throughput
summary: This study develops a schedule-informed temporal fusion forecasting framework to predict hourly airport security-checkpoint throughput. It converts flight schedules into temporally aligned signals to more accurately forecast passenger arrival times for staffing needs.

title: SP3O: Reinforcement Learning from Segment Preferences without Reward Modeling
summary: This paper introduces SP3O, a new method for preference-based reinforcement learning (PbRL) in general stochastic Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) that operates without requiring a reward model. It addresses limitations of existing reward-model-free techniques.

title: Inverted Detection and Control in Steering Vectors
summary: This paper introduces a method for detecting and controlling concepts in large language model outputs using inverted steering vectors. It challenges the assumption of linear discriminability in steering vectors.

title: Scaling an Autoregressive Transformer for Single-Cell Generation
summary: This research studies the application of a scaled autoregressive transformer for generating single-cell gene expression vectors. The paper characterizes the biological fidelity and performance of the generated data.

title: Temporal Leakage in LLM Backtesting: Measurement, Validation, and Adjusted Scores
summary: This paper identifies flaws in standard checks for temporal leakage in LLM backtesting, showing that current methods are uninformative. It proposes methods for measurement, validation, and adjusted scores to address this issue.

title: AcceptMoE: Commitment-Weighted Self-Sizing Verifier Expert Sets for Efficient MoE Speculative Decoding
summary: This research proposes AcceptMoE, a method using commitment-weighted self-sizing verifier expert sets for efficient speculative decoding in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models. It aims to reduce unnecessary expert activations during parallel verification.

title: Joint Affine Spectral Shaping: Coupling Weight and Bias Updates Beyond Weight-Only Muon
summary: This paper introduces Joint Affine Spectral Shaping, an optimization method that couples weight and bias updates in neural networks. It formulates affine layers as a joint momentum matrix and applies spectral mapping.

title: A Graph Signal Processing Perspective on Numerical Sequence Representations in LLM In-Context Learning
summary: This research analyzes numerical sequence representations in LLM in-context learning through a graph signal processing perspective. It aims to better understand how LLMs perform numerical inference.

title: Paired Recipient-based Evaluation of Survival Prediction for Deceased Donor Kidney Transplants
summary: This research explores the use of machine learning for predicting kidney transplant outcomes and proposes a paired recipient-based evaluation method for these survival predictions. The goal is to improve donor-recipient matching.

title: PLAN: Parallel Liquid-Inspired Approximation Network for Efficient Representation Learning in Flexible Job Shop Scheduling
summary: This research introduces PLAN, a Parallel Liquid-Inspired Approximation Network, designed for efficient representation learning in flexible job shop scheduling using deep reinforcement learning. It aims to overcome limitations of attention-centric models.

title: SynEnergy: Anomaly Semantic-Guided Diffusion for Synthetic Energy Data Generation
summary: This research proposes SynEnergy, an anomaly semantic-guided diffusion model for generating synthetic fine-grained energy consumption data. The goal is to address privacy concerns and data-sharing constraints.

title: SMOPD: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning via Specialize-and-Merge Online Policy Distillation
summary: This research introduces SMOPD, a method for multi-reward reinforcement learning that uses specialize-and-merge online policy distillation. It aims to improve model performance by addressing issues with reward signal interaction.

title: Convex-Hull-Neighborhood Smooth Dual Generalization: Controlling Local Correction Propagation in Offline RL
summary: This research introduces a method called Convex-Hull-Neighborhood Smooth Dual Generalization to control local correction propagation in offline reinforcement learning. It aims to manage estimation errors from out-of-distribution actions.

title: Simulation-free and finite-time diffusion model
summary: This paper proposes a new framework for designing generative diffusion models that enables both simulation-free training and finite-time generation. This improves the efficiency of these models.

title: Trajectory-Guided Forget-Recover Network for Continual LLM Unlearning
summary: This research proposes a Trajectory-Guided Forget-Recover Network for continual unlearning in large language models. The method aims to effectively remove sensitive data while maintaining model performance.

title: Lightweight Chunk Selection for Mobile Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: This paper introduces a lightweight chunk selection method to optimize Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for mobile and edge devices. It aims to reduce computation and memory costs by retaining only one retrieved chunk.

title: On the Implicit Flatness Bias of Sharpness-Aware Minimization: A Linear Stability Analysis with Quantitative Hyperparameter Bounds
summary: This research provides a linear stability analysis of Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM), clarifying its implicit bias toward flat minima. It also offers quantitative hyperparameter bounds for the perturbation radius.

title: Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Self-Distilled Reward Shaping
summary: This paper proposes using self-distilled reward shaping to provide denser supervision in agentic reinforcement learning. This method aims to improve how LLM agents learn through interaction by identifying creditable intermediate decisions.

title: SAKI: Score-Aware Low-Rank Key Indexing for Long-Context KV Retrieval
summary: This research introduces SAKI, a Score-Aware Low-Rank Key Indexing method for long-context KV retrieval. It aims to optimize key compression by directly addressing expected attention score distortion.

title: FinVerse: Financial Time-Series Benchmark
summary: FinVerse is introduced as a new benchmark for evaluating the forecasting ability of time-series foundation models in finance. It provides standardized comparisons for heterogeneous financial series.

title: ED-DiT: Physics-Guided Diffusion Pretraining for Transferable Molecular Representations from Electron Density
summary: This research proposes ED-DiT, a physics-guided diffusion pretraining method for learning transferable molecular representations from electron density. It aims to capture molecular electronic structure for various downstream tasks.

title: TabletCraft: Bridging a 4,000-Year Cultural Gap with Bidirectional Akkadian NMT and Cuneiform Rendering
summary: This project introduces TabletCraft, a bidirectional neural machine translation (NMT) system for Akkadian and cuneiform rendering. It aims to bridge a 4,000-year cultural gap by enabling modern users to read and write in the ancient writing system.

title: BBOWP-Bench: Evaluating LLMs on Black-Box Optimization Word Problems
summary: Introduces BBOWP-Bench, a new benchmark for evaluating large language models (LLMs) on their ability to automatically derive optimization problems from natural-language descriptions.

title: MemArena: An Ego-Centric Benchmark for On-Device Agentic Personal Memory Assistants at Scale
summary: Introduces MemArena, an ego-centric benchmark designed to evaluate on-device agentic personal memory assistants, addressing limitations in existing memory benchmarks.

title: OncoTriad-QA: A Patient-Level Radiology-Pathology-Genomics Benchmark for Pan-Cancer Reasoning
summary: Presents OncoTriad-QA, a new patient-level benchmark for evaluating large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) on pan-cancer reasoning, integrating radiology, pathology, and genomics data.

title: Evaluating OpenAI's Privacy Filter: Cross-Lingual, Cross-Domain PII Detection Across 42 Benchmarks
summary: Presents an independent, systematic evaluation of OpenAI's Privacy Filter (OPF), a PII detector, across 42 synthetic benchmarks spanning 22 languages and 5 domains.

title: Preferred, Not Safer: Pairwise Preference Is a Poor Proxy for Clinical Safety
summary: Evaluates the reliability of clinician pairwise preferences as a proxy for clinical safety in large language model (LLM) evaluation, using expert feedback from the MOOVE platform.

title: JudgeArena: A Unified Framework for Reproducible LLM-Judge Evaluation
summary: Introduces JudgeArena, a unified framework for reproducible LLM-as-a-judge evaluation, aiming to address fragmentation in existing methods for ranking language models.

title: Knowing the Form, Not the Function: Automatically Auditing Answer--Authority Decoupling in Legal Benchmarks
summary: Audits legal benchmarks to assess the decoupling between answer correctness and authority grounding in large language models (LLMs), testing whether answer correctness can serve as a proxy for legal authority.

title: Speculative Correction: Draft-then-Refine Decoding for Diffusion Language Models
summary: Proposes Speculative Correction, a plug-and-play inference pattern for diffusion language models (DLMs) that generates a complete draft and then refines the response bidirectionally.

title: Stuck on "A": Diagnosing and Repairing Interface Injury in Attention-to-KDA Linearization of a 0.6B Language Model
summary: Investigates and diagnoses the "interface injury" incurred when converting full-attention layers of the Qwen3-0.6B-Base model to KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) linear-attention layers.

title: Crayotter: Learning Long-Horizon Video Editing Agents via Group-Relative Preference Backpropagation
summary: Introduces Crayotter, a system for learning long-horizon video editing agents by using group-relative preference backpropagation to handle subjective editing quality and heterogeneous requests.

title: ARCHead: Activation-Metric Residual Correction for Large Language Model Output Heads
summary: Proposes ARCHead (Activation-Metric Residual Correction) as a method to improve weight-only quantization for large language model (LLM) output heads, aiming to preserve the vocabulary-logit distribution.

title: Learning a Vector-Symbolic Model for Socio-Cultural Tasks
summary: Explores learning a vector-symbolic model to better represent the impact of socio-cultural structures on decision-making within computational cognitive models.

title: BODHI: Do LLMs Branch Out and Discover Heterogeneous Inferences?
summary: Presents BODHI, a study investigating whether reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) genuinely expands the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) or primarily improves sampling efficiency.

title: FLARE: Few-shot Learning-based Adaptive Reflective Engine
summary: Introduces FLARE, a few-shot learning-based adaptive reflective engine designed to optimize prompt quality in complex, compound AI systems through reflective instruction evolution.

title: Character Iconicity vs. Arbitrariness: An Arabic NLP Perspective
summary: Explores the functional necessity of visual distinctions in Arabic script through an Arabic NLP perspective, using dot removal experiments to analyze character iconicity versus arbitrariness.

title: Aligned in Form, Not in Meaning: The Comprehension - Containment Decoupling of LLM Safety in Low-Resource Bangla Derogatory Speech
summary: Audits five frontier large language models on native Bangla derogatory speech to investigate "Comprehension-Containment Decoupling," suggesting current safety alignment focuses on high-resource surface forms rather than harmful meaning.

title: OPTD: On-Policy Transition Distillation with Consistency-Guided Adaptive Compression for Few-Step Diffusion Language Models
summary: Introduces OPTD (On-Policy Transition Distillation), a method utilizing consistency-guided adaptive compression for few-step distillation to accelerate decoding in diffusion language models (dLLMs).

title: Every Wrong Answer Counts: Option-Level Psychometrics for LLM Multiple-Choice Benchmarks
summary: Proposes option-level psychometrics for large language model (LLM) multiple-choice benchmarks, arguing that analyzing preferences among incorrect options provides more systematic and useful information than binary scoring.

title: Mapping the City Through the Lens of Language Models
summary: Explores how language models interpret underspecified references to cities, measuring their inherent assumptions about urban size, form, infrastructure, environment, and function.

title: TQLite: Multi-LLM Jury Guided Distillation for Real-time MQM Translation Quality Evaluation
summary: Presents TQLite, a multi-LLM jury guided distillation method for real-time MQM (Multidimensional Quality Metrics) translation quality evaluation, addressing the computational expense of large models.

title: Language Models Encode the Contextual Truth of Propositions
summary: This research demonstrates that Large Language Models (LLMs) encode contextual truth by maintaining linear representations of propositions, even when truth is derived from in-context evidence rather than world knowledge.

title: Beyond Accuracy: A Multidimensional Evaluation of Statistical Reasoning in Large Language Models
summary: This study advocates for a multidimensional evaluation of statistical reasoning in Large Language Models (LLMs), moving beyond simple accuracy to assess how models construct and communicate statistical explanations.

title: Emulate or Estimate? The Divergent Strengths of Base and Post-Trained Language Models for Opinion Simulation
summary: This research explores the divergent strengths of base and post-trained Large Language Models (LLMs) in simulating human opinions, attributing conflicting prior results to the conflation of different model types.

title: PI-Mem: Pushing Long-Context Reasoning to 3.6M Tokens with Parallel-Iterative Memory
summary: PI-Mem is a new parallel-iterative memory approach designed to overcome long-context reasoning bottlenecks in Large Language Models (LLMs), pushing capabilities to 3.6 million tokens by addressing challenges in sequential updates and inter-chunk dependencies.

title: SeqLLM: Augmenting LLMs with Behavioral-Sequence Modeling for High-Stakes Decisions at WeChat Pay
summary: SeqLLM augments Large Language Models (LLMs) with behavioral-sequence modeling to enhance merchant risk control at WeChat Pay, enabling more accurate high-stakes decisions by jointly understanding textual profiles and behavioral sequences.

title: Activation-Guided Neuron Intervention to Induce Alzheimer's-Related Computational Language Phenotypes in a Large Language Model
summary: Researchers introduce an activation-guided neuron intervention method to induce Alzheimer's-related computational language phenotypes in a Large Language Model (LLM), helping to establish if model representations functionally contribute to disease-related speech changes.

title: CVPO: Enhancing LLM Reinforcement Learning Reasoning via Value-Variance Adaptation and Dynamic Curriculum Learning
summary: CVPO is a new method that enhances Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning capabilities through reinforcement learning, utilizing value-variance adaptation and dynamic curriculum learning to address feedback precision and problem difficulty drift.

title: PAMT: Process-Aligned Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Domain Machine Translation
summary: PAMT (Process-Aligned Reinforcement Learning) is introduced to improve multi-domain machine translation, enabling large reasoning models to make domain-sensitive decisions such as disambiguation and terminology control.

title: Scalable Frequency- and Length-Aware Subdocument Deduplication for Large Language Model Pretraining
summary: This paper presents a scalable method for frequency- and length-aware subdocument deduplication in large-scale pretraining corpora, aiming to remove redundancy beyond document-level deduplication for Large Language Model training.

title: VIVID: A Culturally Grounded Benchmark Exposing the Figurative Language Gap in Vietnamese NLP
summary: VIVID (Vietnamese Idioms for Validation and Interpretation Depth) is presented as the first systematic benchmark for evaluating culturally grounded figurative language understanding in Vietnamese Natural Language Processing (NLP), comprising 1,636 annotated idioms and proverbs.

title: What Language Does and What the Evidence Supports: A Functional Role Taxonomy and Evidence Audit of Language Grounding in Embodied Agents
summary: This survey provides a functional role taxonomy and evidence audit of language grounding in embodied agents, defining five non-exclusive roles for language to clarify its contribution and grounding within these systems.

title: HomoEnsNER: Does Language Alignment Outperform Architectural Complexity in Gujarati Named Entity Recognition?
summary: HomoEnsNER investigates whether language alignment or architectural complexity is more effective for Named Entity Recognition (NER) in Gujarati, a language challenged by specific linguistic characteristics.

title: From SQL Errors to Concept Gaps: An AI-Powered Knowledge Graph Analytics Platform for Personalized Feedback
summary: This paper describes an AI-powered knowledge graph analytics platform that provides personalized feedback to students learning SQL by connecting their errors to conceptual gaps in database systems courses.

title: Internalizing Academic Writing Workflows for Introduction Generation via Struct-Aware Policy Learning
summary: This research proposes internalizing academic writing workflows for introduction generation using Large Language Models (LLMs) via Struct-Aware Policy Learning, aiming to improve coordination of background, gap, method, and contribution in coherent narratives.

title: ANCHOR-RE: An Agentic Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Grounded Biomedical Relation Extraction
summary: ANCHOR-RE is an Agentic Neuro-Symbolic Framework developed for Grounded Biomedical Relation Extraction, combining the strengths of symbolic systems and Large Language Models (LLMs) to extract structured knowledge from literature.

title: Aligning Large Vision-Language Models at Test Time: A Trajectory-Guided Structured Sampling Approach
summary: This paper introduces a Trajectory-Guided Structured Sampling Approach for aligning Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) at test time, addressing resource-intensive training and mismatches found in existing RL-based alignment methods.

title: ICO: Enhancing Semantic-Shift Jailbreaks via Iterative Context Optimization
summary: ICO (Iterative Context Optimization) is presented as a method for enhancing semantic-shift jailbreaks, which are used to investigate vulnerabilities in foundation models by bypassing safety mechanisms through replacing harmful terms.

title: On the Diversity of Analogy Making in Large Language Models
summary: This research explores the diversity of analogy-making capabilities in Large Language Models (LLMs), investigating this core cognitive function that contributes to novelty and creativity.

title: Relational Priors as Convergence Pressure in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
summary: This study examines the effect of relational priors as convergence pressure in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems, analyzing how implicit social expectations from roles and protocols influence inter-agent behavior.

title: MoEGen: Mixture-of-Experts for Instance-Adaptive LoRA Generation
summary: Introduces MoEGen, a method for instance-adaptive LoRA generation that aims to improve parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) for large language models while addressing storage limitations of existing Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) based PEFT methods.

title: Benchmarking the Benchmarks: Testing the Predictive Validity of Commonsense Benchmarks
summary: A study evaluating the predictive validity of existing commonsense benchmarks for Large Language Models (LLMs), assessing how well they predict real-world task performance by testing 23 models from six families.

title: ArtECulture: Benchmarking Culture-Conditioned Visual Emotion Understanding in Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: Introduces ArtECulture, a new benchmark and task for evaluating multimodal large language models on culture-conditioned visual emotion understanding, which involves predicting and explaining culture-specific emotional perceptions of images.

title: FACTWASH: Catching AI Rewrites That Wash Hearsay into Fact
summary: Introduces "factwashing," a phenomenon where AI systems rewrite information, removing its verifiable source, and releases `factwash`, an open-source tool designed to detect such AI rewrites that turn hearsay into apparent fact.

title: Don't Let Me Ask for It: LLMs Show Deficiencies in Active Multi-Turn Information Acquisition for Abductive Inference
summary: A research paper investigating deficiencies in Large Language Models' (LLMs) active multi-turn information acquisition strategies when performing abductive inference, despite their ability to solve such reasoning tasks.

title: DUD: Decoupled Update Dynamics for Reliable Uncertainty Quantification in Large Language Models
summary: Introduces DUD (Decoupled Update Dynamics), a new mechanistic approach for reliable Uncertainty Quantification (UQ) in Large Language Models (LLMs) to better capture their epistemic state, moving beyond traditional probability-based metrics.

title: Dynamically Allocating Evaluation Effort for Model Ranking
summary: Proposes a method for dynamically allocating evaluation effort in NLP tasks to efficiently rank models, addressing the high costs and poor scalability of exhaustive human evaluation protocols.

title: Predicting Multilingual Classification and Translation Performance of LLMs with Cross-Lingual Alignment $\unicode{x2013}$ Is English Enough?
summary: A study investigating whether English-aligned cross-lingual alignment (CLA) scores can predict the multilingual classification and translation performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) in non-English tasks.

title: Probing Character-level Transformers for the Spanish L-shaped Morphome
summary: Research probing character-level transformers to understand how they learn complex irregular morphological patterns, using the Spanish L-shaped morphome as a test case.

title: Efficient Multilingual Neural Machine Translation via Corpus-Driven Vocabulary Pruning: An English-Arabic Case Study
summary: Proposes a method of corpus-driven vocabulary pruning to enhance the efficiency of multilingual neural machine translation (MNMT) models by reducing excessive memory and computational consumption from large vocabularies and embedding layers.

title: Beyond Initialization Loss: A Systematic Study of Token Embedding Initialization Strategies for LLM Vocabulary Extension
summary: A systematic study of over 20 token embedding initialization strategies for Large Language Model (LLM) vocabulary extension, analyzing their impact on the efficiency of continued pre-training for adapting models to new languages.

title: ConlangBench: Exploring Language Knowledge and Learning in LLMs through Diverse Constructed Languages
summary: Introduces ConlangBench, a new benchmark that uses diverse constructed languages (conlangs) to explore language knowledge and learning capabilities in Large Language Models (LLMs).

title: ChronoLens: Measuring Language Change Across Time, Languages, and Linguistic Levels
summary: Introduces ChronoLens, a computational method for measuring historical language change across different linguistic levels and languages, addressing the challenge of incompatible representations in existing studies.

title: Consensus Measures for Unstructured Biomedical Text Annotations
summary: A study on improving consensus measures and soft inter-rater reliability for annotators working with open-ended labels in unstructured biomedical text annotations.

title: Cross-Lingual Bias in Large Language Models: A Comparative Analysis of English and Swahili
summary: A comparative analysis of cross-lingual bias in Large Language Models (LLMs), investigating whether social biases generalize across languages by testing GPT-5.2 and Gemini with English-Swahili prompt pairs.

title: Hi-TTRL: Regulating Consensus with Hints for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
summary: Introduces Hi-TTRL, a method that regulates consensus with hints for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning (TTRL) to improve the reasoning capabilities of large language models without labeled data.

title: SFT Conflicts, RL Coexists: A Theoretical and Empirical Analysis of Multi-Task Learning for LLMs
summary: A theoretical and empirical analysis comparing Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) for multi-task learning in Large Language Models (LLMs), revealing task conflicts in SFT during multi-stage training.

title: Looking under the Wrong Lamppost: On the Limitations of Automated Translation Quality Estimation
summary: A critical analysis of the limitations inherent in automated Translation Quality Estimation (QE) systems, discussing their shortcomings despite their growing adoption for managing translation quality at scale.

title: Disentangling Language Modeling and Boundaries
summary: Discusses the structural advantages of byte-level language models, highlighting how their shared output space enables exact knowledge transfer between models, contributing to robustness and multilingual fairness.

title: Hunyuan3D-Buffalo 1.0: A Unified Multimodal Model for Scalable 3D Generation, Understanding, and Editing
summary: Announces Hunyuan3D-Buffalo 1.0, a unified multimodal model designed for scalable 3D generation, understanding, and editing, aiming to address constraints from scarce multimodal data in unified 3D modeling.

title: Quo Vadis, World Modeling?
summary: Explores world modeling as an intermediate proxy for AI agents to gather feedback, addressing the challenges of direct real-environment interaction for continuous improvement.

title: Confident but Unreliable: A Behavioral Safety Audit of Vision-Language Models on Brain MRI
summary: Conducts a behavioral safety audit of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in brain MRI interpretation, evaluating their stated confidence against correctness to identify broader failure modes in multimodal systems.

title: Better, Stronger, Faster, and Broader: Structured All-Mask Prediction for MLLM-Based Segmentation
summary: Proposes a new method for MLLM-based segmentation to overcome the trilemma of achieving high performance, preserved dialogue ability, and fast inference, by addressing challenges with embedding-prediction and next-token generation.

title: PixelUp: Zero-Shot Semantic Feature Upsampling for Fine-Grained Vision Tasks
summary: Introduces "PixelUp", a zero-shot semantic feature upsampling method designed to enhance self-supervised Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) for fine-grained vision tasks like semantic segmentation and depth estimation.

title: SAGE: Semantic Explainability of Attention-Based Survival Models in Computational Pathology
summary: Proposes "SAGE" to provide semantic explainability for attention-based survival models in computational pathology, aiming to clarify not just where a model focuses but also which histological features drive its predictions.

title: A Unified 2D Framework for DeepLesion Detection, Segmentation and Short Report Generation
summary: Develops a unified 2D framework for medical image analysis, integrating LLM-based reasoning for lesion detection, segmentation, and short report generation from the DeepLesion dataset.

title: In-Context Collapse in Vision-Language Models and How to Mitigate it?
summary: Identifies and analyzes "in-context collapse" in Vision-Language Models during many-shot in-context learning, where performance surprisingly degrades with more demonstrations, and proposes mitigation strategies.

title: CURV: Enhancing Chart Understanding Through Curriculum Visual Grounded Reasoning
summary: Introduces "CURV" (Curriculum Visual Grounded Reasoning) to enhance multimodal large language models' ability in chart question answering by improving visual grounding and coherent reasoning chains.

title: A Human-in-the-Loop Deep Learning Framework for Color Reconstruction of Lenticular Films
summary: Proposes a human-in-the-loop deep learning framework for accurately reconstructing colors in historical lenticular films, which encode color information in a distinctive spatial format.

title: Test Time Adaptation Methods for Point Cloud Registration in Laparoscopic Surgery
summary: Investigates test time adaptation methods for 3D point cloud registration in laparoscopic surgery, which estimates organ transformations by adapting networks trained on synthetic data to real-time scenarios.

title: RealWeather: Realistic and Scene-Faithful Weather Translation with Driving World Models
summary: Introduces "RealWeather" for realistic and scene-faithful weather translation using driving world models, aiming to generate diverse weather conditions for evaluating autonomous driving systems.

title: Qwen-3D: A Generalist 3D Vision-Language Model for Spatial Understanding
summary: Introduces "Qwen-3D", a generalist 3D Vision-Language Model designed for spatial understanding, addressing challenges in scaling large multimodal models to long videos using 3D geometry compression.

title: Clinically-Grounded Hierarchical Classification for Consistent Chest X-ray Interpretation
summary: Proposes a clinically-grounded hierarchical classification method to improve the consistency and accuracy of automated chest X-ray interpretation by structuring reasoning from broad anatomical systems to specific pathological findings.

title: Standalone DINOv3 for Training-Free Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation in Remote Sensing
summary: Explores the use of standalone DINOv3, specifically DINO.txt, for training-free open-vocabulary semantic segmentation in remote sensing, leveraging image-text contrastive learning to overcome annotation costs.

title: CAPE-T2V: Captioner-Anchored Prompt Enhancement toward Two-Sided Conditioning Alignment in Text-to-Video Generation
summary: Introduces "CAPE-T2V" (Captioner-Anchored Prompt Enhancement) to improve text-to-video generation by aligning conditioning between detailed training captions and user-driven inference prompts.

title: AIDE: Automated Instruction via Distilled Expertise for Reference-Free Motor Skill Coaching
summary: Proposes "AIDE" (Automated Instruction via Distilled Expertise), a reference-free method for generating natural-language coaching feedback on motor skills, aiming to accelerate learning without requiring expert demonstrations.

title: TASQ: Temporal-Adaptive Bit Sparsification Quantization for Diffusion Models
summary: Introduces "TASQ" (Temporal-Adaptive Bit Sparsification Quantization), a method for diffusion models that dynamically adjusts weight precision per denoising step to improve efficiency while preserving quality.

title: RIDGE: Re-Noising with Internal Dynamic Guidance for Image Editing
summary: Introduces "RIDGE" (Re-Noising with Internal Dynamic Guidance), a method for inversion-free flow-based image editing that improves by addressing inconsistencies in displacement between noisy source and target states across noise levels.

title: Global Graph-Validated Optimization for VLM-based 3D Indoor Scene Generation
summary: Explores global graph-validated optimization for VLM-based 3D indoor scene generation, synthesizing diverse and physically plausible 3D layouts from unlabeled assets using free-form language instructions.

title: LDU-Bench: Multimodal LLM Evaluation for Lithography Defect Understanding under Layout-Varying Circuit Backgrounds
summary: Introduces "LDU-Bench," a new benchmark designed for evaluating multimodal large language models on lithography defect understanding, focusing on comprehensive defect morphology and spatial recognition.

title: CorePath: A Breast-Specialized Pathology Foundation Model for Core Needle Biopsy Diagnosis and Risk-Controlled Report Generation
summary: CorePath is a breast-specialized multimodal pathology foundation model developed for diagnosing breast cancer from core needle biopsies and generating risk-controlled reports.

title: DiverseDiT++: Quantifying, Analyzing, and Promoting Representation Diversity in Diffusion Transformers
summary: DiverseDiT++ proposes methods for quantifying, analyzing, and promoting representation diversity within Diffusion Transformers to enhance their visual synthesis capabilities.

title: GSTEP: Global Spatio-Temporal Density-Driven Visual Token Pruning for Efficient Video Large Language Models
summary: GSTEP introduces a global spatio-temporal density-driven visual token pruning method to make Video Large Language Models more efficient by reducing redundant tokens during inference.

title: SUV: Future Scene Understanding as Video Generation for End-to-End Driving
summary: SUV is a unified end-to-end driving framework that models future scene understanding as video generation to improve autonomous vehicle performance.

title: Channel-wise Dynamic Knowledge Distillation via Adaptive Sample Generation for Action Recognition
summary: This paper proposes Channel-wise Dynamic Knowledge Distillation via Adaptive Sample Generation to efficiently compress large action recognition models while improving feature alignment.

title: Multimodal Plant Root Phenotyping with Integration of 3D Skeleton Extraction and Language Analysis
summary: This research presents a multimodal robotic AI framework that integrates 3D skeleton extraction and language analysis for interpretable and data-driven plant root phenotyping, optimizing crop management.

title: Adaptive Two-Stage Visual Token Pruning for Efficient Inference in Video-Language Models
summary: This paper introduces an adaptive two-stage visual token pruning method designed to achieve efficient inference in Vision-Language Models, particularly for resource-constrained environments.

title: Non-Destructive Quantification of Urea Adulteration in Bovine Milk Using Transmittance Multispectral Imaging
summary: This research presents a non-destructive method using transmittance multispectral imaging for quantifying urea adulteration in bovine milk, addressing food quality and health concerns.

title: Rectify Then Diffuse: Disentangling Concepts Before Denoising Trajectory Unfolds
summary: This paper proposes "Rectify Then Diffuse," a method to improve text-to-image diffusion models' handling of multiple concepts by disentangling them before the denoising process begins.

title: Frozen High-Resolution Inference for Cross-City Object Detection: An AI City Challenge 2026 Study
summary: This study analyzes frozen high-resolution inference for cross-city object detection using an RF-DETR-Large detector, focusing on generalization challenges for the AI City Challenge 2026.

title: From Routes to Steps: Separating Semantic Progress from Local Execution in Vision-and-Language Navigation
summary: This paper proposes a method to separate semantic progress from local execution in Vision-and-Language Navigation, improving how agents follow route-level instructions from egocentric observations.

title: CROSS: Cascaded Distillation and Dual-Constraint Grounding for Remote Sensing Referring Segmentation
summary: CROSS introduces cascaded distillation and dual-constraint grounding to enhance Referring Remote Sensing Image Segmentation, addressing limitations in integrating VLMs and the Segment Anything Model.

title: Frequency-Decorrelated Temporal Ensembles for EEG--fNIRS Imagined-Handwriting Decoding
summary: This research proposes frequency-decorrelated temporal ensembles for robust decoding of imagined handwriting from combined EEG and fNIRS signals for brain-computer interface applications.

title: EditFlow3D: Automated Local Editing of 3D Assets with Trajectory Preservation
summary: EditFlow3D introduces an automated method for local editing of 3D assets, enabling precise target localization and trajectory preservation while achieving desired visual guidance.

title: CRIL-U-Net: Compact Ratio-Interaction Learning for Focal Cortical Dysplasia Segmentation from T1w and FLAIR MRI
summary: CRIL-U-Net is a compact ratio-interaction learning model designed for the challenging segmentation of Focal Cortical Dysplasia from T1w and FLAIR MRI scans.

title: Bridging Online and Offline Handwriting via Differentiable Physical Rendering
summary: This research introduces a method using differentiable physical rendering to bridge online and offline handwriting, enabling realistic handwritten text generation for applications like font design and biometric authentication.

title: DRIFT: Derailing Denoising Trajectories of Flow-Matching VLAs with Adversarial Patch Attack
summary: DRIFT demonstrates that flow-matching Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models like pi0, used for robot actions, are vulnerable to adversarial patch attacks despite their reported robustness, raising safety concerns.

title: CrossScope: A Role-Asymmetric World Model for Joint Dual-Scope Surgical Video Prediction
summary: CrossScope introduces a role-asymmetric world model designed for joint dual-scope surgical video prediction, enabling the modeling of future dynamics from multiple independent observers in cooperative systems.

title: iFAN: Inference-Aware Learning for Plain Mask Transformers
summary: iFAN introduces an inference-aware learning method for plain mask transformers, optimizing the training process to better align with the actual pixel-wise competition during segmentation output generation.

title: Self-Supervised Representation-Guided Generative Dataset Distillation
summary: This research proposes a self-supervised representation-guided generative dataset distillation method to compress large training sets into compact synthetic sets while retaining their downstream utility.

title: Open-Linguistic Concept Unified Learning for Cross-Site Interpretable Dermatology Image Diagnosis
summary: This paper presents a method for open-linguistic concept unified learning to achieve interpretable and generalizable dermatology image diagnosis across different sites. It focuses on concept-based models for transparent reasoning in clinical decision-making.

title: CIGTSurv: Clinical Information Guided Tri-modal Survival Prediction with Local Prototype Association and Global Feature Alignment
summary: This research introduces CIGTSurv, a tri-modal survival prediction method that integrates pathology images, genomic data, and underutilized clinical information. It employs local prototype association and global feature alignment for enhanced prediction.

title: Clarity Contrast and Similarity Selection for Multi-Focus Image Fusion
summary: This paper proposes a deep learning method for multi-focus image fusion that incorporates explicit interaction between source images through clarity, contrast, and similarity selection. The goal is to generate an all-in-focus image with improved performance and interpretability.

title: GUI-Lens: Coarse-to-Fine Cropping for GUI Grounding with General-Purpose VLMs
summary: GUI-Lens is a coarse-to-fine cropping method designed to improve GUI grounding for Vision-Language Models (VLMs), enabling more precise location of controls from natural language instructions. This is crucial for building reliable GUI agents.

title: 3DGSI-Assessor: A Large-Scale Dataset and An LMM-based Method for 3D Gaussian Splatting Image Quality Assessment
summary: This research introduces 3DGSI-Assessor, a large-scale dataset and an LMM-based method for assessing the image quality of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) representations. The method aims to evaluate distortions introduced by 3DGS training and compression.

title: Test-Time Scaling for Safe Text-Guided Image Generation via Intermediate Clean Estimates
summary: This paper proposes a test-time scaling method to enhance safety and policy compliance in text-to-image diffusion models by generating intermediate clean estimates. It addresses the critical challenge of preventing prohibited content generation from benign or adversarial prompts.

title: Light-Loco-Parkour: Versatile Perceptive Whole-Body Locomotion via Multi-Skill Distillation
summary: Light-Loco-Parkour presents a versatile perceptive whole-body locomotion system for humanoids that utilizes multi-skill distillation to navigate cluttered terrain. The system enables expressive movements while reacting to the environment and utilizing the robot's full body.

title: Semantic Haptic Feedback Enhances Dexterous Robotic Teleoperation
summary: This research explores how semantic haptic feedback can enhance dexterous robotic teleoperation. It aims to improve human operators' ability to accomplish complex manipulation tasks by providing more informative feedback than simple replication of physical sensations.

title: Toward Certified Functional Safety for Industrial Humanoid Robots: The Fail-Passive Gap and a Feasibility Study
summary: This study investigates the challenges in achieving certified functional safety for industrial humanoid robots, particularly addressing the 'fail-passive gap' for legged platforms. It conducts a feasibility study on current safety certification limitations for these robots.

title: Staying on Spec: Real-Time Monitoring under Uncertainty with a Maritime Case Study
summary: This paper proposes a method for real-time monitoring of robotic systems operating under uncertainty to ensure compliance with complex task and safety specifications. It includes a maritime case study to demonstrate its application.

title: Control Barrier Functions via Minkowski Operations for Safe Navigation among Polytopes
summary: This research introduces a method for safe navigation of robots in polytopic environments using Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) via Minkowski Operations. It aims to synthesize safe control policies that respect robot dynamics, controls, and exact geometry.

title: Contact-Driven Localization in a Freeform Robotic Self-Assembled Structure
summary: This paper presents a contact-driven localization method for swarm robotics within freeform self-assembled structures. It addresses the challenge of accurate relative positioning in reconfigurable systems without relying on external tracking or high-cost sensors.

title: ValueFormer: A Causal Transformer Value Function with Stage-Aware Labels for Semi-Autonomous Vision-Language-Action Policies
summary: ValueFormer proposes a causal Transformer value function with stage-aware labels to improve semi-autonomous Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies. This aims to provide VLA models with a notion of progress, addressing the limitations of behavior cloning in embodied systems.

title: EmbodiedVAE: Disentangled Video VAE for Efficient and Controllable Embodied Manipulation
summary: EmbodiedVAE introduces a disentangled video Variational Autoencoder designed for efficient and controllable embodied manipulation tasks. It aims to overcome limitations of existing VAEs optimized for natural scenes, providing better world models for embodied learning.

title: PACE: Adaptive Budget Allocation for Time-Efficient Embodied Planning
summary: PACE proposes an adaptive budget allocation strategy for time-efficient embodied planning using reasoning-enhanced large language models. The method aims to reduce prohibitive inference delays, making LLM-based planning practical for embodied systems.

title: CUDA MPC: A GPU-Native Solver for Model Predictive Control
summary: CUDA MPC presents a GPU-native solver for Model Predictive Control (MPC), addressing its computational demands for fast dynamics and high-dimensional models. This implementation leverages GPUs to accelerate the online optimization required by MPC.

title: How Should Vision-Language-Action Models Use Proprioceptive State?
summary: This paper investigates how Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, used in embodied AI, should effectively incorporate robot proprioceptive state. It analyzes different input methods for proprioception, including text prompts, vision-language prefixes, and direct expert feeds.

title: A Hierarchical Approach to Imitation Learning for Manipulation Tasks Requiring Time Varying Forces
summary: This research proposes a hierarchical approach to imitation learning for robotic manipulation tasks that require time-varying forces, particularly in contact-rich disassembly. It addresses the inference latency trade-offs inherent in diffusion policies for such applications.

title: Shooting for Contact: Contact-Implicit Multiple Shooting for Dynamic Motion Retargeting
summary: Shooting for Contact introduces a contact-implicit multiple shooting method for dynamic motion retargeting in robotics. This approach prioritizes whole-body dynamics, contact consistency, and actuation limits to generate reproducible contact-rich behaviors for RL policies.

title: Accelerating Human-Aware Robot Trajectory Generation via Diffusion and Consistency Distillation
summary: This research presents a constrained motion planning framework for robot manipulators that accelerates human-aware trajectory generation using diffusion and consistency distillation. The goal is to safely plan robot movements in human-robot interaction scenarios, accounting for collision avoidance.

title: PFM-HR: Pose Flow Matching for Humanoid Robots
summary: This paper introduces PFM-HR, a pose flow matching method to improve reinforcement learning for physics-based humanoid robot tracking, addressing limitations of existing motion priors.

title: Structure-Aware Robust Fine-Tuning: Defending Vision-Language-Action Robots Against Physical Attention Hijacking
summary: This research proposes a structure-aware fine-tuning method to defend Vision-Language-Action (VLA) robots against physical adversarial attacks that could induce manipulation failures.

title: Learning Context-Aware Motion Priors for Humanoid Control
summary: This work presents a method for learning context-aware motion priors to guide humanoid control, enabling more naturalistic behaviors than task-agnostic priors.

title: GraspMeanFlow: SE(3)-Equivariant MeanFlow for Few-Step 6-DoF Grasp Generation
summary: This paper introduces GraspMeanFlow, an SE(3)-equivariant flow-based model for efficient and diverse 6-DoF grasp pose generation for robotic manipulation.

title: PLS-Calib: A Partial Least Squares Framework for Event Camera and Odometry Calibration under Ground Motion Constraints
summary: This research proposes PLS-Calib, a Partial Least Squares framework for calibrating event cameras and odometry sensors on ground-constrained robots with limited motion.

title: RoboReact: Agentic Skill Distillation from Generated Egocentric Videos for Generalizable Whole-Body Manipulation
summary: This paper introduces RoboReact, a method for distilling agentic skills from generated egocentric videos to enable generalizable whole-body manipulation in humanoid robots.

title: Flying over The Uncertain Nature (FORTUNE): Intelligent and Humanistic 3D Path Planning for Low-Altitude Collaboration
summary: This research focuses on FORTUNE, an intelligent 3D path planning system for low-altitude drones performing collaborative sensing in dynamic urban environments, considering uncertainty and human factors.

title: A Low-Cost Hybrid Reservoir Computing Model for Isolated Sign Language Video Recognition
summary: This study proposes a low-cost hybrid reservoir computing model to achieve efficient and accurate isolated sign language video recognition on edge devices.

title: Continue or Replan? Bernoulli-Continuation Policy Learning for Adaptive Horizon Execution
summary: This paper presents Bernoulli-Continuation Policy Learning for adaptive horizon execution, improving replanning decisions in chunk-based Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for robots.

title: Lightweight 3D Object Detection via Mamba-Based Knowledge Distillation
summary: This work introduces a lightweight 3D object detection method using Mamba-Based Knowledge Distillation for efficient perception in autonomous driving and robotic navigation.

title: Principles of Robot Autonomy
summary: This item discusses the principles and field-tested methods of robot autonomy, highlighting its move from research labs into real-world deployments across various domains.

title: Pivot-Centric Trajectory Prediction: Bridging Long Horizons via Dynamical Guidance
summary: This research proposes Pivot-Centric Trajectory Prediction, a method that uses dynamical guidance to improve long-horizon motion forecasting for autonomous vehicles.

title: Human Centric Embodied Intelligence for Soft Wearable Robotics
summary: This paper explores the integration of human-centric embodied intelligence in soft wearable robots for applications such as rehabilitation, occupational assistance, and human augmentation.

title: Unified Visuomotor Targets: Supervising VLAs Beyond Physical Actions
summary: This research investigates using unified visuomotor targets to supervise VLA models more effectively by bridging the gap between high-level visual language representations and low-level robot actions.

title: LiLa-WAM: Lightweight Latent Reasoning World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation
summary: This paper introduces LiLa-WAM, a lightweight latent reasoning world-action model designed to provide efficient and anticipatory robotic control for manipulation tasks.

title: Track4Action: Distilling World-Centric 3D Tracker into Vision-Language-Action Policies
summary: This research presents Track4Action, a method for distilling a world-centric 3D tracker into Vision-Language-Action policies to provide robots with richer supervision about how commands change the environment.

title: GORDON: Graph-based Object-centric Rewards for Decomposition of Long-Horizon Manipulation
summary: This paper proposes GORDON, a method using graph-based object-centric rewards for decomposing and learning long-horizon manipulation skills in reinforcement learning for robots.

title: Design and Evaluation of an AI-Enabled Cloud-Edge Architecture for Connected Precision Agriculture Farms
summary: This study details the design and evaluation of an AI-enabled cloud-edge architecture to monitor and detect plant diseases for connected precision agriculture farms.

title: EvoHIL: Self-Evolving Reward and Flow-Matched Policy Optimization for Robust Human-in-the-Loop Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper introduces EvoHIL, a framework for self-evolving reward and flow-matched policy optimization to achieve robust human-in-the-loop reinforcement learning for robot manipulation.

title: ETA: A New Agentic Paradigm for Embodied Tasks
summary: This article discusses ETA, a new agentic paradigm aimed at enabling general-purpose robots to perform embodied tasks in unfamiliar environments and learn from experience.

title: Bimanual Manipulation Within an 8 GB Budget: Zero-Copy Sensing and Quantized ACT on an Entry-Level Jetson
summary: Bimanual manipulation policies trained with imitation learning are typically evaluated on workstation or datacenter-class GPUs, leaving the cost of deploying them on embedded hardware largely uncharacterized. We present a bimanual SO-101 system running entirely on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super (8 GB), the entry-level tier of NVIDIA's embedded line, using a desktop GPU (RTX 3070) only for offline training, evaluated on pick-and-place of a deformable beanbag. First, we build a GStreamer capture pipeline backed by NVMM buffers that removes redundant host-device copies from three-camera sensing. Contrary to expectation, the conventional path fit the memory budget and dropped no frames; what zero-copy sensing recovers is CPU headroom (peak single-core utilization 98.0% to 77.0%) and worst-case latency (117.31 ms to 101.52 ms). Second, we train ACT and Diffusion Policy on identical demonstrations, each at its own reference budget (100k gradient steps for ACT, 200k for Diffusion Policy). ACT converges to a task-competent policy (19/20 trials) while Diffusion Policy does not converge to a usable one (0/10) even at twice the step count, which we attribute to differing convergence costs rather than an accuracy ceiling. Third, we convert ACT to TensorRT. FP16 reduces mean inference latency from 114.02 ms to 17.93 ms (6.4x) and INT8 to 12.65 ms (9.0x), with task success preserved at all three precisions (19/20, 18/20, 19/20). We report two findings not previously documented for ACT: TensorRT's general-purpose INT8 calibration quantizes the ResNet18 backbone but accepts zero of 145 transformer layers, explaining INT8's negligible size reduction over FP16 (0.9%) despite a further 28% latency gain; and the need for quantization is conditional on ACT's action-chunking configuration, feasible in full precision at n_action_steps = 100 but not at the per-step re-prediction temporal ensembling requires.

title: Stochastic Multiple Shooting Trajectory Optimization via Sequential Local Policy Evaluation
summary: Stochastic single shooting trajectory optimization methods such as Model Predictive Path Integral control (MPPI) have been widely adopted in robotics due to their ability to reason about probabilistic dynamics and provide solutions where model gradients are noisy, costly to evaluate, or unavailable. However, satisfaction of terminal constraints when shooting over long action sequences is often sample inefficient, requiring a large number of iterations for convergence. In this paper, we present a stochastic multiple shooting method that optimizes short control action sequences connected via local feedback policies to improve sample efficiency and convergence to a terminal set. Additionally, we show that we are able to synthesize approximate system Jacobians purely from rollouts, making the method suitable for model-based reinforcement learning with black-box dynamics. We demonstrate the algorithm has improved sample efficiency and terminal set convergence for three nonlinear, underactuated optimization problems: a classic cartpole swingup task with analytical dynamics, a cartpole swingup task with learned neural network dynamics, and a VTOL quadplane performing a high angle-of-attack, precision post-stall landing maneuver.

title: SLAMFormer-$\infty$: Infinite SLAM Transformer for Unbounded Frontend and Backend Processing
summary: We introduce the Infinite SLAM Transformer (SLAMFormer-$\infty$), the first geometric transformer capable of supporting both long-range frontend and backend processing without an explicit distance bound. Instead of relying on a first-frame-anchored formulation, SLAMFormer-$\infty$ employs memory conditions to define flexible coordinate systems and scales for input frames, enabling more expressive structural conditioning. Built upon this formulation, the frontend preserves efficient local computation, while the backend jointly optimizes long-range trajectories and scene geometry in a globally consistent manner. Experimental results demonstrate that SLAMFormer-$\infty$ achieves superior or highly competitive performance in both trajectory estimation and scene reconstruction across large-scale datasets. Notably, SLAMFormer-$\infty$ generalizes to extremely long trajectories, successfully operating on sequences exceeding $17\mathrm{km}$.

title: PhyAI: Real-Time Physical AI at the Edge, Scalable Rollouts in the Cloud
summary: Physical AI policies require inference throughout their lifecycle, including model evaluation, cloud reinforcement learning rollout, edge GPU serving, and onboard deployment. Although these settings share the same checkpoint and action semantics, they often rely on separate inference programs. To unify them, we build PhyAI, a Physical AI inference engine with a single runtime that keeps architecture-specific conditioning, solver, cache, and output logic in model adapters while sharing graph execution, kernels, memory management, and parallel services. The same codebase runs vision-language-action (VLA) models and world-action models (WAMs) on single or multiple GPUs across onboard, edge, and cloud deployments. We used the adapter interface to add MiniCPM-Robot on the day of its release. PhyAI achieves 1.40x-4.65x speedups over the official implementations of pi0, pi0.5, GR00T N1.7, and MiniCPM-Robot. On Cosmos3-Nano-Policy-DROID it reduces latency from 2.46 to 1.18 s on eight H20 GPUs (CFG=2, TP=4), a 2.08x speedup. Specialized runtimes remain faster in several configurations, so our goal is one runtime with competitive latency rather than the fastest result in every case. Detailed profiles reveal why different models need different execution policies: on a Hopper-series GPU at batch size one, the pi0.5 action expert accounts for 8.8% of FLOPs but 57.2% of latency; at batch size 32 its share drops to 13.5% and throughput reaches about 100 samples/s. Cosmos3 remains generation-dominated and gains only 14.3% throughput as batch size increases from 1 to 16. We further introduce the control-time Roofline, which distinguishes inference-bound from environment-bound control; the measured pi0.5 points on four LIBERO suites are environment-bound while Cosmos3 stays inference-bound. Code and benchmarks: https://github.com/mingti-org/phyai.

title: Mixed-Initiative Human-Robot Teaming under Suboptimality with Online Bayesian Adaptation
summary: For effective human-agent teaming, robots and other artificial intelligence (AI) agents must infer their human partner's abilities and behavioral response patterns and adapt accordingly. Most prior works make the unrealistic assumption that one or more teammates can act near-optimally. In real-world collaboration, humans and autonomous agents can be suboptimal, especially when each only has partial domain knowledge. In this work, we develop computational modeling and optimization techniques for enhancing the performance of suboptimal human-agent teams, where the human and the agent have asymmetric capabilities and act suboptimally due to incomplete environmental knowledge. We adopt an online Bayesian approach that enables a robot to infer people's willingness to comply with its assistance in a sequential decision-making game. Our user studies show that user preferences and team performance indeed vary with robot intervention styles, and our approach for mixed-initiative collaborations enhances objective team performance ($p<.001$) and subjective measures, such as user's trust ($p<.001$) and willingness to comply with the robot ($p<.001$).

title: Electrostatic Clutch-Based Mechanical Multiplexer with Increased Force Capability
summary: As robotic systems become increasingly articulated, conventional actuation still dedicates one motor to each degree of freedom (DoF). Mechanical multiplexers address this limitation by allowing a single motor to control multiple outputs through clutches, reducing the number of required motors. However, previous multiplexers have relied on bulky mechanical clutch designs, limiting their development. This study presents an electrostatic capstan clutch-based transmission architecture that enables high-force mechanical multiplexing with independent, simultaneous, and fully actuated control of multiple outputs from a single motor. Our transmission implements four fully-actuated linear outputs, achieving individual output forces of up to 212 N and output speeds of up to 69.5 mm/s. We demonstrate our transmission on a commercial tendon-driven hand, where sequentially allocating system-wide torque capacity to individual outputs increased vertical grip strength by 4.09x and raised horizontal carrying capacity to 111.2 N, the highest reported among five-fingered tendon-driven robotic hands. These results demonstrate that electrostatic clutch-based mechanical multiplexing enables high-force, independent, simultaneous, and fully actuated control while overcoming the limitations of previous mechanical multiplexers.

title: FGGS-LiDAR: Ultra-Fast, GPU-Accelerated Simulation from General 3DGS Models to LiDAR
summary: While 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has emerged as a strong representation for photorealistic rendering, its vast ecosystem of assets remains difficult to use for high-performance LiDAR simulation, a critical tool for robotics and autonomous driving. We present \textbf{FGGS-LiDAR}, a geometry-first framework that bridges this gap in a plug-and-play manner. Our method converts pretrained 3DGS assets into watertight meshes directly from Gaussian parameters, without requiring LiDAR-specific supervision or architectural alterations, via volumetric discretization and Truncated Signed Distance Field (TSDF) extraction. We pair this with a GPU-accelerated ray-casting module that simulates LiDAR returns at over 500 FPS and supports batched multi-environment simulation with up to 4096 environments. In large-scale parallel settings, FGGS-LiDAR achieves an order-of-magnitude lower LiDAR simulation latency than Isaac Sim. We validate FGGS-LiDAR on both indoor and outdoor scenes, demonstrating high LiDAR-simulation fidelity. Furthermore, on COLMAP-posed indoor benchmarks, we compare against existing 3DGS-to-mesh baselines and report lower LiDAR-simulation error. Code is at https://github.com/discoverse-dev/FGGS-LiDAR.

title: PACE: Physics Augmentation for Coordinated End-to-end Reinforcement Learning toward Versatile Humanoid Table Tennis
summary: Humanoid table tennis (TT) demands rapid perception, proactive whole-body motion, and agile footwork under strict timing--capabilities that remain difficult for end-to-end control policies. We propose a reinforcement learning (RL) framework that maps ball-position observations directly to whole-body joint commands for both arm striking and leg locomotion, strengthened by predictive signals and dense, physics-guided rewards. A lightweight learned predictor, fed with recent ball positions, estimates future ball states and augments the policy's observations for proactive decision-making. During training, a physics-based predictor supplies precise future states to construct dense, informative rewards that lead to effective exploration. The resulting policy attains strong performance across varied serve ranges (hit rate$\geq$96% and success rate$\geq$92%) in simulations. Ablation studies confirm that both the learned predictor and the predictive reward design are critical for end-to-end learning. Deployed zero-shot on a physical Booster T1 humanoid with 23 revolute joints, the policy produces coordinated lateral and forward-backward footwork with accurate, fast returns, suggesting a practical path toward versatile, competitive humanoid TT. We have open-sourced our RL training code at: https://github.com/purdue-tracelab/TTRL-ICRA2026
