summary: Investigates how privileged information (PI)-conditioned teachers can introduce bias and break the self-distillation process in compute-efficient reinforcement learning alternatives.

title: ContextWeave: A Real-World Workflow Benchmark
summary: Introduces ContextWeave, a real-world workflow benchmark designed to evaluate how memory and recalled experience improve the performance of language agents in long-horizon, stateful tasks.

title: WorldCycle: Self-Verifiable Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Video World Models
summary: Proposes WorldCycle, a self-verifiable reinforcement learning approach designed to improve the accuracy and overcome compounding errors in long-horizon video world models.

title: Short-term load forecasting under EU-AI Act Requirements in Safety-Critical Environments: Results from a 41-day live challenge on the aggregated German transmission-grid load
summary: This paper analyzes short-term load forecasting in the electric power industry under the requirements of the EU AI Act, focusing on determinism, reproducibility, and auditability in safety-critical environments. It presents results from a 41-day live challenge on the German transmission-grid load.

title: From Score Matrices to Football-Aware Match-State Simulation: An Auditable LLM Harness for Exact-Score Reranking
summary: This research introduces an auditable LLM harness for exact-score reranking in football forecasting, combining statistical models with contextual understanding of game dynamics. It aims to improve prediction accuracy by simulating match states beyond pure probabilities.

title: Item Response Theory for AI Safety
summary: This paper proposes using Item Response Theory to improve the measurement and interpretation of AI safety in language models, addressing limitations of current aggregated safety benchmarks. It aims to provide a more reliable assessment of how safely models behave.

title: Hierarchical Graph Memory for LLM Agents with Path-level Localization and Rewrite
summary: This research introduces hierarchical graph memory for LLM agents, designed for long-term reasoning with efficient updates, path-level localization, and rewrite capabilities. It aims to improve structural organization for multi-hop retrieval and reasoning.

title: ABSeeker: Training Long-Horizon Search Agents via Answer-Backtracked Credit Assignment
summary: ABSeeker is a new method for training long-horizon search agents by using answer-backtracked credit assignment, which improves learning for agents performing multiple sequential actions to search, retrieve, verify, and integrate evidence. This approach addresses the limitations of uniform treatment of steps in existing training methods.

title: CoPlan: A Trustworthy Co-Intelligence Interface for Care Planning through Role-Based Contestable Argument Graphs
summary: CoPlan is an AI-supported co-intelligence interface for care planning that uses role-based contestable argument graphs, allowing clinicians, patients, and caregivers to inspect and challenge AI recommendations for complex decisions. This aims to foster trustworthiness and improve coordination.

title: OctoLong: Mid-Training On Cross-Repository Code Contexts Enhances Long-Context Modeling
summary: OctoLong improves long-context modeling in language models by integrating mid-training on cross-repository code contexts. This method aims to enhance capabilities for in-context learning, self-improvement, and long-horizon agentic workflows.

title: Argus: A General-Purpose Agentic Runtime for Long-Horizon Reasoning
summary: Argus is a general-purpose, persistent, and self-evolving agentic runtime designed for long-horizon reasoning, featuring components like Manager, Planner, and Engineer. It allows agents to adapt and pivot based on evidence and observed constraints.

title: AutoProteinEngine: A Large Language Model Driven Agent Framework for Multimodal AutoML in Protein Engineering
summary: AutoProteinEngine is a large language model-driven agent framework that facilitates multimodal AutoML in protein engineering. This framework aims to overcome challenges in training and implementing deep learning models for biologists without specialized expertise.

title: TourSynbio-Search: A Large Language Model Driven Agent Framework for Unified Search Method for Protein Engineering
summary: TourSynbio-Search introduces a novel large language model-driven agent framework for a unified search method in protein engineering. It aims to efficiently retrieve biological information from vast databases and scientific literature.

title: Temporal Context Awareness: A Defense Framework Against Multi-turn Manipulation Attacks on Large Language Models
summary: This paper proposes "Temporal Context Awareness" as a defense framework to protect Large Language Models from multi-turn manipulation attacks. It aims to circumvent adversaries' attempts to build context and elicit harmful or unauthorized responses.

title: RAG-Stack: Co-Optimizing RAG Serving Performance and Quality
summary: RAG-Stack is a system designed for co-optimizing the serving performance and quality of Retrieval-augmented Generation (RAG) systems. It addresses the complexity of configuring various components like retrieval indexes to enhance knowledge-intensive LLM applications.

title: Towards a New Grammar of Reasoning for Artificial Legal Intelligence and the Mecelle as Its Semantic Protocol
summary: This article proposes a new "grammar of reasoning" for Artificial Legal Intelligence, introducing the Mecellem semantic protocol as an ontologically grounded framework to address the epistemic and methodological challenges of traditional legal practice.

title: C$^2$MOE: Consistency and Complementarity-guided Mixture of Experts for Incomplete Multimodal Emotion Learning
summary: C$^2$MOE proposes a Consistency and Complementarity-guided Mixture of Experts model to enhance Multimodal Emotion Recognition in Conversations (MERC) when faced with incomplete multimodal inputs. It aims to improve robustness against missing modalities that degrade performance.

title: AI-driven Multimodal Representation Learning for Latent Mediation Structure Discovery of Socioeconomic Disadvantage, Psychosocial Factors, and Cardiometabolic Multimorbidity: Insights from the All of Us Research Program
summary: This research develops an AI-driven multimodal mediation framework for discovering latent structures linking socioeconomic disadvantage, psychosocial factors, and cardiometabolic multimorbidity. It integrates diverse health data from the All of Us Research Program.

title: Governing Execution Risk in Agentic AI Systems: A Trajectory-Guided Framework for Red Teaming
summary: This paper proposes a trajectory-guided framework for red teaming to govern execution risk in agentic AI systems, particularly when integrated into organizational workflows. It aims to identify and mitigate risks from malicious or untrusted inputs.

title: NuclearDiffusion: Text-to-Image Foundation Models for Learning Nuclear Energy Concepts
summary: NuclearDiffusion introduces specialized text-to-image foundation models designed for learning nuclear energy concepts, aiming to generate accurate imagery in this engineering domain. This addresses the limitations of general-purpose models that often produce physically incorrect images.

title: EDATracer: An Agentic Framework for Large-Scale EDA Artifact Analysis
summary: EDATracer is an agentic framework designed for large-scale analysis of diverse artifacts generated by electronic design automation (EDA) tools. It aims to simplify debugging, optimization, and understanding of chip design flows.

title: CheckOne: Lightweight Fault Detection and Mitigation for Vision Transformers
summary: CheckOne introduces a lightweight fault detection and mitigation method for Vision Transformers, enhancing their reliability in safety-critical applications. It addresses concerns about hardware faults by providing symmetric protection mechanisms for deep neural networks.

title: Reconstructing Persistent Worlds from Narratives for Narrative-Grounded Interactive Experiences
summary: This paper investigates methods for reconstructing persistent virtual worlds from narratives to create interactive experiences. It focuses on labor-intensive challenges like narrative planning, scene, and gameplay generation.

title: Robust and Personalized Federated Learning for Aircraft-Engine Prognostics under Benign and Adversarial Client Heterogeneity
summary: This study explores robust and personalized federated learning for aircraft-engine prognostics, handling benign and adversarial client heterogeneity. It enables joint training of remaining-useful-life models from engine sensor data without sharing raw data.

title: Beyond the QBER Threshold: A Temporal QBER Based Machine Learning Framework for Multi Attack Detection in BB84 QKD
summary: This paper proposes a machine learning framework based on temporal Quantum Bit Error Rate (QBER) for multi-attack detection in BB84 Quantum Key Distribution (QKD). It aims to detect stealthy attacks that remain below the conventional QBER threshold.

title: Recurrent Residual Quantization: A Progressive Multi-Precision Representation for LLMs
summary: This work introduces Recurrent Residual Quantization, a progressive multi-precision representation for Large Language Models (LLMs). It aims to provide flexible trade-offs between accuracy, memory, and throughput for LLM deployment by offering multiple bit-widths from a single checkpoint.

title: Learning to Resolve Neutron Resonances with Fully Convolutional Neural Networks
summary: This research explores using Fully Convolutional Neural Networks to automatically detect neutron resonances in transmission spectra. It aims to augment traditional R-Matrix codes by addressing the complexity and noise in neutron transmission data.

title: An Explainable LLM Agent Layer for Open-World Anomaly Detection in Oil Wells
summary: This paper describes an explainable LLM Agent Layer designed for open-world anomaly detection in oil wells. It combines autoencoder-based detection, multiclass classification, and novelty detection to provide explanations for identified anomalies.

title: SJEPA: Learning Elegant Latent Dynamics with Hybrid Symbolic-Neural Predictors
summary: This paper introduces SJEPA, a reconstruction-free Joint-embedding Predictive Architecture framework that learns predictive representations with elegant latent dynamics. It uses hybrid symbolic-neural predictors to learn abstract states by predicting target embeddings from context embeddings.

title: Spend Bits Where Queries Look: KV Cache Vector Quantization with Attention-Preserving Transforms
summary: This work proposes KV Cache Vector Quantization with Attention-Preserving Transforms to optimize long-context LLM decoding. The method aims to reduce the Key-Value cache size to improve decoding speed and serving capacity by applying quantization where queries look.

title: Spatiotemporal Graph Transformer for Traffic Intelligence in Edge Computing
summary: This research presents a Spatiotemporal Graph Transformer for traffic intelligence in edge computing environments. It focuses on accurate traffic forecasting to enable proactive resource management by capturing strong spatial correlations and long-range temporal dependencies.

title: SpecDrop: Parameter-Free Category-Conditioned Routing for Modular Specialization
summary: This paper introduces SpecDrop, a parameter-free category-conditioned routing mechanism for modular specialization in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) networks. It investigates whether the bottleneck in MoE performance lies in routing algorithms or alignment between training signals and routing decisions.

title: LiNC: Lightweight Noise Correction via Per-Sample Trust and Gaussian Mixture Modeling
summary: This paper proposes LiNC (Lightweight Noise Correction), a method to correct label noise in medical imaging datasets using per-sample trust and Gaussian Mixture Modeling. It aims to improve the reliability and clinical effectiveness of machine learning models trained on noisy data.

title: Understanding Fault Tolerance of Adversarially Robust Pruned Models
summary: This study investigates the fault tolerance of adversarially robust pruned Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) when deployed on resource-constrained neuromorphic hardware. It examines their susceptibility to adversarial input perturbations and hardware-induced weight faults like stuck-at-zero errors.

title: TS2TabPFN: Time Series Classification and Extrinsic Regression through Feature Extraction and a Tabular Foundation Model
summary: This paper introduces TS2TabPFN for time series classification and extrinsic regression using feature extraction and a tabular foundation model. It addresses challenges in obtaining value from temporal sequences, which are ubiquitous in practical applications.

title: A Comparative Study of Feature Selection Methods for EHR Diagnosis Codes in Opioid Use Disorder Prediction
summary: This paper presents a comparative study of feature selection methods for EHR diagnosis codes in predicting Opioid Use Disorder. It addresses the challenges of high-dimensional, sparse, noisy, and redundant input variables in electronic health record-based predictive modeling.

title: Unscented KalmanNet: a hybrid deep learning filter with calibrated posterior covariance for nonlinear state estimation
summary: This paper introduces Unscented KalmanNet, a hybrid deep learning filter with calibrated posterior covariance for nonlinear state estimation. It aims to improve upon the traditional Unscented Kalman filter by handling unknown and time-varying noise statistics.

title: From Non-Convex Self-Concordant Regularization to Scalable Quasi-Newton Training of PINNs
summary: This research explores scalable quasi-Newton training methods for Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) using non-convex self-concordant regularization. It addresses the challenges of indefinite and poorly scaled local curvature in PINN residual objectives for high-accuracy solutions.

title: Attention-Only White-Box Transformer via LeJEPA-Based Self-Supervised Pretraining
summary: This work proposes an Attention-Only White-Box Transformer through LeJEPA-Based Self-Supervised Pretraining. It re-examines the derivation of white-box networks and self-supervised learning paradigms from a joint perspective.

title: Random features for Grassmannian kernel approximation with bounded rank-one projections
summary: This paper proposes a family of random feature maps for scalable kernel machines on low-dimensional subspaces, specifically the Grassmannian manifold. These representations are useful when data classes are well described by the span of a few samples.

title: Transferable Dual-Stream Representations for Mesoscale-Preserving Sea Surface Temperature Downscaling
summary: This research focuses on transferable dual-stream representations for mesoscale-preserving sea surface temperature downscaling using deep learning models. It aims to generate numerically plausible and physically meaningful outputs, unlike methods that produce overly smooth results.

title: Geometry-Informed Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Pre-trained Molecular GNNs for Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability Prediction
summary: This study proposes Geometry-Informed Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of pre-trained molecular Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability (BBBP) prediction. This is a critical screening task in central nervous system drug discovery, despite its current challenges.

title: Real-time probabilistic tsunami forecasting via generative AI
summary: This research utilizes generative AI for real-time probabilistic tsunami forecasting to enhance public risk awareness by providing more nuanced predictions under uncertain conditions.

title: Cost-Aware Multi-Objective Bandits: Theory and Application to Budgeted LLM Configuration Evaluation
summary: This paper formulates LLM configuration evaluation as a cost-aware multi-objective bandit problem to address challenges posed by limited budgets, varying costs, and competing objectives.

title: ATLAS: Adaptive Topological Learning with Abstract Successors for Continual Learning
summary: This paper introduces ATLAS, an adaptive topological learning method with abstract successors, aimed at improving sample efficiency and robustness for continual reinforcement learning when environments change.

title: Looking in the Mirror: Introspecting Side-Effect Misalignments Induced by Fine-Tuning
summary: This research investigates how fine-tuning large language models can induce side-effect misalignments, degrading original alignment properties while acquiring new capabilities.

title: Manipulation-Proof Oblivious Audits against Deceptive Model Providers
summary: This paper proposes manipulation-proof oblivious audits as a mechanism to ensure the integrity of machine learning model assessments, especially in regulatory contexts against deceptive model providers.

title: EvtGraph: Event-Adaptive Compression for Sparse Temporal Graph Learning in Multimodal Time Series
summary: EvtGraph is a proposed unified framework for event-adaptive compression in sparse temporal graph learning, designed to handle irregular and information-dense multimodal time series efficiently.

title: Towards Trustworthy Hypergraph Neural Networks under Label Noise
summary: This research aims to improve the trustworthiness of Hypergraph Neural Networks (HGNNs) by enhancing their robustness and performance when dealing with noisy labeled data.

title: NodeJEPA: Structure-Conditioned Latent Prediction for Node-Level Graph Self-Supervised Learning
summary: NodeJEPA introduces a novel self-supervised learning method for graphs using structure-conditioned latent prediction, designed to produce representations less dependent on low-level input statistics.

title: Non-asymptotic implicit bias of logistic regression at early-stage gradient descent dynamics
summary: This paper investigates the non-asymptotic implicit bias of logistic regression during early-stage gradient descent dynamics, exploring how this bias prevents overfitting to spurious patterns.

title: NeuroPB: Scaling Neural Decoding with Pretrained Behavioral Representations
summary: NeuroPB proposes scaling neural decoding for brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) by leveraging pretrained behavioral representations, overcoming limitations in the scale and heterogeneity of neural recordings.

title: When Proxy Prediction Becomes Equation Reconstruction: Diagnostics and Residual Learning for Factor-Derived Proxy Supervision
summary: This research examines instances in scientific machine learning where proxy prediction may amount to reconstructing the proxy-generating equation, proposing diagnostics and residual learning to address this.

title: Elbow-Based MoE Routing: A Training-Free Inference Time Plugin for Expert Selection
summary: This paper introduces Elbow-Based MoE Routing, a training-free inference-time plugin that dynamically selects experts in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models based on relevance rather than a fixed top-k.

title: Training-Free Hashing-Based Attention via Binary Principal Components
summary: This paper proposes a training-free hashing-based attention mechanism using binary principal components to address the efficiency bottleneck of self-attention in long-context large language models (LLMs).

title: MESH: Memory-Efficient Sinkhorn Optimization for Mixture-of-Experts Training
summary: MESH is a proposed memory-efficient Sinkhorn optimization method designed to improve the training stability and efficiency of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models by addressing direct application limitations.

title: Not Every Divergence Should Be Suppressed: Counterfactual Recoverability in On-Policy Distillation
summary: This research explores counterfactual recoverability in on-policy distillation, arguing that not every divergence should be suppressed and proposing to determine when an erroneous prefix is correctable.

title: Generative Optimization for Incentivized Advertising with Global Level Constraints
summary: This paper proposes a generative optimization framework for incentivized advertising, aiming to efficiently allocate rewards and maximize user engagement under global constraints despite complex user dynamics.

title: Robustness Emerges Early in Training Dynamics, but Is Not Preserved
summary: This research identifies a 'robustness fading phenomenon' where deep neural networks initially develop robust representations during early training, but these properties are not preserved throughout the process.

title: Tropical Algebraic Geometry for Neuronal Representations: An Arakelov-Green Measure Based Descriptor for Graph Learning
summary: This paper introduces a descriptor for graph learning in neuronal representations, based on Tropical Algebraic Geometry, to better capture both graph topology and spatial geometry in 3D neuronal morphologies.

title: Local Violation Certification for Linear Predict-Then-Optimize Pipelines
summary: This paper proposes a method for local violation certification in linear predict-then-optimize pipelines, aiming to ensure the safety, fairness, and reliability of high-stakes operational decisions.

title: A Model Merging Approach for Continual MLLM Unlearning
summary: This paper introduces a model merging approach for continual unlearning in multimodal large language models (MLLMs), addressing the challenge of removing private or sensitive information in ongoing scenarios.

title: Why Ranking Anomaly Detection Algorithms Isn't as Reliable as You May Think
summary: This paper discusses the challenges in reliably ranking anomaly detection algorithms, noting that many novel methods claim state-of-the-art performance despite difficulties in consistent evaluation. It highlights issues with measuring and comparing the effectiveness of these algorithms.

title: Transfer Learning for Named Entity Recognition of Classical Latin through LLM Prompting
summary: This paper describes a system developed by Team uOttawa that uses transfer learning and LLM prompting for Named Entity Recognition in Classical Latin. The work contributes to ancient language research and is part of the EvaLatin 2026 evaluation campaign.

title: When More Becomes Less: Position-Dependent Repetition Effects in Language Models
summary: This research investigates how the repetition of target tokens affects prediction in language models, demonstrating that the impact is position-dependent and not uniform across readout slots. It introduces a two-probe design to study these effects.

title: Learning Sexism Detection Using Multi-Agent Perspectivist Preference Optimization
summary: This paper proposes a Multi-Agent Perspectivist Preference Optimization (MAP-PO) framework to address human disagreement in sexism detection labeling. It aims to develop NLP systems that capture differing perceptions of sexism rather than relying on majority votes.

title: Mind the Cap: Output-Budget Regimes Change the Measured Multilingual Reasoning Gap
summary: This research investigates how a fixed output-token cap in multilingual evaluations can skew the measured reasoning gap between native and translated languages. It argues that this cap acts as a hidden experimental variable affecting benchmark results, specifically on MGSM.

title: Visualizing Graph-to-Answer Mechanism Recovery in Materials-Science Hypothesis Generation
summary: This case study focuses on visualizing how AI co-scientists, using a Qwen3-8B model adapted for materials science, generate hypotheses and recover scientifically meaningful mechanisms. It aims to demonstrate that fluent AI output also preserves scientific validity.

title: Test, then Route: How Language Models Execute In-Context Conditional Rules Across Models and Languages
summary: This research investigates how language models execute in-context conditional rules, probing whether they form a "runtime circuit" with distinct test and routing modules. The study uses activation patching with a four-donor design to analyze this behavior.

title: Large Language Models for Low-Resource Languages: A Conceptual Framework for an Electronic Explanatory Dictionary of the Tajik Language
summary: This paper outlines a conceptual framework for developing an electronic explanatory dictionary for the low-resource Tajik language, utilizing large language models. The work addresses the absence of a comprehensive digital lexicographic resource for Tajik.

title: Patients-like-me: A Variational LM--GNN Framework for Explainable Clinical Prediction
summary: This research proposes a variational framework that combines language models and graph neural networks for explainable clinical prediction using electronic health records. The framework leverages LMs for textual representations and GNNs for incorporating inter-patient relationships and enhancing explainability.

title: Hallucinations on the Board: Tool-Augmented Evaluation of LLM Chess Commentary
summary: This paper investigates the use of large language models for generating chess commentary and proposes a tool-augmented evaluation method to assess their hallucinations. It compares LLM outputs against expert-level evaluations from superhuman game engines.

title: Towards End-to-End Multilingual Metaphor Processing: Integrating Detection, Translation, and Evaluation
summary: This research addresses the challenges of multilingual metaphor processing by proposing an integrated approach that combines detection, translation, and evaluation. It highlights that successful interpretation and translation of metaphorical language require reasoning beyond literal lexical meaning.

title: The Fairness Collapse Phenomenon: Bias Amplification in Language Models Trained on Synthetic Data
summary: This paper introduces the concept of "fairness collapse," where bias is amplified in language models trained on synthetic data, akin to model collapse. This phenomenon raises significant concerns regarding the use of open data in training AI systems.

title: Eliciting Intrinsic Hallucinations in LLMs via Semantically Equivalent Adversarial Attacks
summary: This research presents a method for eliciting "intrinsic hallucinations" in large language models, even when using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). It achieves this by employing semantically equivalent adversarial attacks to expose vulnerabilities in the models.

title: Searching for Sound-Meaning Collisions: Graph-Based Affordance Retrieval and Multi-Evaluator Ranking for Pun Translation at CLEF 2026 JOKER Task 2
summary: This paper explores a computational approach to pun translation by modeling it as a discovery and exploration process. It proposes using graph-based affordance retrieval and multi-evaluator ranking to find sound-meaning collisions for translating wordplay, participating in CLEF 2026 JOKER Task 2.

title: MIDAS: Multi-LLM Iterative Data-Adaptive Summarization
summary: This paper introduces MIDAS, a Multi-LLM Iterative Data-Adaptive Summarization method that orchestrates multiple large language models for text summarization. MIDAS aims to ensure strict adherence to domain-specific guidelines, output formats, and organizational conventions for enterprise summarization tasks.

title: Pun Intended: Multi-Agent Translation of Wordplay with Contrastive Learning and Phonetic-Semantic Embeddings
summary: This research explores three multi-agent approaches for translating puns from English to French, combining large language models with linguistic constraints. The methods utilize contrastive learning and phonetic-semantic embeddings to handle wordplay.

title: DataRx: Missingness-Aware Sampling for Safer Large Language Model Task-Specific Fine-Tuning
summary: This paper reveals that task-specific fine-tuning can weaken the safety guardrails of aligned large language models. It proposes "Missingness-Aware Sampling" as a strategy to preserve safety during the fine-tuning process.

title: Right Reset: Chunking by Prefix Removal
summary: This paper introduces "Right Reset" (RR), a new probing technique that analyzes causal language models by removing their left context. This method reveals processing boundaries where subsequent tokens are handled with minimal change, thereby measuring the preservation of the right-hand context.

title: Equitable System-Prompt Selection via Constrained Mixed-Strategy GroupDRO
summary: This research addresses the problem of large language models providing varied quality answers to semantically equivalent questions. It proposes a method for equitable system-prompt selection using Constrained Mixed-Strategy GroupDRO to ensure more consistent and fair responses.

title: The Calibration Floor: Format Repair Can Masquerade as Self-Correction at Small-to-Mid Scale
summary: This paper shows that accuracy changes in language model self-revision are often due to format repair, not improved reasoning, testing this phenomenon across various LLMs.

title: FinReportBench: Measuring and Improving Institution-Grade Financial Report Generation
summary: This paper introduces FinReportBench, an expert-grounded benchmark designed to measure and improve the generation of institution-grade financial reports by large language models.

title: EdgeLM: Edge Demonstrations for Language Models' Table Understanding
summary: This paper proposes EdgeLM, a method to improve large language models' table understanding by selecting 'edge demonstrations' for in-context learning, rather than just similar ones.

title: Social Pressure Breaks Majority Voting in LLM Safety Panels
summary: This study demonstrates that misleading context can cause majority voting in LLM safety panels to fail, impacting their ability to detect unsafe content.

title: MERaLiON-GR: Speech Gender Recognition Model for English and SEA Languages
summary: MERaLiON-GR is presented as a new speech gender recognition model capable of binary classification (female/male) for English and Southeast Asian languages, based on finetuning MERaLiON-SpeechEncoder-2.

title: D$^2$F-ReAG: Dynamic Decomposition and Filtering for Multi-Hop Reasoning-Augmented Generation
summary: This paper introduces D$^2$F-ReAG, a method that uses dynamic decomposition and filtering to enhance Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for multi-hop reasoning, addressing LLMs' reliance on static internal knowledge.

title: The Evaluator Is Part of the Experiment: Measuring Open-Ended LLM Conformity
summary: This paper introduces a new experimental protocol for measuring open-ended LLM conformity, acknowledging that the evaluator's judgment is an integral part of the assessment process.

title: Energy- and Memory-Efficient PEFT Methods for Personalized On-Device SLMs on Consumer GPUs
summary: This research explores energy- and memory-efficient Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) methods for personalizing Small Language Models (SLMs) on resource-constrained consumer GPUs for on-device deployment.

title: K-EXAONE 2.0 Technical Report
summary: This technical report introduces K-EXAONE 2.0, an open-weight multilingual foundation model developed by LG AI Research, which expands upon its predecessor's architecture.

title: RESPClinBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Clinical Decision-Making and Longitudinal Disease Management in Respiratory Specialty Care
summary: This paper introduces RESPClinBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal clinical decision-making and longitudinal disease management capabilities of AI in respiratory specialty care.

title: ODRA: Synthesizing Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Sessions with Structured Chain-Of-Thought and Dynamic Patient Resistance
summary: This paper introduces ODRA, a method for synthesizing Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) sessions that adheres to therapeutic structure while modeling dynamic patient resistance using structured chain-of-thought.

title: EuroExec: Frontier Language Models Fall Short of Expert Judgment on European Executive Decision Tasks
summary: This paper introduces EuroExec, a new human-expert-evaluated benchmark used to assess the performance of frontier LLMs on complex European Executive Decision Tasks.

title: Relational Response Fields: A General Theory of Black-Box LLM Response Consistency and Recovery
summary: This paper proposes 'Relational Response Fields,' a general theory for understanding black-box LLM response consistency and recoverability to address reliability challenges.

title: Representing Visual Evidence for Item Difficulty Prediction: Visual Textualization and Image-Native Modeling
summary: This research investigates methods, including visual textualization and image-native modeling, for representing visual evidence to predict the difficulty of educational assessment items.

title: STRIVE: Probing Reasoning Limits in Graded Plausibility Generation and Evaluation
summary: This paper introduces STRIVE, a method designed to probe the reasoning limits of AI models in generating and evaluating graded plausibility for event knowledge.

title: Relevant but Incomplete: Referential Dangling as a Paradigm-Level Failure Mode in Hard Prompt Compression
summary: This paper identifies 'Referential Dangling' as a structural failure in hard prompt compression techniques, where independent selection can split dependent evidence pairs, leading to incomplete context.

title: The Personalization Mirage: How LLMs Fabricate User Profiles, and Why Self-Monitoring Misleads
summary: This study examines 'over-inference' in personalized LLMs with persistent memory, where models fabricate user attributes, introducing MirageBench to evaluate this phenomenon.

title: When Memory Lies: An Empirical Study of Spatial Memory Staleness in VLM Agents
summary: This empirical study investigates 'Spatial Memory Staleness' in memory-augmented VLM agents, exploring how outdated persistent spatial knowledge affects their ability to reconcile memory claims with observations.

title: Causal Evidence Extraction and Triangulation in Crisis Reports using Large Language Models: A ReliefWeb-based Study
summary: This study presents a two-stage LLM pipeline for extracting and triangulating causal evidence from humanitarian crisis reports to facilitate decision-making.

title: Breaking the Curse ofMultilinguality inMany-to-Many Speech-to-Text Translation via a Resource-AwareMixture of Speech Encoders
summary: This paper proposes a resource-aware mixture of speech encoders to overcome the 'curse of multilinguality' in many-to-many speech-to-text translation for multimodal large language models.

title: EASy: Towards Efficient LLM-Based Agentic System
summary: This paper introduces EASy, a framework designed to optimize the execution efficiency of LLM-based agentic systems, which are used for solving complex tasks by coordinating specialized agents. It addresses the challenge of efficiency under practical constraints for agentic systems.

title: When Absence Is Evidence: Evaluating Completeness-Sensitive Negative Reasoning in Large Language Models
summary: This research evaluates large language models' (LLMs) ability to perform completeness-sensitive negative reasoning, specifically when determining if something is absent from a record only when evidence completely covers the query scope. It highlights how LLMs should respond when information is genuinely absent versus merely unknown.

title: Evaluating Theory of Mind in Reasoning Models: Robustness over Reasoning
summary: This paper evaluates the robustness of large language models (LLMs) on Theory of Mind (ToM) tests, examining whether their strong performance indicates true ToM capabilities or limitations in the evaluation methods. It focuses on assessing reasoning-oriented LLMs.

title: Easy to Complete, Hard to Choose: Investigating LLM Performance on the ProverbIT Benchmark
summary: This paper introduces ProverbIT, a new benchmark to investigate large language models' (LLMs) performance on culturally embedded linguistic expressions, specifically proverbs. It aims to understand how LLMs process these nuanced forms of language.

title: Kathleen Writes: Autoregressive Generation and Data Scaling Without Attention
summary: This research explores an attention-free architecture called "Kathleen Writes" that uses a wavetable encoder and multi-scale reverberant state for autoregressive generation. It demonstrates that this architecture, without pretraining, can generate media comparable to strong baselines using limited parameters.

title: IslamicTurathBench: A Multi-Task, Multi-Discipline Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models on the Islamic Scholarly Tradition (turath)
summary: This paper introduces IslamicTurathBench, a multi-task and multi-discipline benchmark designed to evaluate large language models (LLMs) on their understanding and application of the Islamic scholarly tradition. It addresses the need for specialized evaluations in religious and cultural domains.

title: EmpaAva: An Open-source Agentic 3D-Avatar Empathetic Live Chatbot
summary: EmpaAva is introduced as the first open-source, agentic 3D-avatar empathetic chatbot capable of translating empathetic response generation from text into live, face-to-face video-call interactions. It allows users to converse with a 3D digital human that responds empathetically.

title: Caching for the Future: Scrub Jay Episodic Memory Principles for Agent Memory Systems
summary: This research proposes applying "Scrub Jay Episodic Memory Principles" to agent memory systems to manage the varying validity of stored memories across sessions. It aims to prevent contamination of retrieved context with outdated facts by treating memory persistence based on content type.

title: InsightEmb: Learning Action-Intent Embeddings for Agentic Insight Retrieval
summary: This paper introduces InsightEmb, a method for learning action-intent embeddings to facilitate agentic insight retrieval, allowing self-improving agents to efficiently recall reusable insights from past experiences. This improves an agent's ability to progress towards its goal by retrieving relevant information at each decision step.

title: Guideline-as-Oracle: Zero-Annotation Training of an Ophthalmic Telephone Triage Agent
summary: This paper introduces "Guideline-as-Oracle (GAO)," a zero-annotation method for training a multi-turn ophthalmic telephone triage agent by compiling American Academy of Ophthalmology guidance into an operational rule table. This approach aims to overcome the difficulties of scaling supervision for medical agents due to annotation costs and privacy.

title: A Modular Part-of-Speech Tagger for Scottish Gaelic using spaCy
summary: This research presents a modular Part-of-Speech (PoS) tagger for Scottish Gaelic developed using spaCy, addressing the challenge of natural language processing for morphologically rich, low-resource languages. It aims to improve digital resources for endangered languages like Scottish Gaelic.

title: Skill-Use: Can LLMs Actually Use Skills in Agentic Harnesses?
summary: This paper investigates whether large language model (LLM) agents can effectively use "skills," which are structured documents specifying actions and tools, within agentic harnesses. It aims to evaluate the practical utility of skills in LLM agent performance beyond just task success.

title: Do Language Models Know Their Slang? Queer Slang Understanding in User-Generated Content
summary: This research introduces Slang-Q, a new manually curated dataset designed to evaluate language models' understanding of queer slang within user-generated English content. It addresses the underrepresentation of culturally specific linguistic expressions in Natural Language Processing research.

title: A-SR: Self-Evolving Agentic LLMs for Symbolic Regression via Hierarchical Coordination
summary: This paper proposes A-SR, a self-evolving agentic framework for symbolic regression that uses hierarchical coordination among large language models (LLMs) to discover closed-form equations from data. It aims to improve upon existing LLM-guided methods by addressing heterogeneous search failures more effectively.

title: Evaluation Pitfalls and Sparsity Limitations in LLM-based Confidence Estimates for Classification
summary: This research examines evaluation pitfalls and sparsity limitations in large language model (LLM)-based confidence estimates for classification tasks, highlighting issues such as extremely sparse outputs from common approaches like verbalization. It critiques current methods for indicating when LLM predictions can be trusted.

title: Strengthening Target-Language Features: SAE-Based Steering for Multilingual Inference
summary: This paper proposes an inference-time multilingual steering method using sparse autoencoders (SAE) to strengthen target-language features in multilingual large language models. This technique aims to improve performance across languages without requiring parameter updates or extensive multilingual training data.

title: Does Out-of-Sight Equal Out-of-Mind in CoT Monitorability?
summary: This research investigates the monitorability of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning in large language models (LLMs), particularly examining whether "latent CoT approaches" obscure the decision-making process. It evaluates how transparent LLM reasoning remains when explicit tokens are replaced with internal representations.

title: State2State: Environment-Derived Mid-Training for LLM Agents
summary: This paper introduces "State2State," a new method for training LLM agents that relies on environment-derived mid-training instead of solely supervised fine-tuning or online reinforcement learning. This approach aims to address the scalability bottlenecks of externally specified tasks and supervision signals.

title: Advancing Utility Pole and Sign Detection Through Deep Learning
summary: This research presents a deep learning framework for the automated detection of utility poles and signs, aiming to improve the efficiency and safety of infrastructure inspection. This application of AI is crucial for maintaining power distribution systems and public services.

title: LoRetta: A Foundation Model and Extensive Dataset for Global-Scale Remote Sensing Dense Image Matching
summary: LoRetta is introduced as a new foundation model and extensive dataset designed for global-scale remote sensing dense image matching. It addresses the challenges of matching images with variations in acquisition time, season, viewpoint, and spatial resolution for applications in computer vision and photogrammetry.

title: Perception Before Reasoning: Dynamic Latent Reasoning for Video Understanding and Question Answering
summary: This paper introduces a method for video question answering that uses dynamic latent reasoning to ground language queries in visual evidence, aiming to answer questions efficiently without relying on long textual rationales for simple cases.

title: Teaching Foundation Models to Read mmWave: Pose-Guided Kinematic Representation for Human Behavior Understanding
summary: This research proposes a pose-guided kinematic representation to help large language models interpret millimeter-wave radar data for human behavior understanding, addressing challenges in aligning privacy-friendly radar observations with language.

title: Radar4D-VLM: Proposal-Grounded Temporal 4D Radar Reasoning Across Frozen Language Models
summary: This paper introduces Radar4D-VLM, a radar-only temporal vision-language model designed for autonomous driving, which leverages 4D radar as a standalone perceptual modality to enhance robustness in adverse visibility.

title: RUTA: Principled Visual Token Allocation via Rate-Utility Optimization
summary: This research introduces RUTA, a method for principled visual token allocation that uses rate-utility optimization to efficiently manage high-resolution images and long videos in vision-language models, reducing computational and memory costs.

title: TRNet: Topography-Guided Frequency Rectification and Structure-Aware Decoding for Multimodal Paddy Rice Segmentation
summary: This paper presents TRNet, a multi-modal deep learning model designed for segmenting paddy rice from very-high-resolution satellite imagery, which integrates topography-guided frequency rectification and structure-aware decoding to address challenges in mountainous regions.

title: TriCLE: Tri-Modal Vision-Language Reasoning for Edge-Deployed Fine-Grained Clustering
summary: This research introduces TriCLE, a system for tri-modal vision-language reasoning designed for edge-deployed fine-grained clustering in aerial observation, addressing the challenges of limited memory, compute, and connectivity.

title: PADFormer: Pose-agnostic Anomaly Detection from Sparse View Images
summary: This paper proposes PADFormer, a novel method for pose-agnostic anomaly detection from sparse view images, which aims to handle significant pose variations more efficiently than complex 3D reconstruction approaches.

title: OmniVR: Joint Video-Audio Conditional Generation for Restoring Degraded Historical Films
summary: This paper presents OmniVR, the first joint audio-video generative restoration model designed to restore degraded historical films by addressing co-occurring visual and audio degradations simultaneously.

title: SIGNPOST-Bench: Benchmarking Text-Vision Conflict Resolution in Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces SIGNPOST-Bench, a new controlled counterfactual benchmark designed to evaluate how multimodal large language models resolve conflicts between visual and textual cues when making grounded predictions.

title: Binding Biometrics with AI Agent Identifiers for Delegation of Authority
summary: This paper explores binding biometrics with AI agent identifiers to address accountability and authorization in agentic AI systems, ensuring human operator authorization for critical tasks.

title: CLIP-CC-Bench: Evaluating Paragraph-Level Video Descriptions in Video-Language Models
summary: This paper introduces CLIP-CC-Bench, an evaluation suite designed to benchmark video-language models on their ability to generate accurate, long-form, paragraph-level video descriptions, moving beyond short clips and single-sentence metrics.

title: iStructTab: Structured Feature Sequencing for Multimodal Learning of Image and Tabular Data
summary: This research introduces iStructTab, which uses Graph-Enhanced Descriptor Sequencing (GEDS) as a structured feature sequencing algorithm to improve multimodal learning by addressing representation issues when combining image and tabular data.

title: Image Classification Using CNN-QNN Hybrid Model with Optimized Correlated Features
summary: This paper proposes a method for image classification using a hybrid CNN-QNN model, enhancing accuracy by optimizing the correlation among convolutional neural network features used as inputs to the quantum neural network.

title: ReGround: Restoring Visual Grounding in Multi-Step Reasoning through Self-Diagnosis and Visual Re-Examination
summary: This paper introduces ReGround, a method to restore visual grounding in Vision-Language Models during multi-step reasoning by enabling self-diagnosis and visual re-examination, addressing the issue of reliance on language priors over image evidence.

title: Free-Lunch Augmentation by Revisiting Diffusion-Based Data Generation for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Object Detection
summary: This research explores using diffusion-based data generation for "free-lunch" data augmentation to improve Cross-Domain Few-Shot Object Detection, specifically addressing challenges posed by domain gaps and data scarcity.

title: CofactVLA: Deconfounding Vision-Language-Action Models via Counterfactual Intervention
summary: This paper introduces CofactVLA, a method that uses counterfactual intervention to deconfound Vision-Language-Action models, addressing the "vision-override" phenomenon that hinders robotic manipulation.

title: Faster-WAM: Efficient Inference-Time Future Conditioning for Robust World Action Models
summary: This paper introduces Faster-WAM, a method to achieve efficient inference-time future conditioning for robust World Action Models, aiming to improve robot manipulation without incurring prohibitive computational costs.

title: Foreseeing the Invisible: Amodal Reconstruction of Leaf Fossil Images
summary: This paper presents AmodalDINO, a multi-head dense-prediction model that performs amodal reconstruction to recover missing tissue and complete the shape of degraded leaf fossils, aiding paleobotanical studies.

title: Predict, Then Retrieve: Cross-Instance Future-State Retrieval from Video Prefixes
summary: This paper introduces Predictive State Retrieval (PSR), a new task where a model observes a video prefix and a temporal question to retrieve instances from other videos or images that depict an object's predicted future state.

title: UBLLIE: Unified Backlight and Low-Light Image Enhancement
summary: This paper proposes UBLLIE, a unified and unsupervised enhancement framework designed to address both backlight and low-light images by correcting severe exposure imbalance or global underexposure.

title: OmniRouting: A Semantic-Coupled Multimodal Benchmark for Constraint-Aware Spatial Reasoning in PCB Routing
summary: This paper introduces OmniRouting, a multimodal benchmark designed to evaluate large language models' capabilities in constraint-aware spatial reasoning for PCB routing problems. It assesses their ability to handle complex geometric, topological, and electrical constraints.

title: ToolArtist: Tool-Using Unified Multimodal Models for Agentic Image Generation
summary: ToolArtist proposes a framework for unified multimodal models that leverage tool-using and agentic capabilities for complex image generation tasks. It aims to overcome limitations of text-to-image models in semantic understanding and multi-step reasoning by integrating external knowledge.

title: Season: Spectrum-Aware Orthogonal Gradient Refinement for Transfer-Based Adversarial Attacks
summary: Season introduces a spectrum-aware orthogonal gradient refinement framework to improve transfer-based adversarial attacks against Vision Transformers and CNNs. The method addresses the poor transferability of attacks between heterogeneous architectures.

title: When does training on downscaled images yield the same gradients?
summary: This research investigates when training diffusion transformers on downscaled images can yield similar gradients as training on full-resolution images. It explores the relationship between resolution, noise, and signal preservation in diffusion models.

title: Q-CueGraph: Query-Conditioned Visual Evidence Graphs for Multimodal Reasoning
summary: Q-CueGraph proposes a method for multimodal large language models to explicitly decide where to inspect an image based on a query, using visual evidence graphs. This improves task-conditioned policy for image inspection, moving beyond simple crop or zoom tools.

title: TwinIR: Coordinated Invisible Dual-Point Attacks on Online HD Map Construction
summary: TwinIR introduces a method for coordinated invisible dual-point physical attacks targeting online HD map construction systems used in autonomous driving. It identifies limitations in existing attack methods due to cross-boundary compensation effects.

title: Beyond Global Routing Aggregation: Phase-Aware Expert Merging for MoE Vision-Language Models
summary: This paper proposes Phase-Aware Expert Merging to optimize Mixture-of-Experts Vision-Language Models by reducing their storage burden through efficient expert aggregation. It focuses on improving the efficiency of MoE-VLMs without full expert pool storage.

title: EndoVLM: An Endoscopy Vision-Language Pre-training Model via Anatomy-Guided Sparsity and Progressive Alignment
summary: EndoVLM is an endoscopy vision-language pre-training model designed to advance endoscopic image analysis by leveraging rich semantic knowledge from clinical reports. It incorporates anatomy-guided sparsity and progressive alignment for more effective learning.

title: REZE: Recognition-Based Zero-Shot Extraction for Video Temporal Grounding
summary: REZE introduces a recognition-based zero-shot extraction method for video temporal grounding, addressing limitations of direct timestamp generation by VLMs. This approach improves the accuracy of identifying video intervals corresponding to natural-language queries.

title: Not All Redundant Tokens Are Alike: Analyzing Visual Token Pruning through Token Roles
summary: This research analyzes visual token pruning methods in Vision-Language Models by examining the roles of different tokens during pruning. It aims to understand how pruning decisions impact the computational efficiency and performance of VLMs.

title: DIVE: Dynamic Iterative Visual Evidence Construction for Efficient Vision-Language Models
summary: DIVE proposes a method for efficient vision-language models by dynamically constructing visual evidence and iteratively pruning low-scoring tokens. This addresses the computational bottleneck caused by long visual token sequences in VLMs.

title: GeoReward: Mitigating Contextual Variable Overestimation in Vision-Language Models for Cross-Market Preference Prediction
summary: GeoReward introduces a method to mitigate Contextual Variable Overestimation in Vision-Language Models when used for cross-market preference prediction. It aims to prevent VLMs from overestimating dominant visual-textual cues at the expense of critical sparse contextual variables.

title: CARVE: Cross-Slice Anisotropic Reallocation of Visual Evidence for Efficient 3D Medical Volume Understanding
summary: CARVE proposes a method for Cross-Slice Anisotropic Reallocation of Visual Evidence to improve the efficiency of slice-based MLLMs for 3D medical volume understanding. It aims to reduce the burden of thousands of visual tokens by optimizing how evidence is captured across adjacent slices.

title: Coupled Continuous-Discrete Generation for Scene Text Image Super-Resolution
summary: This paper introduces a coupled continuous-discrete generation approach for Scene Text Image Super-Resolution (STISR). The method aims to recover visually plausible appearance and preserve character semantics from degraded inputs, addressing issues of error propagation in existing systems.

title: FocusMem: Factorizing Content, Readout, and Trust in Latent GUI Memory
summary: FocusMem proposes a method for factorizing content, readout, and trust in latent GUI memory for AI agents. It offers a compact solution for agents to remember useful experiences and unfinished progress by compressing multimodal trajectories into continuous tokens.

title: EgoAfford: Task-Oriented Affordance Grounding via Egocentric Referring Segmentation
summary: EgoAfford presents a method for task-oriented affordance grounding using egocentric referring segmentation. It aims to connect the semantic roles of objects with task-state-aligned visual observations for complex, multi-step planning in AI systems.

title: VoxStruct3D: Structure-Leading Flow Matching for Voxel-Space 3D MRI Synthesis
summary: VoxStruct3D introduces a structure-leading flow matching approach for voxel-space 3D MRI synthesis. This method aims to generate high-fidelity 3D MRI images with both globally coherent anatomy and fine-grained voxel-level detail, overcoming limitations of latent diffusion.

title: ColorFD: A Finite-Difference Guided Black-Box Physical Adversarial Attack for Remote Sensing Object Detection
summary: ColorFD proposes a finite-difference guided black-box physical adversarial attack method targeting remote sensing object detectors. It addresses the underexplored area of physical attacks in real-world scenarios, which are often overlooked compared to digital attacks.

title: OutLangSplat: 3D Language Gaussian Splatting for UAV Outdoor Scenes
summary: OutLangSplat introduces a 3D Language Gaussian Splatting method for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) outdoor scenes, embedding open-vocabulary language features for efficient 3D scene understanding. It aims to overcome limitations of existing methods in large-scale outdoor environments.

title: Talk2Sensors: 3D Visual Grounding in Autonomous Driving via Sensor-Adaptive Physical Cue Matching
summary: Talk2Sensors proposes a method for 3D visual grounding in autonomous driving by using sensor-adaptive physical cue matching. It aims to improve embodied intelligence in real-world outdoor perception by effectively utilizing heterogeneous sensor inputs.

title: PhysMind: From Video to Executable Worlds for Training-Free Physical Reasoning
summary: Introduces PhysMind, a framework that enables training-free physical reasoning from video by interpreting object dynamics and predicting future or counterfactual outcomes, addressing limitations in existing VLM interpretations.

title: MetaVideoAgent: Automated Video-Agent Evolution for Long-Form Video Understanding
summary: Presents MetaVideoAgent, an automated system for evolving video-agent designs to efficiently understand long-form, multimodal videos by locating sparse, question-relevant evidence and adapting to diverse content structures.

title: The First EgoCross Challenge at EgoVis 2026: Cross-Domain Egocentric Video Question Answering
summary: Describes the EgoCross Challenge at EgoVis 2026, a benchmark designed to evaluate how multimodal large language models generalize in cross-domain egocentric video question answering beyond common scenarios.

title: COSMO: Consensus-Driven Shift Modulation for Source-Free Domain Adaptation
summary: Introduces COSMO, a method for source-free domain adaptation that uses consensus-driven shift modulation to adapt source-trained models to unlabeled target domains without source data, mitigating source bias.

title: TRCoRSurg: Temporal-Relational Co-Reasoning for Surgical Video Triplet Recognition
summary: Presents TRCoRSurg, a method that employs temporal-relational co-reasoning for surgical video triplet recognition, aiming to understand complex surgical scenes by recognizing interdependent entities and their relational consistency over time.

title: HiSC: Hierarchical Spatial Clustering Token Compression for Efficient 3D Scene Understanding
summary: Introduces HiSC, a hierarchical spatial clustering token compression method designed to enhance the efficiency of 3D vision-language models by reducing token redundancy in 3D scene understanding, thereby lowering computational costs.

title: DAC-Pose: Dual-Agent Collaborative Framework for Pose-Guided Human Generation
summary: Proposes DAC-Pose, a dual-agent collaborative framework for pose-guided human generation that uses AI agents for complex semantic reasoning to avoid visual artifacts from drastic viewpoint shifts in generative image synthesis.

title: Visual Anchoring in Diffusion: Multimodal Zero-Shot Skeleton Action Recognition
summary: Presenting a method for multimodal zero-shot skeleton action recognition that integrates visual anchoring from diffusion models to provide crucial context from RGB data, enhancing disambiguation of unseen actions with similar skeleton dynamics.

title: DisMix: Order-Aware Mixup for Medical Imaging via Disentangling Ordinal and Non-Ordinal Features
summary: Introduces DisMix, an order-aware mixup data augmentation strategy for medical imaging that disentangles ordinal and non-ordinal features, specifically designed to improve performance in ordinal classification tasks like disease grading.

title: Overcoming Statistical Bias in Action-Controllable World Models
summary: Discusses methods for overcoming statistical bias in action-conditioned world models, aiming to ensure they learn causal relationships for predicting visual environment evolution under agent actions rather than relying on misleading statistical shortcuts.

title: Kitchen Robotic Manipulation utilizing Foundation Models
summary: Presents a modular perception pipeline for kitchen robotic manipulation, utilizing foundation models to enable robots to robustly and adaptably handle diverse tasks, specifically focusing on dishware in household environments.

title: Interpretable Fuzzy Inference for UAV Target Tracking Using Bounding-Box Geometry
summary: Explores an interpretable fuzzy inference method for UAV target tracking, utilizing bounding-box geometry from onboard vision to provide robust continuous yaw estimation for cooperative aerial-ground robotics.

title: SiMDex: Mining Similar Egocentric Videos for Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Manipulation
summary: Presents SiMDex, a similarity-based data mining framework designed to select relevant egocentric human videos to enhance data efficiency and performance for cross-embodiment dexterous robot manipulation during VLA post-training.

title: SAFECAST: Robust Failure Detection for VLA Policies with Contrast-Set Training and Calibration
summary: Introduces SAFECAST, a robust failure detection method for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies that uses contrast-set training and calibration to identify deployment-time distribution shifts and prevent rollout failures.

title: Structured LLM Reasoning for Zero-Shot Human--Robot Coordination Under Hidden Goals
summary: Presents a structured large language model (LLM) architecture for zero-shot human-robot coordination in cooperative tasks with hidden goals, decomposing decision-making based on a Dec-POMDP formulation.

title: Approximate Multi-Objective Search Under Rulebooks
summary: Discusses approximate multi-objective search methods for robotic planning, incorporating 'rulebooks' to formalize complex priority relationships among objectives, which generalizes Pareto and lexicographic dominance.

title: SSC: A Verifiable Structured Representation for Bimanual Manipulation Labelling
summary: Introduces SSC, a verifiable structured representation for bimanual manipulation labeling that decomposes long-horizon demonstrations into semantic subtask segments, improving policy training and evaluation for robotic systems.

title: GUARD: Grounding Uncertainty and Ablation-Based Risk Detection for Diffusion-Based VLAs
summary: Presents GUARD, a test-time failure detection method for diffusion-based vision-language-action (VLA) policies that measures grounding uncertainty using ablation to identify situations where predictions are weakly supported by visual and linguistic evidence.

title: Retrieve in Time, Correct in Frequency
summary: Discusses a method to improve long-horizon manipulation in frozen vision-language-action (VLA) policies by using corrective evidence from successful rollouts and frame retrieval to address accumulated execution errors and visual aliasing.

title: Static Timing Orchestration for Tree-Structured Robot Control Firmware
summary: Describes a static timing orchestration approach for tree-structured robot control firmware, aimed at reducing development complexity and improving maintainability for increasingly complex robotic systems by generating firmware from structural description files.

title: GASP: GPU-Accelerated Safe Planner for Real-Time Collision-Aware Motion Generation with Latent Trajectory Sampling
summary: Introduces GASP, a GPU-accelerated planner for real-time, collision-aware joint-space motion generation in known environments, using B-spline trajectory parameterization and a convolutional neural network.

title: Mind-VLA: Instruction-Aware Spatial Representation Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Presents Mind-VLA, a method for improving Vision-Language-Action models by introducing instruction-aware spatial representation alignment that focuses on specific target objects within 3D scene geometry.

title: Suppression Sticks, Locality Is Fragile: A Closed-Loop Target-and-Control Audit of Task-Vector Negation in VLA Policies
summary: Investigates the behavioral locality of task-vector negation in multitask Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies through a closed-loop robot control audit across various skills.

title: Enabling Urgency-aware Robot Swarm Intralogistics using Smart IoT Tags
summary: Proposes a system for urgency-aware intralogistics using decentralized robot swarms in warehouses, addressing the need to prioritize moving items based on urgency with smart IoT tags.

title: A GitOps-Driven Annotation Catalog for Fully Automatic Railway Operations
summary: Discusses a GitOps-driven annotation catalog designed to support robust AI-based perception systems for fully automatic railway operations (GoA3-GoA4), essential for reliable obstacle detection.

title: Explicit Language Memory for Long-Horizon Planning in Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Proposes integrating explicit language memory into Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to overcome challenges in long-horizon planning and improve cross-task compositional generalization.

title: From Transparent Labware Segmentation to Collision Avoidance: A Real-Time Edge-Aware Perception Pipeline
summary: Presents a real-time edge-aware instance segmentation framework for robots, enabling collision avoidance with challenging transparent laboratory glassware using only visual perception.

title: Deliberate Before You Fly: Vision-Guided Spatial Deliberation for UAV See-and-Reach Navigation
summary: Introduces Vision-Guided Spatial Deliberation for UAV see-and-reach navigation, allowing aerial agents to approach language-specified targets by explicitly modeling fine-grained spatial relationships before acting.

title: PRIMAL3: Pathfinding via Reinforcement and Imitation Multi-Agent Learning - Leveraging LaCAM3
summary: Presents PRIMAL3, an ultra-large-scale learning-based framework for multi-agent pathfinding that integrates reinforcement learning, topology-aware communication, and LaCAM3-guided training.

title: DreamWAM: Beyond RGB Future Prediction for World Action Models
summary: Introduces DreamWAM, an approach that improves World Action Models by moving beyond RGB future prediction to disentangle task-relevant state transitions from nuisance variations in the observed world.

title: BridgeVLA++: A Data-Efficient, Generalizable, and Memory-Augmented Vision-Language-Action Framework for 3D Manipulation
summary: Presents BridgeVLA++, a data-efficient and generalizable Vision-Language-Action framework for 3D robot manipulation, which is memory-augmented to address limitations of existing VLA methods.

title: SpikingNav: Robust Embodied Navigation with Spiking Neural Policies
summary: Introduces SpikingNav, a system for robust embodied navigation that uses energy-efficient Spiking Neural Policies to make sequential decisions from egocentric observations in physical environments.

title: Differential 6-DOF Pose Estimation with Provable First-Order Immunity to Camera Calibration Errors
summary: Presents a method for differential 6-DOF pose estimation that offers provable first-order immunity to camera calibration errors, essential for applications in robotic manipulation and autonomous systems.

title: A Multi-Sensor Dataset for Monitoring the Operational Environment of Rail Vehicles
summary: Presents a multi-sensor dataset designed for monitoring the operational environment of rail vehicles, crucial for the development and reliable operation of AI-powered automated railway systems (GoA2-GoA4).

title: Exact Model-Free Policy Iteration for Co-safe LTL Planning
summary: Studies exact model-free policy iteration for co-safe linear temporal logic planning objectives within finite Markov decision processes, leveraging reinforcement learning.

title: Learning When to Stop: Prefix-Optimal Dynamic Diffusion Policies for Continuous Control
summary: Introduces Prefix-Optimal Dynamic Diffusion Policies for continuous control, a method that adaptively reduces the computational cost of diffusion policies by optimizing the number of denoising steps.

title: AI-based single-shot structured-light depth reconstruction for real-time laparoscopic surgical guidance
summary: Presents an AI-based single-shot structured-light depth reconstruction method for real-time laparoscopic surgical guidance, enhancing depth perception for autonomous and semi-autonomous robotic surgery.

title: Curiosity-Diffuser: Curiosity Guide Diffusion Models for Reliability
summary: Introduces Curiosity-Diffuser, which applies curiosity-guided learning to diffusion models to improve the reliability and reduce hallucinations in imitation policies for robotic intelligence.

title: Gaussian-LIC2: LiDAR-Inertial-Camera Gaussian Splatting SLAM
summary: Presents Gaussian-LIC2, the first photo-realistic LiDAR-Inertial-Camera Gaussian Splatting SLAM system, achieving high visual quality, geometric accuracy, and real-time performance for robust pose estimation.

title: Arnold: A multi-task, multi-embodiment muscle transformer policy
summary: Introduces Arnold, a multi-task, multi-embodiment muscle transformer policy designed for controlling high-dimensional and nonlinear musculoskeletal models of the human body in various skills.

title: RESample: A Robust Data Augmentation Framework via Exploratory Sampling for Robotic Manipulation
summary: This paper introduces RESample, a data augmentation framework for robotic manipulation that uses exploratory sampling to improve training datasets for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models. It addresses the need for corrective supervision in imitation learning datasets for robots.

title: Imitation Learning from Human Motion Alone Does Not Guarantee Biomechanically Plausible Gait Kinetics
summary: This study examines the limitations of motion imitation learning in robotics and human gait modeling, finding that it doesn't guarantee biomechanically plausible gait kinetics without explicit kinetic information. It assesses the ability of motion imitation alone to estimate biological joint moments.

title: SafeLand: Safe Autonomous Landing in Unknown Environments with Bayesian Semantic Mapping
summary: SafeLand proposes a method for safe autonomous landing of uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) in unknown, dynamic environments using Bayesian Semantic Mapping. It addresses safety challenges for UAV operations near people and infrastructure.

title: SACK : Safe Active Continual Koopman Learning for Uncertain Systems with Contractive Guarantees
summary: SACK introduces a Safe Active Continual Koopman Learning method with contractive guarantees for uncertain systems, leveraging Koopman operator theory to represent nonlinear dynamics. It addresses the performance degradation of Koopman models learned from data by ensuring safety and continuous adaptation.

title: Learning Direct Control Policies with Flow Matching for Autonomous Driving
summary: This paper presents a flow-matching planner for autonomous driving that directly generates actionable control trajectories, including acceleration and curvature profiles. The model uses a bird's-eye-view (BEV) raster of the scene to generate control sequences.

title: GenTrack: Physical Alignment for Robot-Native Motion Generation and Zero-Shot Humanoid Tracking
summary: GenTrack proposes a method for physical alignment in robot-native motion generation and zero-shot humanoid tracking to address the gap between kinematic plausibility and real-world execution. It uses text-to-motion generators to provide scalable supervision for humanoid robots.

title: DeepThinkVLA: Enhancing Reasoning Capability of Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: DeepThinkVLA investigates whether Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning genuinely enhances the reasoning capability of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models. The research systematically diagnoses when and why CoT helps robots act, addressing inconsistencies in prior findings.

title: Seeking Physics in Diffusion Noise
summary: This research probes intermediate denoising representations of pretrained Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) to determine if video diffusion models encode signals predictive of physical plausibility. It finds that physically plausible and implausible videos are partially separable in mid-layer feature space.

title: A Systematic Review and Taxonomy of Reinforcement Learning-Model Predictive Control Integration for Linear Systems
summary: This paper provides a systematic review and taxonomy of the integration between Reinforcement Learning (RL) and Model Predictive Control (MPC) for linear systems. It highlights their combined potential for constrained decision-making and adaptive control.

title: DM$^3$-Nav: Decentralized Multi-Agent Multimodal Multi-Object Semantic Navigation
summary: DM$^3$-Nav is a fully decentralized multi-agent semantic navigation system designed for multimodal open-vocabulary goal specification and multi-object missions. It operates without a central coordinator, global map aggregation, or shared common knowledge.

title: TerraZero: Procedural Driving Simulation for Zero-Demonstration Self-Play at Scale
summary: TerraZero is a procedural driving simulation designed for zero-demonstration self-play at scale, aimed at training robust autonomous driving agents. It provides a fast, realistic, and diverse environment for reinforcement learning, covering critical edge cases.

title: AI designs new virus not found in nature
summary: A Stanford-led research team has used generative AI to design a synthetic virus — the first time artificial intelligence has been harnessed to create a organism that has never been seen in nature. Why it matters: What could go wrong? The big picture: It could be the first step toward the nightmare scenario AI experts have already warned about: deadly pathogens that can't be stopped, because they've been created too quickly for our current surveillance systems to stop them. The research could also lead to medical breakthroughs, which is the hope of the research team that conducted the study. "The ability of genome language models to generate entire functional genomes has not been tested," they wrote. Driving the news: Researchers wrote in Science that they used an AI model to design viruses that can infect and kill the microbe E. coli. While that could go a long way toward controlling deadly bacterial infections, the technology could be harnessed to develop more complex forms of life — and even help design biological weapons. The intrigue: The news also throws a new twist into government efforts to regulate high-risk research . The Trump administration has been focused on "gain of function" research on natural pathogens — as has Sen. Rand Paul (R-Ky.), whose committee held Anthony Fauci in contempt Thursday for refusing to answer questions from lawmakers investigating the origins of the COVID-19 pandemic. But the AI work created something entirely new. It goes way beyond just studying how to manipulate natural viruses. Between the lines: Biotechnology is regulated through a patchwork of laws and agencies, with breakthroughs frequently outpacing regulators. The Trump administration last month issued a policy for stopping high-risk research in the life sciences that prohibits federally funded "gain of function" research and calls for enhanced oversight of projects involving harmful biological agents. But that didn't specifically address AI-driven research, which is evolving at breakneck speeds. What they're saying: Johns Hopkins health security experts Thomas Inglesby and Moritz Hanke, writing in the same issue of Science , praised the Stanford team for taking precautions, but said there aren't enough existing guardrails to oversee generative genomics. "The ability to compose viral genomes using generative AI now exists; the governance to safely steer it does not," they wrote .
