title: SkillTrace: Multi-Trace Provenance Auditing for LLM-Agent Skill Reuse
summary: SkillTrace is a new method for multi-trace provenance auditing designed to track and verify the reuse of skills within rapidly growing LLM-agent ecosystems.

title: Otter: A Time-Aware, History-Conditioned Human Chess AI
summary: Otter is a 15.3M-parameter human chess AI that predicts human move selection by modeling play as a time-aware, sequential process, conditioned by an encoder that processes the last 20 moves.

title: SearchAuditor: Auditing and Attributing Failures in Long-Horizon Search Agents
summary: SearchAuditor is a new tool designed for auditing and attributing failures in long-horizon deep search agents, which often produce incorrect answers due to complex reasoning errors propagating through web interactions.

title: PD-GS: Phoneme-Driven 3DGS for Audio-Driven Talking Heads
summary: PD-GS is a new phoneme-driven 3D Gaussian Splatting technique designed to improve accurate lip articulation and prevent "leaky mouth" artifacts in audio-driven talking head rendering.

title: When Privileged Guidance Misaligns: State-Matched Routing and Contextualized Self-Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents
summary: This research explores State-Matched Routing and Contextualized Self-Distillation as methods to improve training for multi-turn agents, addressing issues when privileged guidance misaligns in interactive environments.

title: Small Foundation Models of Human Cognition and Behaviour
summary: This research investigates "Small Foundation Models of Human Cognition and Behaviour," training models from 135M to 14B parameters to understand if they process task structure or rely on statistical shortcuts.

title: Project2Task: Graph-Guided Project-Level Planning for Autonomous Research
summary: Project2Task introduces a graph-guided planning method for autonomous research, enabling AI agents to manage long-horizon projects by breaking them down into multiple bounded tasks.

title: TriQua: Reconciling Granularity and Context in Factuality Evaluation
summary: TriQua is a new evaluation method designed to reconcile granularity and context in LLM factuality assessment, addressing the trade-off between atomic facts and broader statements in the "decompose-then-verify" paradigm.

title: Coherence-Oriented Dream Scene Visualisation
summary: The Dream Scene Visualiser (DSV) system uses a large language model to transform written dream descriptions into a temporal sequence of four panel images, facilitating the communication of dreams.

title: Search2Skill: Skill Distillation Beyond Knowledge Boundaries Via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
summary: Search2Skill is a new method for skill distillation that uses rubric-based reinforcement learning to enable LLM-based agents to acquire and evolve reusable skills beyond their initial knowledge boundaries.

title: LUNAR: Benchmarking Personalized Large Language Models on UNiversal User BehAvioR Logs
summary: LUNAR is introduced as the first benchmark to evaluate cross-domain behavioral personalization in personalized large language models, addressing limitations of existing benchmarks that rely on textual personas or isolated signals.

title: WorldClaw: Agentic 3D Open-World Generation at Scale
summary: WorldClaw is presented as a fully agentic, coarse-to-fine framework designed for generating large-scale, freely explorability 3D worlds from open-ended text input. It aims to address challenges in maintaining spatial coherence and rich local content in generated environments.

title: OrchestraBench: Evaluating Multi-Agent Orchestration Failure Modes, Recovery, and Decomposition Quality
summary: OrchestraBench is introduced to evaluate multi-agent orchestration frameworks, focusing on their failure modes, recovery mechanisms, and decomposition quality, rather than just task accuracy. It aims to diagnose the causes of pipeline failures in agent systems.

title: Agentic self-driving microscopy benchmarks support qualification but do not necessarily generalize to unseen tasks
summary: This paper discusses the limitations of agentic self-driving microscopy benchmarks, stating that while they support qualification, they may not generalize well to unseen tasks. It highlights the nascent state of research into agentic control of physical scientific infrastructure.

title: CASCADE: An Agentic Regulatory Network Framework for Patient-Data-Validated Downstream Perturbation Prediction
summary: CASCADE is an agentic framework that utilizes precomputed regulatory networks exposed via MCP to predict the downstream transcriptional effects of gene perturbation, validated using patient data. This framework aims to improve predictions in the context of cancer gene research.

title: Counterfactual Analysis via Large Language Models
summary: This research paper investigates the application of large language models, specifically GPT-3.5, for performing counterfactual analysis to predict potential outcomes in hypothetical scenarios. The study focuses on its utility for decision-making in areas like online lending.

title: DoctorAgents: an agentic framework to iteratively refine AutoML pipeline for small clinical temporal data
summary: DoctorAgents introduces an agentic framework designed to iteratively refine AutoML pipelines specifically for small clinical temporal data. This aims to improve the development of effective machine learning pipelines for medical decision-making despite data constraints.

title: C$^3$PO: Evaluating Cross-Modal Composition and Counterfactual Performance in Omnimodal Models
summary: C$^3$PO is introduced as a new benchmark with 3,404 samples spanning video, audio, image, and text, designed to evaluate the cross-modal composition and counterfactual performance of omnimodal models (MLLMs). It aims to address issues of brittle cross-modal reasoning in current MLLMs.

title: Adaptive Arena-based Contestable Argumentative Network-of-Experts for Open-Ended Care Plan Coordination
summary: CANOE (Contestable Argumentative Network-of-Experts) is presented as an adaptive, arena-based framework for open-ended care plan coordination, designed to synthesize diverse information across multiple disciplines. It aims to address the limitations of monolithic LLM pipelines in transparent and safe decision-making.

title: Evaluating and Improving Pedagogical Fit in LLM-Based AI Tutors with the Pedagogical Suitability Index
summary: This research focuses on evaluating and improving the pedagogical fit of LLM-based AI tutors by introducing a Pedagogical Suitability Index. The goal is to ensure AI tutor responses are not just correct but also pedagogically appropriate for learners.

title: Negotiating Risk Boundaries in AI for Policing Through Mixed-Stakeholder Deliberation
summary: This paper presents findings from a mixed-stakeholder deliberation workshop focused on negotiating risk boundaries for AI tools used in policing, particularly addressing issues of racial bias. It highlights the importance of including affected communities in decisions about AI adoption.

title: SCP-NL2TL: Selective Conformal Prediction with Semantic Verification for Natural Language to Temporal Logic Specifications
summary: SCP-NL2TL introduces a method for selective conformal prediction with semantic verification, translating natural language instructions into machine-interpretable temporal logic specifications. This enables robots and autonomous systems to plan, reason, and formally verify their behavior more reliably.

title: Recursive Synthesis for Long-Horizon Terminal Tasks
summary: This research proposes a recursive synthesis method to address the high cost and scalability issues of producing high-quality long-horizon training data for terminal agents. The method aims to keep instructions, environment, solutions, and verifiers consistent across tasks.

title: EcoAgent-Bench: Evaluating Economic Decision-Making in Budget-Constrained LLM Agents
summary: EcoAgent-Bench is introduced as a new benchmark for evaluating the economic decision-making capabilities of budget-constrained LLM agents. It focuses on how agents manage resources and make choices among different tools or strategies during task completion.

title: Hyper-ES: Effective Evolution Strategies for LLM Reasoning via Descent Direction Merging
summary: Hyper-ES proposes an effective evolution strategy for improving LLM reasoning by utilizing descent direction merging, addressing the ineffectiveness of directly applying traditional evolution strategies to large language models. This method offers an alternative to gradient-based fine-tuning.

title: SkillTV-Bench: Benchmarking How Well Judges Perform on Skill-Augmented Agentic Execution
summary: SkillTV-Bench is introduced as a new benchmark focused on evaluating the performance of "judges" in assessing skill-augmented agentic execution, particularly for LLM agents performing long-horizon tasks. This shifts evaluation beyond final-response scoring to full execution verification.

title: StepReflect: Structured UI Transition Reflection for Mobile GUI Agents
summary: StepReflect is a proposed method for structured UI transition reflection for autonomous mobile GUI agents, designed to improve reliable long-horizon execution. It addresses the limitations of costly open-ended multimodal reasoning in handling GUI state transitions.

title: Epistemic Trustworthiness in Generative AI: A Normative Framework for Warranted Reliance in High-Stakes Workflows
summary: This paper proposes a normative framework for epistemic trustworthiness in generative AI, addressing the conditions under which reliance on AI outputs is warranted in high-stakes professional workflows. It investigates a central question for responsible AI regarding user beliefs and reasoning.

title: Measuring and Detecting Harmful AI Sycophancy
summary: This paper focuses on measuring and detecting harmful AI sycophancy in large language models, specifically "preference-induced stance reversal sycophancy" (PSRS). It addresses the issue of models altering their stance merely to align with user preferences, highlighting potential negative impacts.

title: SkillHEX: Improving Agent Skills via Hypothesis-Driven Autonomous Exploration and Exploitation
summary: SkillHEX is a method for improving agent skills through hypothesis-driven autonomous exploration and exploitation, enabling on-demand skill evolution for LLM agents. This addresses challenges of manual skill maintenance, such as high costs and scalability issues.

title: Refining Over Resampling: Test-Time Self-Correction for LLM Reasoning
summary: This paper explores test-time self-correction methods to refine Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning, aiming to improve performance by efficiently diversifying answer patterns rather than repetitive sampling.

title: DreamGuard: Efficient Runtime Guardrail for LLM Agents via Risk-Aware World Model
summary: DreamGuard is presented as an efficient runtime guardrail system for Large Language Model (LLM) agents, designed to mitigate risks by checking proposed actions before agents interact with external tools and real-world systems.

title: Shaping Human-AI Interactions to Provide Improvement Pathways and Balance Competing Objectives
summary: This item discusses the dynamics of human-AI interactions, focusing on how individuals form beliefs about AI systems, strategically present information, and receive feedback or decisions, highlighting broader implications for AI deployment.

title: RA-CAD: Learning Post-Execution Critique for State-Aware Text-to-CAD Generation
summary: RA-CAD introduces a method for text-to-CAD generation that translates natural language into parametric CAD codes, utilizing a post-execution critique mechanism to improve design accuracy and reduce manual effort.

title: Unified Agent: Managing Interactions across Devices
summary: This article discusses the need for a Unified Agent capable of managing interactions across multiple user devices, addressing current limitations where AI agent systems struggle with scattered observations and distributed contexts.

title: Subliminal Learning is Non-Semantic Distillation
summary: This research reveals 'Subliminal Learning' as a form of non-semantic distillation in modern language models, where biases or behaviors are transferred from a teacher to a student model via seemingly unrelated synthetic data, posing challenges for AI safety.

title: Activity Frames: Deterministic Screen-Activity Compilation for Agent Memory and Replay
summary: Activity Frames is a deterministic, zero-model pipeline that compiles passively captured screen activity into agent memory, allowing computer-use agents to store and replay user routines instead of re-deriving them.

title: ChainClaw: A Layered Agent Framework for Reliable On-Chain Execution
summary: ChainClaw is introduced as a layered agent framework designed to enable reliable on-chain execution for general-purpose large language model agents, addressing challenges specific to stateful, adversarial, and economically irreversible blockchain environments.

title: When Agentic AI Meets Integrated Sensing and Communication
summary: This item discusses how Agentic Artificial Intelligence is transforming Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) into a goal-driven, closed-loop intelligent system, termed AISAC, moving beyond function-oriented physical-layer technology.

title: When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents
summary: This paper investigates how self-evolving LLM agents can suffer from 'skill contamination,' where new skills degrade performance beyond a critical point, proposing a 'Pre-Commit Gating' mechanism to prevent this.

title: Cautious Context Steering for Language Model Personalization
summary: This paper proposes 'Cautious Context Steering,' a method for personalizing language models to individual user preferences by aligning responses with diverse goals and backgrounds, rather than relying on separate adapters or reward models.

title: ViSR-KGC: Visual Subgraph Reasoning with Vision-Language Models for Multimodal Knowledge Graph Completion
summary: ViSR-KGC is a method for Visual Subgraph Reasoning using Vision-Language Models to achieve Multimodal Knowledge Graph Completion, inferring missing entities or relations from knowledge graphs that include both text and images.

title: Runtime Observability for Heterogeneous Attention Memory
summary: This research proposes a runtime observability contract for heterogeneous attention memory in modern AI models, covering various memory types like KV cache, latent caches, and recurrent states to understand their behavior under compression.

title: Seeing Is Not Deciding: Can Multimodal LLMs Act as Effective CEOs?
summary: This research investigates the capability of Multimodal Large Language Models to act as effective autonomous decision-making agents in executive business scenarios, specifically their ability to perceive and integrate visual business evidence.

title: AppDeltaWorld: Transition-Grounded Delta Code World Model for Mobile GUI Agents
summary: AppDeltaWorld introduces a transition-grounded delta code world model for Mobile GUI Agents, enabling them to operate apps through pixel perception and touch actions while addressing challenges in collecting real trajectories for sensitive applications.

title: MS-MLB: An Open Machine Learning Benchmark for Blood-Based MS Classification
summary: MS-MLB is presented as an open machine learning benchmark designed for the classification of Multiple Sclerosis using blood RNA expression data, aiming to evaluate the potential of blood-based diagnostic tools.

title: When Do Corrective Features Help? An Agent for Corrective Feature Discovery on Black-Box Forecasters
summary: This work explores when corrective features are beneficial, proposing an agent for corrective feature discovery that mines interpretable features to drive a lightweight post-hoc corrector for improving black-box forecasters.

title: PPDL: LLM-Based Flows as Probabilistic Programs
summary: PPDL proposes treating LLM-based flows as probabilistic programs to address the challenge of building reliable applications that leverage large language models, aiming to provide measures of confidence and improve accuracy.

title: Decoupling Perception from Description: Computation-Grounded Representation Alignment between Multivariate Time Series and Language
summary: This research addresses the 'self-supervision trap' in training multimodal models to align time series with language, proposing a computation-grounded representation alignment method to decouple perception from description and improve label quality.

title: Disentangling 3D Modeling from Spatial Reasoning
summary: This research proposes a new paradigm for spatial reasoning by explicitly disentangling 3D perception from reasoning in AI models. It focuses on how modern perception models can effectively estimate 3D information.

title: Marginal Matching Does Not License Factorized Sampling: Auditing Conditional Style Leakage in Factorized Generative Models
summary: This paper audits conditional style leakage in factorized generative models, demonstrating that marginal matching of latent style variables does not guarantee independence from class information. It challenges common interpretations of these models.

title: PRISM: Priority-aware Rubric Internalization via Structured Multimodal Data Synthesis
summary: This research introduces PRISM, a method for priority-aware rubric internalization via structured multimodal data synthesis. It aims to improve multimodal AI models' ability to follow instructions with varying importance levels.

title: Beyond Full-Model Rollback: AuroSFT for Adapter-State Multi-Task Fine-Tuning
summary: This paper introduces AuroSFT for adapter-state multi-task fine-tuning, addressing the challenge of different tasks reaching optimal generalization at different times. It improves the optimization process for heterogeneous data mixtures in AI models.

title: Beyond Rotations: AuroOFT for Expressive Quantized Orthogonal Fine-Tuning
summary: This paper presents AuroOFT, a method for expressive quantized orthogonal fine-tuning that extends parameter-efficient adaptation of low-bit language models. It aims to overcome limitations of linear orthogonal transformations in task-specific updates.

title: An Emerging Retail Portfolio Management Application: Personalized, Tax-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Natural Language Goals
summary: This work presents an application of personalized, tax-aware reinforcement learning with natural language goals for retail portfolio management. It aims to provide individual investors with more sophisticated and personalized financial advice.

title: Evaluating Machine Learning Models for Post-Wildfire Debris-Flow Prediction
summary: This research evaluates machine learning models for predicting post-wildfire debris flows, a critical task for hazard mitigation. It addresses the complexities of identifying reliable models due to overlapping event data.

title: Rectifying Geometric Misalignment: Online Source-Free Adaptation for Class-Imbalanced EEG
summary: This paper proposes an online source-free adaptation method to rectify geometric misalignment for class-imbalanced EEG data in Brain-Computer Interfaces. It aims to improve the generalization of EEG-based BCIs across subjects and sessions.

title: QEvict: Recoverable Quantized KV Eviction for Attention-Drift-Robust Long-Context Decoding
summary: This paper introduces QEvict, a method for recoverable quantized Key-Value (KV) eviction designed to reduce the memory footprint of the KV cache in autoregressive large language models. It enables attention-drift-robust long-context decoding.

title: Quantum-Structured World Models (QSWMs) for Predictive Latent Dynamics
summary: This research introduces Quantum-Structured World Models (QSWMs) as a new paradigm for learning predictive latent dynamics in AI. It explores representing world model states using quantum structures instead of classical methods.

title: IFlowNets: Extending Generative Samplers to Learn Strategies in Incomplete Information Games
summary: This paper introduces IFlowNets, a framework extending generative samplers to learn strategies in incomplete information games. It investigates novel applications of generative sampling by blending reinforcement learning and CFR methods.

title: EvoHarness-RL: Learning Self-Evolving Runtime Harness for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: This research introduces EvoHarness-RL, a method for learning self-evolving runtime harnesses that support long-horizon LLM agents. It addresses challenges in state formation and tool invocation to improve agent performance.

title: Hybrid Probabilistic Zonotopes for Identifiable and Refinable Predictive Uncertainty
summary: This paper introduces Hybrid Probabilistic Zonotopes as a method to provide identifiable and refinable predictive uncertainty in neural networks. It aims to separate distinct sources of uncertainty in prediction tasks.

title: Matrix Zonotopic Attention: A Context-Adaptive Value Projection for Set Transformers
summary: This research introduces Matrix Zonotopic Attention, a context-adaptive value projection mechanism for Set Transformers. It analyzes the asymmetry between input-dependent routing and input-independent value projection in multi-head attention.

title: KV-Skill: Forging Expertise in the Model's Native Language
summary: This paper introduces KV-Skill, a design space for forging expertise within a model's native language by exploring alternative methods for storing task knowledge. It aims to improve modularity and shareability of model capabilities.

title: Align-RAG: Alignment Is All You Need for TSFM In-Context Learning
summary: This paper introduces Align-RAG, a method for retrieval-augmented forecasting that adapts frozen Time Series Foundation Models to new domains using in-context learning. It focuses on alignment for merging retrieved examples without fine-tuning.

title: LC-GRPO: Bridging Train-Inference Gap for Flow-Based GRPO with Langevin Correction
summary: This paper introduces LC-GRPO, a method that bridges the train-inference gap for flow-based Generative Reinforcement Policy Optimization using Langevin Correction. It addresses the discrepancy between deterministic sampling and stochastic rollouts.

title: GAUGE: Granularity-Adaptive Counterfactual Gating of Evidence for Incomplete Multimodal Classification
summary: This research introduces GAUGE, a method for granularity-adaptive counterfactual gating of evidence in incomplete multimodal classification. It aims to improve AI models' ability to handle missing modalities by selectively retaining reliable components.

title: Reasoning Errors Have a Region and a Direction in the Residual-Stream Trajectory of LLMs
summary: This research investigates reasoning errors in Large Language Models (LLMs) by identifying their region and direction within the residual-stream trajectory. It aims to distinguish sound from flawed reasoning by analyzing layerwise displacements.

title: When Does Consensus Mean Correctness? Measuring the Agreement-Accuracy Coupling with Semantics-Preserving Re-Rendering
summary: This paper investigates when model consensus implies correctness by measuring the agreement-accuracy coupling with semantics-preserving re-rendering. It examines the premise that agreement across perturbed inputs reflects true correctness.

title: Consistency Has a Computable Blind Spot: A Commutation Theory of Label-Free Reliability for Vision-Language Figure Reading
summary: This paper identifies a computable blind spot in label-free reliability evaluations for vision-language models, showing that systematic misreadings can persist despite input perturbations.

title: SEAM: Global consistency beyond local accuracy in scientific machine learning
summary: This work introduces SEAM, a method for validating scientific machine learning models that establishes global consistency beyond local accuracy, addressing limitations in current explanation methods.

title: Spectral Aliasing Pretext: A novel task for Self-Supervised fault diagnosis in rotating machinery
summary: Researchers propose Spectral Aliasing Pretext (SAP), a self-supervised learning method that pretrains models on unlabeled vibration data to improve fault diagnosis in rotating machinery.

title: CircuitSteer: Geometrically Aligned Multi-Layer Steering via Sparse Autoencoder Circuits
summary: This paper presents CircuitSteer, a new method for geometrically aligned multi-layer steering in large language models using sparse autoencoder circuits, aimed at controlling LLM behavior for AI alignment.

title: Equipment-centric workpiece localization in near real-time using deep learning-based vision and event-driven finite state machines
summary: This study details an equipment-centric framework using deep learning-based vision and finite state machines for near real-time workpiece localization in challenging industrial environments like hot forging.

title: GROM: Gradient-Free Rapid One-Shot Machine Unlearning
summary: This paper introduces GROM, a gradient-free, rapid, one-shot machine unlearning method designed to efficiently remove specific sensitive knowledge from large language models.

title: Predicting Task Difficulty Without Rollouts
summary: This research explores predicting task difficulty for AI agents directly from task descriptions without requiring costly simulations, enabling better evaluation and environment design.

title: Evidential Rule Learning for Interpretable Classification with Abstention
summary: Researchers introduce Fast Evidential Rule Learning (FERL), a method for interpretable classification that provides transparency about decisions and allows models to abstain when reliability is low.

title: Alternating Levenberg-Marquardt Training of Physics-Informed Neural Networks with Fourier-Enhanced Features
summary: This paper proposes an alternating Levenberg-Marquardt training method with Fourier-enhanced features to improve Physics-Informed Neural Networks' accuracy for complex partial differential equations.

title: BioM-JEPA: joint-embedding prediction of graph-connected gene blocks in single cells
summary: Researchers present BioM-JEPA, a joint-embedding predictive architecture that uses aggregate representations of graph-connected gene blocks to learn from single-cell transcriptomes more effectively.

title: How Far Do Simple Transformations Translate Across Text Embedding Models?
summary: This investigation examines the extent to which simple transformations can translate representations across different text embedding models, crucial for AI-to-AI latent communication.

title: Observation-Grounded Self-Predictive Reinforcement Learning for Visual Continuous Control
summary: This work introduces a new observation-grounded self-predictive reinforcement learning method designed to achieve sample-efficient policy learning from pixels for visual continuous control.

title: A Unified Risk View of Uncertainty: Posterior Risk for Disentanglement and Evaluation Beyond Proxies
summary: This paper proposes a unified posterior risk view for understanding and disentangling different types of uncertainty in AI models, essential for reliability in safety-sensitive applications.

title: Do Tabular Foundation Models Agree with Themselves?
summary: This study investigates the internal consistency of Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) by examining how these transformer-based models align with their own predictions.

title: ProDVI: Programmatic Dynamics Priors for Value Network Initialization
summary: This paper introduces ProDVI, a method that uses programmatic dynamics priors to provide informative initializations for value networks, thereby improving sample efficiency in Deep Reinforcement Learning.

title: BioKD: Selective Physiology-to-Video Knowledge Distillation via Reliability Gate for Emotion Recognition
summary: This paper proposes BioKD, a reliability-aware physiology-to-video knowledge distillation framework, to improve emotion recognition by selectively integrating physiological signals with video data.

title: Hybrid-Adaptive Thread Tuning to Mitigate Simulation Execution Bottlenecks in High-Performance Reinforcement Learning Inference
summary: Researchers present a hybrid-adaptive thread tuning strategy designed to mitigate simulation execution bottlenecks and optimize performance in high-performance reinforcement learning inference systems.

title: Does Latent Context Help? A Controlled Evaluation of Inverse Reinforcement Learning in Arctic Shipping
summary: This research evaluates the utility of Inverse Reinforcement Learning for AI-assisted navigation in Arctic shipping, focusing on the interpretability and robustness of reward models in dynamic environments.

title: Kastor: An efficient fine-tuning strategy for generative emulation of PDE simulations
summary: This paper introduces Kastor, an efficient fine-tuning strategy for generative AI models to accelerate physical simulations by emulating Partial Differential Equation solvers.

title: Is Self-Pretraining really useful to improve diagnosis in medical Time Series?
summary: This research investigates whether Self-PreTraining (SPT) improves diagnostic performance in various types of medical time series data, extending its application from long-context benchmarks.

title: LLM Inference Under Bursty Workload Distribution: Modifying the WAIT Algorithm
summary: This research focuses on improving scheduling algorithms to optimize throughput and latency for Large Language Model (LLM) inference under bursty workload distributions. It proposes modifying the WAIT algorithm to enhance performance.

title: SkillTFM: Gated Skill Evolution for Training-Free Adaptation of Tabular Foundation Models
summary: This paper introduces SkillTFM, a framework for training-free adaptation of Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) using gated skill evolution. It aims to improve general-purpose tabular learning across various real-world applications.

title: Threshold-Based Early Stopping of Accumulations in Neural Networks with Binary Activation
summary: This research proposes a threshold-based early stopping method for accumulations in neural networks with binary activation. This technique aims to improve the efficiency and enable low-power inference for binary neural networks in constrained deployments.

title: Simulator-Grounded Large Language Models for Industrial Causal Reasoning: Tool-Use, Structured Injection, and Plant-Portable Retrieval for Wastewater Treatment Decision Support
summary: This paper explores methods like tool-use, structured injection, and plant-portable retrieval to ground Large Language Models (LLMs) for industrial causal reasoning. The application is demonstrated with decision support for wastewater treatment plant operators.

title: Mean-Field Dynamics of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Large Language Models
summary: This study introduces a mean-field dynamics framework to provide theoretical explanations for the behavior of chain-of-thought reasoning in Large Language Models (LLMs). It seeks statistical regularities to deepen understanding and guide model optimization.

title: Universal Pathologies, Conditional Consequences: A Triple-Robustness Analysis of RAG for Multi-Hop Traceability
summary: This research presents a triple-robustness analysis of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems for multi-hop traceability. It compares GraphRAG and vector RAG performance, varying embedders and corpora to understand pathologies and consequences.

title: RIG-RoPE: Relation- and Instance-Gated Rotary Positional Encoding with Duration-Aware Temporal Coordinates
summary: This paper introduces RIG-RoPE, a new variant of Rotary Positional Encoding that uses relation- and instance-gated mechanisms with duration-aware temporal coordinates. It aims to improve positional encoding in modern language and multimodal models.

title: Beyond Sentiment: Comparing Traditional NLP and LLM-Based Multi-Dimensional Analysis for Political News Evaluation
summary: This paper compares traditional NLP and LLM-based multi-dimensional analysis for evaluating political news, moving beyond sentiment analysis to explore rhetorical, ideological, and framing dimensions.

title: Scaffold-Mediated Post-Training: Co-Evolving Model Parameters and Procedural Scaffold Graphs
summary: This research proposes scaffold-mediated post-training for Large Language Models, a method that co-evolves model parameters and procedural scaffold graphs. It aims to help models automatically acquire and internalize complex strategies.

title: Large Language Models Threaten Double-blind Review
summary: This paper argues that Large Language Models (LLMs) pose a threat to the integrity of double-blind peer review by potentially compromising author anonymity. It discusses the implications for scientific bias and fairness.

title: Safe Evolution with Circuit Anchors
summary: This paper draws an analogy from biological evolution to discuss "safe evolution with circuit anchors," where core regulatory components remain stable. This concept is applied to ensure safety in evolving complex systems, likely AI.

title: SemiAdapt-Instruct: Extensible Instruction Tuning via Latent Domain-Specialised Adapters
summary: This paper presents SemiAdapt-Instruct, a modular framework for extensible instruction tuning of LLMs using latent domain-specialized adapters. It aims to extend model capabilities without full retraining in evolving domains.

title: PoolBench: A Benchmark for Pooling Strategies in Concept Representation Evaluation for Decoder-Only LLMs
summary: This paper introduces PoolBench, a new benchmark specifically designed to evaluate and compare different pooling strategies for concept representation in decoder-only Large Language Models (LLMs).

title: Where Privacy Risk Lives in English-Source Multilingual RAG: A Stage-Decomposed Audit Across Five Query Languages
summary: This research conducts a stage-decomposed audit to investigate where privacy risks reside in English-source multilingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems. It examines vulnerability to personal information extraction across five query languages.

title: Cross-Architecture Steering Transfer in Language Models: A Systematic Empirical Study
summary: This systematic empirical study investigates cross-architecture steering transfer in language models, exploring if shared internal representations of semantic concepts enable functional behavioral control across different model architectures.

title: A Study of ASR Adaptation and Representation Dimensionality Reduction in Persian Speech Emotion Recognition Using Whisper
summary: This study investigates ASR adaptation and representation dimensionality reduction for Persian Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) using the Whisper model. It focuses on addressing challenges in low-resource languages.

title: Conditional Cognitive Biases in LLMs: How Biased User Turns Modulate In-Context Reasoning
summary: This research evaluates conditional cognitive biases in state-of-the-art instruction-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs). It uses a novel experimental framework to analyze how biased user turns modulate in-context reasoning.

title: CNM-BERT: A Drop-In Structural Embedding for Chinese Characters via Ideographic Description Sequences
summary: This paper introduces CNM-BERT, a new structural embedding method for Chinese characters based on Ideographic Description Sequences. It aims to improve performance for rare and out-of-vocabulary characters compared to token-based encoders.

title: ConWriter: Transition-Constrained Stateful Long-Form Story Generation with Lightweight Neuro-Symbolic Consistency Control
summary: This paper proposes ConWriter, a training-free neuro-symbolic framework for transition-constrained stateful long-form story generation. It aims to improve narrative consistency across extended contexts.

title: DREAM: LLM-based Dynamic Role-playing via Event-Aware Memory Graph
summary: This paper introduces DREAM, an LLM-based framework for dynamic role-playing agents that leverages an event-aware memory graph. It aims to enable immersive and high-fidelity character simulation with temporally consistent behavior.

title: Position: It's Time to Optimize LLMs for Self-Consistency
summary: This position paper discusses common failures in large language models like sycophancy and incomplete logical generalization, arguing for optimizing LLMs for self-consistency to address these issues during pre- and post-training.

title: Analysis of Numerical Localisation in LLM Translations
summary: This research analyzes the capability of five large language models to perform numerical localization, specifically for times, numbers, and dates, extending previous work on numerical translation.

title: Constraint-First Reasoning: A Training-Free Protocol for Exploiting Answer-Space Constraints in Mathematical Problem Solving
summary: This paper introduces Constraint-First Reasoning (CFR), a training-free two-stage prompting protocol designed to help large language models avoid violating explicit requirements in mathematical problem solving.

title: Evidence Lock Before Commitment: A Frozen Interface Degrades LLM-as-Judge Evaluation
summary: This research investigates how the "evidence lock before commitment" workflow, common in LLM-as-Judge evaluations, can degrade the assessment by not reflecting the internal decision order of reasoning-capable models.

title: Mood Matters: How Syntactic Sensitivity Undermines Safety Alignment
summary: This paper explores how syntactic sensitivity in large language models can undermine safety alignment, demonstrating how changes in grammatical tense can lead to sophisticated jailbreaks.

title: Example-Guided Prompting for Document-Level Text Simplification
summary: This research introduces an example-guided prompting method to improve the consistency and quality of large language models in document-level text simplification tasks.

title: DBLAST: Dependent Block Drafting for Stochastic Speculative Decoding
summary: This paper introduces DBLAST, a new dependent block drafting method for stochastic speculative decoding, aimed at accelerating the inference speed of large language models.

title: Different Perturbations, Different Mechanisms: Understanding Continued Pre-training for Zero-Shot Dialect Robustness
summary: This research explores the mechanisms by which different perturbation-based continued pre-training strategies enhance zero-shot dialect robustness in multilingual language models.

title: Where Models Converge and Humans Diverge: A Coverage Framework for Distributional Pluralism in Open-Ended Generation
summary: This research introduces a coverage framework to analyze the differences between large language models and humans in open-ended generation tasks, highlighting where models converge and humans diverge in creative output.

title: SkillZip: Contract-Preserving Graph Compression for Scalable Agent Skill Libraries
summary: This paper introduces SkillZip, a method for contract-preserving graph compression designed to create scalable agent skill libraries for large language models, optimizing for limited context budgets.

title: FOCUS: Decoupling Expert Personas in LLMs to Enhance Domain Expert Capabilities
summary: This research introduces FOCUS, a method for decoupling expert personas in large language models to enhance their domain expert capabilities by mitigating cross-domain coupling.

title: Human-Like Anaphor Resolution in Large Language Models
summary: This research investigates the human-like anaphor resolution capabilities in large language models, comparing their performance against factors identified in cognitive science.

title: Relay, Don't Route: Adaptive Population Handoff for Cost-Efficient LLM-Driven Evolution
summary: This paper proposes "Adaptive Population Handoff," a new method to enable cost-efficient large language model-driven evolution for tasks like program search and algorithm discovery by adaptively combining models.

title: Answer First, Reason Later: Commitment Order in Diffusion LLMs
summary: This research investigates the commitment order in masked diffusion language models, showing that the freedom to commit tokens in any order can be a point of failure in reasoning tasks.

title: Sparse Mutual Information Graph Averaging for Improving Random Indexing Embeddings
summary: This paper proposes using sparse mutual information graph averaging to refine random indexing (RI) vectors, aiming to improve sparse word embeddings in AI systems.

title: Mitigating Scoring Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge via Random Number Generation
summary: This research proposes mitigating scoring bias in LLM-as-a-Judge systems through random number generation, addressing the tendency of LLM evaluators to generate particular scores.

title: Once a Response, Always a Response: Detecting LLM-generated Text via Latent Prompt Restoration
summary: This research introduces a new method called "latent prompt restoration" for robustly detecting text generated by large language models, addressing concerns about misinformation and misuse.

title: How to Recognize New Words: A Comparison Between Context Biasing Methods and Speech LLMs
summary: This research compares context biasing methods with speech large language models for improving automatic speech recognition's ability to recognize new and rare words.

title: On-Policy Delta Distillation for Multilingual Math Reasoning
summary: This research studies On-Policy Distillation (OPD) and its advanced variant (OPD$^2$) as post-training methods to enhance multilingual mathematical reasoning capabilities in large language models.

title: Hierarchical Latent Prediction for Language Models
summary: This research explores Hierarchical Latent Prediction as an alternative pre-training paradigm for language models, aiming to improve their performance in long-horizon reasoning and planning tasks.

title: M$^3$R-Bench: A Unified Benchmark for Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Metaphor Understanding
summary: Introduces M$^3$R-Bench, a new unified benchmark for evaluating evidence-grounded multimodal metaphor understanding in AI systems, focusing on conceptual understanding and cross-modal reasoning.

title: Decomposed Entailment for Factuality Checking and Hallucination Detection
summary: Presents HallDetect, a lightweight, reference-free, and black-box framework for detecting hallucinations and checking factuality in Large Language Models by decomposing entailment.

title: MoCA: Implicit Social Context Analysis
summary: Discusses the challenge of AI understanding implicit social contexts in human communication, which involve indirect, socially and culturally grounded signals.

title: Enhancing Social Intelligence in LLMs with Hierarchical Reasoning and Utterance-Level Goal Rewarding
summary: Proposes methods to enhance the social intelligence of Large Language Models in dynamic social interactions by applying hierarchical reasoning and utterance-level goal rewarding.

title: MameLoshnLM: Yiddish Language Model and Evaluation Benchmark
summary: Introduces MameLoshnLM, the first open-source 8-billion-parameter language model specifically developed for the Yiddish language, addressing the scarcity of digital resources for Yiddish AI.

title: Mapping Similarity Spaces across Embedding Models with Synthetic Query Probing
summary: Investigates how similarity scores and geometric properties can be mapped across different embedding models to improve RAG systems and facilitate model migration.

title: MACRO: Markov Chain Routing of Transformer Layers
summary: Introduces MACRO (Markov Chain Routing of Transformer Layers), a new method for dynamically routing execution paths through transformer layers to improve LLM performance without updating model weights.

title: Causal Episodic Memory for Feedback-Driven Agent Repair
summary: Introduces MERIT, a training-free agent that uses causal episodic memory to store and apply successful corrections, enabling efficient repair of Text-to-SQL failures in subsequent episodes.

title: Clinical Communication Processing with Models Trained on LLM-Generated Synthetic Data: A Structured Survey and Novel Application Case Studies
summary: Presents a structured survey and case studies on processing clinical communication using AI models trained on LLM-generated synthetic data, highlighting applications in healthcare.

title: EpiBench: Can LLMs Understand Epitopes for Antibody Drug Discovery?
summary: Introduces EpiBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the capability of Large Language Models to understand epitopes, which is crucial for antibody drug discovery.

title: FormBharo: Designing and Evaluating a Voice Agent for Conversational Form Filling in Rural India
summary: Presents FormBharo, a voice agent designed and evaluated to enable conversational form filling for illiterate populations in rural India, facilitating access to social benefits.

title: Training-Free Token-Level Steering for LLM Personalized Co-Writing
summary: Proposes a method for training-free token-level steering to achieve personalized co-writing with Large Language Models, addressing computational costs and data updates.

title: Beyond Sequence Order: Syntax-Informed Positional Embeddings for Transformers
summary: Introduces SiPE (Syntax-informed Positional Embeddings), a new method to enhance Transformers by incorporating syntactic structure into positional embeddings, going beyond simple sequence order.

title: Decolonizing Linguistic Policies in Automated Speech Recognition: A Framework for Cross-Culturally Competent Speech AI
summary: Examines linguistic policies in Automatic Speech Recognition, arguing that failures for low-resource languages reflect implicit policies, and proposes a framework for cross-culturally competent speech AI.

title: NeSy-RAG: Neuro-Symbolic RAG for Explainable Question Answering
summary: Introduces NeSy-RAG, a neuro-symbolic Retrieval-Augmented Generation system designed to improve explainable question answering by grounding Large Language Models in external knowledge.

title: Benchmarking and Enhancing LLMs for Rule-Intensive Review of National Standard Documents
summary: Evaluates and proposes methods to enhance Large Language Models for rule-intensive review of national standard documents, using China GB/T standards as a testbed.

title: Benchmarking the Benchmarks: Evaluating Benchmarks for Conversational Agents
summary: Introduces a reference framework to evaluate the quality of benchmarks used for conversational agents, addressing issues like inconsistent tasks and limited policy coverage.

title: RP-OPSD: Reasoning-Pivot-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multilingual Reasoning Transfer
summary: Proposes RP-OPSD (Reasoning-Pivot-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation), a new paradigm to extend reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models to multilingual contexts.

title: The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling
summary: Discusses the concept of tool calling in Large Language Models, which enables them to act as agents beyond their training data, and presents a systematic evaluation of tools as code.

title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
summary: Investigates a method called Selective Context Preference Optimization, which trains language models to learn when to trust or disregard external context signals to improve accuracy.

title: MapTCL: Temporal Consistency Learning via Bidirectional Alignment for Vectorized HD Map Construction
summary: This paper proposes MapTCL, a method for constructing reliable online HD maps in dynamic urban environments by improving temporal consistency through bidirectional alignment and feature-level temporal fusion.

title: Innocent Panels, Hateful Stories: Evaluating and Detecting Hateful Intent in Multi-Turn Visual Story Generation
summary: This research evaluates and proposes methods to detect hateful intent in multi-turn visual story generation produced by text-to-image systems like Gemini and GPT-Image, addressing the potential for harmful narratives.

title: StyleComposer: Training-Free Multi-Reference Style Composition
summary: StyleComposer is a training-free method for multi-reference style composition, allowing users to combine distinct style attributes like color, texture, and structure from different sources within a diffusion model.

title: In-Context Forcing: Uncovering Context Effects in Autoregressive Video Diffusion
summary: This paper introduces 'In-Context Forcing' to analyze and improve how autoregressive video diffusion models use context, aiming to prevent shortcuts and enhance temporal semantic consistency in generated videos.

title: Grad-CAM for Vision Transformers: A Systematic Taxonomy and Audit of Methodological Ambiguity in Explainable AI
summary: This research provides a systematic taxonomy and audit of methodological ambiguities when adapting Grad-CAM, a visualization technique, for use with Vision Transformers in Explainable AI.

title: A Paragraph is Worth a Thousand Captions: Rethinking Text Supervision for Vision-Language Retrieval
summary: This paper proposes rethinking text supervision for vision-language retrieval, suggesting that training with detailed paragraph descriptions rather than short captions can enhance model ability to retrieve images from complex text.

title: Context Matters: Support Set Selection and Failure Detection for In-Context Medical Image Segmentation
summary: This research investigates the critical role of support set selection and failure detection in in-context learning (ICL) for medical image segmentation, emphasizing how the support set influences model performance.

title: Positive-Unlabeled Preference Optimization For Chest X-ray Report Generation
summary: This paper proposes Positive-Unlabeled Preference Optimization to improve Vision-Language Models for chest X-ray report generation, addressing issues of omission noise in retrospective clinical data.

title: LoDA: A Level of Detection Aware Method and a Multimodal Sensing Benchmark for Object Level Change Detection
summary: LoDA is a new method and multimodal sensing benchmark designed for detecting object-level changes in 3D LiDAR maps, critical for maintaining up-to-date HD maps in autonomous driving and smart-city services.

title: Text-Guided Refinement of Multi-sequence Glioma Subregion Segmentation with a Vision-Language Foundation Model
summary: This research explores using a Vision-Language Foundation Model for text-guided refinement of multi-sequence glioma subregion segmentation, aiming to improve accuracy and efficiency in radiotherapy planning.

title: Adapting Vision Foundation Models with Cascaded Semantics
summary: This paper proposes 'Cascaded Semantics' as a method for adapting Vision Foundation Models, extending prompt tuning to efficiently adapt pre-trained Vision Transformers with a small set of additional prompt parameters.

title: MOSAIK: Multi-Patch Content-Aware Spatial Allocation of Image Tokens for Efficient Generation
summary: MOSAIK is a method designed to enhance the efficiency of pixel-space diffusion models for image generation by employing multi-patch content-aware spatial allocation of image tokens, thereby reducing self-attention complexity.

title: CDSeg: A Renderable Gaussian Carrier for Image-to-3D Label Transfer
summary: CDSeg (Cross-Domain Segmentation via Gaussian Splatting) is a novel label-transfer interface that enables the robust transfer of 2D image labels to 3D, providing spatial persistence for segmentation masks.

title: VideoArgus: Agentic Rubric-Grounded Unified Evaluation for Video Generation and Editing
summary: VideoArgus is a new agentic, rubric-grounded framework for unified evaluation of video generation and editing models, designed to provide comprehensive and evidence-based scoring beyond existing benchmarks.

title: APQF: Agentic Profiling-Guided Structured Pruning and Mixed-Precision Quantization with Adaptive Fine-Tuning
summary: APQF introduces an agentic profiling-guided method for structured pruning and mixed-precision quantization with adaptive fine-tuning, aiming to optimize deep neural networks for efficient deployment on resource-constrained edge devices.

title: DynaPix: Can Vision-Language Models Identify the Exact Future?
summary: DynaPix is a new benchmark designed to rigorously evaluate Vision-Language Models on their ability to identify the exact future state of a physical scene, ensuring predictions are precisely checkable against reality.

title: HERA: Historical Evidence Routing Adapter for Physical Prediction in Latent World Models
summary: HERA (Historical Evidence Routing Adapter) is proposed to enhance predictive video models by improving their ability to route and utilize historical evidence for more accurate physical prediction, especially in scenarios with occlusion.

title: OmniMech: All-in-one Multimodal Mechanical Benchmark for 3D Reconstruction
summary: OmniMech is presented as an all-in-one multimodal mechanical benchmark for 3D reconstruction, specifically designed to evaluate vision-language models generating executable CAD programs with fine-grained geometry for industrial design.

title: Hierarchical Flow Matching for 3D Point Cloud Generation
summary: This paper introduces Hierarchical Flow Matching, a new method for generating high-quality 3D point clouds that captures both global shape topology and local geometric details, improving upon existing flow-based and diffusion models.

title: From Sports to Safety: Benchmarking Proactive Risk Inference in MLLMs
summary: This research introduces a new benchmark that uses sports scenarios to evaluate the proactive risk inference capabilities of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs), focusing on the anticipation of real-world physical hazards.

title: EffectLearner: World-Aware Object-Effect Reasoning for Real-World Video Object Removal
summary: EffectLearner is a new method for world-aware object-effect reasoning for real-world video object removal, maintaining high-fidelity and spatiotemporally coherent restoration.

title: CoordRefer: Coordinate-Aware 3D Visual Grounding from Multiview Images
summary: CoordRefer is a coordinate-aware 3D visual grounding method from multiview images that predicts a coordinate frame and regresses a 3D bounding box for localization.

title: Beyond Frame Selection: Rethinking Long-Video Understanding with MLLMs
summary: This work rethinks long-video understanding with Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) by proposing methods beyond frame selection to overcome token limitations for temporally sparse evidence.

title: Uncertainty-Aware World Model for Aerial Image-Goal Navigation
summary: This research introduces an uncertainty-aware world model for aerial image-goal navigation, allowing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to reach target locations specified by goal images.

title: ALTER: Modeling Longitudinal Changes via Regional Differencing for 3D CT Report Generation
summary: ALTER is a method for modeling longitudinal changes via regional differencing for 3D CT report generation, aiming to automatically create accurate radiology reports from CT scans.

title: TruthLens: Object Hallucination Detection via Self-Evaluating Truthfulness Scores in LVLMs
summary: TruthLens is a method for object hallucination detection in Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs) by self-evaluating truthfulness scores based on separable hidden representations.

title: Dual-Output Multi-Exposure HDR Reconstruction via SDR Fusion and Gain Map Inverse Tone Mapping
summary: DOME-HDR is a dual-output multi-exposure HDR reconstruction framework that jointly produces a perceptually balanced SDR image and a consistent HDR image via gain map inverse tone mapping.

title: SCI-CLIP: Segment-Centric Inference with Reference Memory for Training-Free Open-Vocabulary Segmentation
summary: SCI-CLIP offers segment-centric inference with reference memory for training-free open-vocabulary segmentation, addressing limitations in patch-level vision-language features.

title: ChronoVision: Temporal Reasoning via Latent State Reconstruction
summary: ChronoVision improves temporal reasoning in multimodal large language models for complex visual cognitive tasks by using latent state reconstruction to articulate continuous visual changes.

title: Vorch-IR: Long-Form Unified Multimodal Identity Replacement Video Generation
summary: Vorch-IR is a method for long-form unified multimodal identity replacement video generation, capable of transferring identities while preserving motion, expressions, and temporal structure.

title: Vorch-Streamer: Extending Human Audio-Visual Generation to Real-Time Long-Form Streaming
summary: Vorch-Streamer extends human audio-visual generation to real-time long-form streaming, enabling causal, continuous synthesis with maintained audiovisual synchronization and visual consistency.

title: URNet: A Unified Reparameterized Network for Efficient RGB-D Semantic Segmentation
summary: URNet is a unified reparameterized network for efficient RGB-D semantic segmentation, addressing limitations of existing methods that use dual encoders for RGB and depth inputs.

title: DistMedVL: Distributional Vision-Language Alignment for Uncertainty-Aware Medical Image Segmentation
summary: DistMedVL proposes a distributional vision-language alignment method for uncertainty-aware medical image segmentation, addressing challenges in cross-modal alignment under clinical conditions.

title: SciQNet: Two-Stage Multimodal Adaptation for Scientific Image Quality Assessment
summary: SciQNet is a two-stage multimodal adaptation system for scientific image quality assessment, evaluating both visual clarity and scientific informativeness of images.

title: TAU-Bench: From Anomaly Instance Tracking to Fine-Grained Video Anomaly Understanding
summary: TAU-Bench is a new benchmark focused on fine-grained video anomaly understanding, enabling models to identify, track, and interpret anomalous events in videos.

title: StreamArena: Toward Continuous, Interactive, and Long-Horizon Agentic Streaming Video Understanding
summary: StreamArena is an evaluation environment for continuous, interactive, and long-horizon agentic streaming video understanding, designed for autonomous multimodal agents in real-world settings.

title: G$^2$ARD-GS: Geometry-Guided Anchor-Regularized Gaussian Splatting Distillation
summary: G$^2$ARD-GS is a geometry-guided anchor-regularized Gaussian Splatting distillation method designed to reduce the storage, transmission, and rendering costs of 3D Gaussian Splatting models.

title: LAWM-3D: Learning 3D-Aware Latent Actions from Human Videos for Generalizable Robot World Models
summary: LAWM-3D proposes learning 3D-aware latent actions from human videos to create generalizable robot world models, enabling robots to perform forward rollout and planning.

title: One Ranking, Any Budget: Matryoshka Evidence-to-Context Frame Selection for Long-Video Understanding
summary: This research introduces Matryoshka Evidence-to-Context Frame Selection, a method for optimizing frame selection in Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) for long-video understanding across various budgets.

title: PhyLatent: Learning Dynamics-Relevant Representations for JEPA World Models
summary: PhyLatent proposes a dynamics-relevant training objective for JointEmbedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) world models, aiming to preserve physical states and action consequences in representations.

title: Engram-E2VID: Reference-Based Event-to-Video Reconstruction via Generative Activation of Appearance Engrams
summary: This paper introduces Engram-E2VID, a method for reconstructing RGB video frames from an event stream and a reference frame by leveraging generative activation of appearance engrams. It aims to recover fine-grained temporal cues to create video from sparse event data.

title: LiteKD-Net: Lightweight Knowledge-Distilled Network for Mobile Image Denoising
summary: LiteKD-Net is a lightweight, knowledge-distilled network designed for mobile image denoising, focusing on achieving good restoration quality with low computational cost. It addresses the challenge of limited large-scale training data by using a physics-guided noise simulation.

title: ConceptADapt: Concept-guided Adaptive Feature Reconstruction with Dynamic Attention for Few-Shot Industrial Anomaly Detection
summary: ConceptADapt is a method for few-shot industrial anomaly detection that uses concept-guided adaptive feature reconstruction with dynamic attention to identify visual defects. It is designed for scenarios with limited normal training samples per category.

title: UniVVT: A Unified End-to-End Framework for High-Fidelity Video Virtual Try-on
summary: UniVVT is a unified end-to-end framework designed for high-fidelity video virtual try-on, which synthesizes video of a person wearing a target garment while preserving identity, motion, and scene dynamics. It aims to integrate separate modules for a more coherent solution.

title: GST-Bench: Can VLMs Develop Global Spatial Awareness from Video?
summary: This paper introduces GST-Bench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate if Vision-Language Models (VLMs) can develop global spatial awareness from continuous, long-horizon video streams. It aims to address limitations of existing benchmarks that focus on local spatial perception.

title: Beyond Relevance: Bayesian Evidence Acquisition for Agentic Whole-Slide Image Reasoning
summary: This research proposes a Bayesian evidence acquisition approach for agentic whole-slide image reasoning, where an agent sequentially gathers visual evidence to answer diagnostic questions. It aims to move beyond simple semantic relevance for more robust evidence collection.

title: HyTBE: Hyperbolic Target-Background Expert Model for Cross-Domain Infrared Small Target Detection
summary: HyTBE is a Hyperbolic Target-Background Expert Model designed for cross-domain infrared small target detection, aiming to improve performance when generalizing to unseen infrared domains. It focuses on enhancing target responses and suppressing background noise.

title: Vorch-Director: Interactive World Story Model via Noise-Aware Error Rectification
summary: Vorch-Director is an interactive world story model that uses noise-aware error rectification for minute-scale audio-visual generation. It extends a short-window generator to produce continuous audio and video content.

title: Evidence-Driven Dynamic Visual Selector for Efficient Long Video Understanding
summary: This paper presents an Evidence-Driven Dynamic Visual Selector designed to improve efficient long video understanding for MLLM-based systems by selecting query-relevant frames. The approach aims to mitigate computational costs and context length limitations without relying on external proxy scorers.

title: VSMP-IMU: Video-Grounded Semantic Motion Programs for Sensor-Aware Synthetic IMU Generation
summary: VSMP-IMU introduces Video-Grounded Semantic Motion Programs for generating synthetic IMU data, aiming to reduce dependency on labeled sensor data for wearable human activity recognition. This method helps enhance HAR machine learning model performance, especially in low-resource settings.

title: KVAE: Family of Tokenizers for Multimodal Generative Models
summary: KVAE is a family of tokenizers designed for multimodal generative models, particularly within latent diffusion modeling, to map input signals to compressed representations. These tokenizers are integral to the generation process, impacting learning speed and quality of synthesized outputs.

title: Vorch-Omni: Multi-Task Orchestration of Sight and Sound
summary: Vorch-Omni is a model for multi-task orchestration of sight and sound, building on advances in generative video modeling. It aims to provide diverse generation, reference-based synthesis, extension, and editing capabilities by distinguishing various signal types.

title: Ordered Diffusion for 3D Human Registration
summary: Ordered Diffusion is a method for 3D human registration, addressing the inherent ambiguity in human scans caused by acquisition noise, occlusions, and soft tissue dynamics. It moves beyond traditional regression tasks to provide more robust alignment.

title: STAIL: Semantic Text-Anchored Incremental Learning for Medical Imaging via Large Language Models
summary: STAIL proposes Semantic Text-Anchored Incremental Learning for medical imaging, utilizing Large Language Models to mitigate catastrophic forgetting when continually adapting to new clinical tasks. This method moves beyond pixel-level rehearsal by leveraging semantic text anchors.

title: VLAff: Vision-Language-Affordance Model for Unified Actionable Affordances
summary: VLAff is a Vision-Language-Affordance Model designed to learn unified actionable affordances for robot manipulation skills from human videos. It aims to bridge the embodiment mismatch between humans and robots by focusing on object-centric, embodiment-agnostic affordances.

title: A System for Train Condition Monitoring and Structural Health Assessment of Rail Vehicles
summary: This paper describes a system for train condition monitoring and structural health assessment of rail vehicles, leveraging artificial intelligence within the ongoing digitalization of rail systems. It highlights the transformation of design, operation, and maintenance practices.

title: Failing Gracefully: Mitigating Impact of Inevitable Robot Failures
summary: This research focuses on mitigating the impact of inevitable failures in service robots operating in complex household environments, such as software crashes, hardware degradation, or unpredictable interactions. It acknowledges that while failures cannot be entirely eliminated, their effects can be reduced.

title: Unified Planning-Learning Framework for Robust UUV Navigation Under Partial Observability
summary: This paper presents a unified planning-learning framework for robust navigation of Unmanned Underwater Vehicles (UUVs) in dynamic environments with partial observability. The system integrates persistent occupancy mapping, global clearance-aware planning, and risk-aware local control.

title: World-to-Wrist: Task-Conditioned Future Wrist Modeling for Fine-Grained Robot Manipulation
summary: This research introduces task-conditioned future wrist modeling for fine-grained robot manipulation, addressing how vision-language-action (VLA) models use wrist-view observations. It aims to help robots anticipate local wrist interactions within the context of global tasks.

title: PathCover: A Fast Convex Decomposition along a Path via Randomized Iterative Space Partitioning (RISP) on Point Clouds
summary: PathCover is a framework for autonomous robot navigation that rapidly generates obstacle-free regions for trajectory planning using Randomized Iterative Space Partitioning (RISP) on point clouds. It aims to overcome computational bottlenecks of existing corridor generators.

title: Search-Aided Joint Agent-Environment Reinforcement Learning for Robust Lifelong Multi-Agent Path Finding with Rotations
summary: This research introduces a search-aided joint agent-environment reinforcement learning method for robust lifelong multi-agent path finding, enabling agents to continuously plan collision-free paths for new goals.

summary: This research proposes Latent Fact-Checking, a method to detect misinformation by analyzing truthfulness as a geometric property within a language model's representation space using activation engineering.

title: Sharding Prevents LLM Oversight Failures and Adversarial Exploitation
summary: This research proposes sharding as a mechanism to prevent Large Language Model oversight failures and mitigate adversarial exploitation, particularly when models are tasked with rendering multiple verdicts.

title: Adversarial Causal Intervention Falsification
summary: This research investigates adversarial causal intervention falsification, a sequential game designed to reveal whether generative models encode incorrect causal structures despite accurately reproducing observational distributions.

title: Fixed and Adaptive Topological DeepONets: Functional Measurements on Hausdorff Locally Convex Spaces
summary: This paper introduces Fixed and Adaptive Topological DeepONets, an improvement over traditional DeepONets that replaces point samples with continuous linear functionals for encoding input functions. This method builds on the Topological DeepONet framework to enhance functional measurements.

title: MiGHT-EHR: A Multi-task Graph Transformer for Heterogeneous Temporal Electronic Health Records
summary: This paper introduces MiGHT-EHR, a multi-task graph transformer model designed to learn from heterogeneous, temporally ordered Electronic Health Records (EHRs). The model aims to improve clinical prediction by effectively processing complex EHR data.

title: SNI-GNN: SmartNIC-Assisted Full-Graph GNN Training with In-Network Embedding Prediction
summary: SNI-GNN is a SmartNIC-assisted system designed for full-graph Graph Neural Network (GNN) training, aiming to improve scalability on multi-server clusters. It reduces inter-node communication and preserves accuracy by predicting remote embeddings in-network.

title: ED-CSP: Crystal Structure Prediction from Electron Diffraction
summary: ED-CSP is a method for predicting periodic 3D crystal structures by recovering them from sparse and unindexed electron diffraction observations. It addresses a generative inverse problem in materials science.

title: Beyond Attention: Signed Integrated Gradients Attribution in a BiomeGPT-Style Microbiome Transformer
summary: This paper introduces Signed Integrated Gradients Attribution as a method to interpret downstream classification in feature-tokenized transformer models, specifically in the context of a BiomeGPT-style microbiome transformer. The technique aims to explain how such models make decisions.

title: CertBind from Multimodal Connectivity to Certifiable Retrieval Decisions
summary: CertBind is a multi-modal system that enables certifiable retrieval decisions by integrating lightweight connectors with frozen multimodal encoders. It addresses challenges in expanding cross-modal reach while preserving retrieval capabilities.

title: Robust Average-Reward Markov Decision Processes: Minimax-Optimal Learning via Plug-in Reductions
summary: This theoretical paper investigates Robust Average-Reward Markov Decision Processes, focusing on minimax-optimal learning strategies via plug-in reductions. It determines the sample complexity required to learn an epsilon-optimal robust policy under model uncertainty.

title: Newton-Schulz Retraction-Based Inference Enables Hidden Quantum Markov Models to Outperform Classical HMMs
summary: This paper demonstrates that Newton-Schulz Retraction-Based Inference enables Hidden Quantum Markov Models (HQMMs) to outperform classical Hidden Markov Models (HMMs). HQMMs generalize HMMs by incorporating quantum operators and density matrices for more complex dynamics.

title: Bootstrap-Conditioned Action Selection with Tabular Foundation Models
summary: This paper explores Bootstrap-Conditioned Action Selection with Tabular Foundation Models to improve sample-efficient personalization in contextual bandits. It addresses challenges like sparse data, biased interactions, and cold starts by leveraging pre-trained foundation models.

title: Theoretical Foundations of Communication-Efficient, Robust, and Practical Distributed and Federated Optimization
summary: This paper establishes theoretical foundations for communication-efficient, robust, and practical distributed and federated optimization in machine learning. It addresses the challenges of large-scale AI training in distributed systems.

title: Quantization Damage Is Multiplicative, Not Additive
summary: This paper examines "Quantization Damage" in Large Language Models (LLMs), identifying it as multiplicative rather than additive, and its silent impact on model decisions. It details how quantization can affect an agent's ability to use tools or maintain safety refusals during deployment.

title: CrystalGRPO: Target-Aligned and Coverage-Preserving Reinforcement Learning for Flow-Based Crystal Structure Prediction
summary: CrystalGRPO introduces a reinforcement learning post-training method for flow-based generative models to improve crystal structure prediction (CSP). It focuses on target-aligned and coverage-preserving optimization to enhance downstream target recovery.

title: Flowing Through States: Neural ODE Regularization for Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper proposes Neural ODE Regularization for Reinforcement Learning to address misalignment between environment dynamics and latent state transitions in neural networks for sequential decision-making tasks. It aims to improve how latent representations evolve.

title: Retrofitting Linear Attention into Diffusion Language Models
summary: This paper explores retrofitting linear attention into Diffusion Language Models (dLLMs) to enhance their performance. This modification aims to improve inference acceleration through parallel decoding in these alternative generative models.

title: The Sparsity Whisperer
summary: This paper, titled "The Sparsity Whisperer," proposes a new approach to pruning Large Language Models (LLMs) that goes beyond existing criteria. It focuses on identifying and preserving sparsity-sensitive neurons to more effectively reduce inference costs.

title: Cryptanalytic Extraction of Isolated Bias-Free GLU Feed-Forward Blocks by Antipodal Separation
summary: This paper introduces a method for cryptanalytic extraction of isolated bias-free Gated Linear Unit (GLU) feed-forward blocks, a common component in modern language models. This technique extends previous extraction methods that did not cover GLU blocks.

title: Bypassing Krum: Selection-Aware Backdoor Attacks in Federated Learning
summary: This paper presents "Selection-Aware Backdoor Attacks" that can bypass robust aggregation methods like Krum in federated learning. It demonstrates a vulnerability in these systems, enabling adversarial clients to compromise model integrity.

title: Dueling World Models: Advantage-Style Action Channels for Common-Mode Distractor Rejection
summary: This paper introduces Dueling World Models, which utilize advantage-style action channels to address common-mode distractor rejection. This method improves latent world models' ability to distinguish predictions for different actions even when scenes contain uncontrolled motion.

title: Multi-Level Modeling of Large Language Model Inference Latency and Energy via Hybrid Analytical--Machine-Learning Predictors
summary: This paper introduces multi-level modeling using hybrid analytical-machine learning predictors to estimate and optimize the inference latency and energy consumption of Large Language Models (LLMs). The goal is to enhance sustainable AI deployment and hardware-aware design.

title: Solver-Guided Reasoning for Mixed-Equilibrium Strategies
summary: This paper proposes Solver-Guided Reasoning for Mixed-Equilibrium Strategies to enhance Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning in complex games. This method moves beyond human-centric data by integrating solvers to improve equilibrium reasoning.

title: CubicQuant: Parametric Non-Uniform Codebooks for High-Throughput LLM Inference with 1-8-Bit Weights
summary: Weight quantization for large-language-model inference must balance adaptive reconstruction levels with representations regular enough for efficient GPU execution. Uniform integers constrain each group to a linear grid. Low-bit floating-point formats use a fixed exponent-mantissa structure, while learned codebooks gain flexibility at the cost of irregular decoding and additional metadata. We introduce CubicQuant, a parametric non-uniform scalar format that preserves a dense integer code stream while adapting reconstruction levels within each weight group. A monotonic cubic curve, specified by two shape parameters and one scale, maps uniformly spaced magnitude codes to non-uniform levels. The family spans 1-8-bit weight payloads, contains symmetric uniform integer quantization as an exact special case, and has effective width B + 64/G bits per weight for payload width B and group size G. We derive population distortion under Uniform, Gaussian, and Laplace distributions, formulate continuous and Dynamic-A8-carrier-aware fitting objectives, and describe direct packed-weight GPU execution. For finite groups of G=128 with 15,360 samples per distribution, W4 CubicQuant reduced reconstruction RMSE relative to optimally clipped four-bit uniform integer quantization by 3.90% on Uniform, 13.49% on Gaussian, and 28.14% on Laplace samples. Relative to the best enumerated four-bit finite floating-point format, the reductions were 3.90%, 9.44%, and 6.27%. Preliminary H200 kernel measurements show a workload-dependent crossover: model-dtype execution is faster for narrow GEMV, while Dynamic A8 becomes favorable as row count grows. The results establish the format's representational promise and direct executability; downstream model quality and cross-device end-to-end performance remain open evaluation questions.

title: Hidden Gauge Controls Feature Specialization in ReLU Networks
summary: Training changes a network's predictions while allocating task-relevant structure across its internal units. In an overparameterized ReLU network, several neurons can begin with exactly the same functional role, yet one may acquire a teacher feature while the others become redundant. We call the identity of that neuron feature ownership and ask whether it can be controlled by a parameter choice invisible to the initial predictor. In a tractable Gaussian teacher--student model, we fix the complete initial function and vary only a positive-homogeneous scaling gauge. Opposite gauges produce distinct feature trajectories and a sharp $\Theta(D^2)$ separation in specialization time that no global change of clock can explain. Among any fixed number of initially duplicate students, assigning the favorable gauge to one neuron deterministically selects it as the owner and drives the remaining functional contribution to zero. An exact reaction--transport decomposition attributes the effect to different mobilities for changing a feature's coefficient and direction. We prove global selection and functional pruning, extend finite-time selection to visible perturbations and small-step full-batch gradient descent, and verify the predicted loss, alignment, pruning, and dissipation trajectories in population and finite-sample training. The initial predictor therefore determines neither when the feature is learned nor which neuron learns it.

title: ArchEGraph: A Large-Scale Graph Dataset for Geometry-Topology-Physics Aligned Building Energy Modeling
summary: Accurate estimation of building energy use is essential for achieving carbon neutral and sustainable buildings. To better understand the influence of design decisions on building energy use and calibrate machine learning models that can give architects and engineers rapid design feedback, large-scale datasets are needed that explicitly map building geometry to performance. We present ArchEGraph, a large-scale benchmark dataset that represents buildings as heterogeneous graphs with aligned geometry, topology, weather, and zone-level thermal loads.
