The dataset contains 5,481 buildings and 49,326 validated building-weather simulation cases. In total, it includes over 133,000 space nodes and 1.44 million face nodes, reflecting substantial geometric and topological complexity. Based on ArchEGraph, we define two benchmark tasks: (i) graph reconstruction from polygonal meshes, aiming to recover topological structure from geometric representations; and (ii) topology-informed load prediction, which leverages graph structure and temporal weather conditions to forecast zone-level response time series. We further introduce standardized evaluation protocols for both tasks and conduct cross-building and cross-climate generalization experiments to assess model robustness. ArchEGraph provides a unified testbed for studying geometry-topology-physics coupling in building energy modeling, enabling the development and evaluation of scalable and generalizable surrogate models.

title: Faster Query-Key Learning Sharpens Attention in Self-Attention Models
summary: A standard self-attention layer consists of two interacting circuits: the query-key circuit that governs attention allocation, and the output-value circuit that maps attended representations to predictions. Collapsed and factorized parameterizations of the query-key and output-value circuits lead to qualitatively different attention patterns. In particular, some parameterizations give sharper attention to task-relevant tokens, at a similar training loss. We analyze how the parameterizations of these circuits shape the parameter trajectories in single-layer self-attention models trained for next-token prediction. Through gradient-flow analysis, we show that factorization induces implicit rescaling of the two circuits' learning rates. We derive closed-form dynamics showing that output-value and query-key parameters move along a line, with relative speeds determined by their learning rates. Faster query-key learning relative to output-value learning thus produces sharper attention, as the model compensates for slower output-value learning by increasing attention mass on relevant tokens. Experiments show that differences in the relative learning rates of the two circuits govern attention concentration. This improves attention interpretability proxies while maintaining comparable predictive performance.

title: Understanding Differentiable Embeddings Through Differential and Integral Geometry
summary: How can an analyst decide whether a nonlinear dimensionality reduction embedding can be trusted? Existing diagnostics provide only partial answers: projection glyphs characterize local sensitivity, map-continuity scores measure local conditioning, and transport-based analyses reveal path-dependent inconsistencies. However, these methods appear unrelated and provide no common framework for understanding when they agree or not. We show that they are all derived from a single geometric object induced by every differentiable embedding, whether defined implicitly through optimization or explicitly by a learned mapping. This framework provides two complementary geometric views of an embedding. The differential view explains local behavior: its first-order term recovers projection glyphs, while its second-order curvature quantifies how far their linear approximation remains reliable. The integral view follows the same geometry along high dimensional paths and determines whether an embedding depends only on the current state or also on the path taken to reach it. We further show that map-continuity is a prerequisite for the other analyses. The framework is theoretically complete for diagnostics derived from the embedding geometry, and we prove the integral view irreducible: no amount of local measurement at any number of points, to any order of derivative, reproduces what it detects. Classical rank-based metrics form a complementary class based on finite-scale neighborhood relationships. Experiments on synthetic and real datasets validate theoretical predictions, demonstrate accurate curvature-based trust estimates on single-cell embeddings, and show that the integral analysis distinguishes single-valued embeddings from path-dependent optimization-based embeddings in ways that existing pointwise diagnostics cannot.

title: Graph Machine: Exploring Edge Mechanisms as an Inductive Bias
summary: Transformers provide a powerful architecture for global content-based matching, but reasoning problems may benefit from a stronger inductive bias toward iterative traversal of latent relations. We introduce Graph Machine, an architecture with two explicit edge-based mechanisms: Edge-augmented attention, in which edges modulate attention between nodes, and edge-centric referral, in which nodes exchange addresses to update their edges. Conceptually, this enables the model to dynamically and differentiably construct and revise relational graphs across layers. We study this inductive bias using Sudoku under controlled settings and find that Graph Machine outperforms Transformer baselines, with ablation studies and mechanistic analysis attributing the gains to the edge mechanisms. Surprisingly, we found that the model discovers a compact edge-based construction for Sudoku geometry. Our results support explicit edge mechanisms as a promising architectural design, motivating broader evaluation.

title: Mathematical Principles and Experimental Discoveries of the Emergence of Symbolic Patterns in Artificial Neural Networks
summary: Artificial Neural networks (ANNs) are often treated as black-box models, making explainability a central challenge in deep learning. Many engineering methods have been proposed to approximately explain the ANN from various perspectives, such as feature attribution and visualization. However, it remains a long-standing open question whether the complex inference logic of an ANN can be explained exhaustively and concisely as sparse symbolic patterns. This raises a deeper inquiry: does the emergence of symbolic patterns reflect a natural law rather than chance? Here, we show that across a broad class of ANNs trained on diverse tasks, their inference logic can indeed be reformulated as sparse symbolic interactions. We further prove that two common mathematical criteria, which are implicitly required across tasks, lead to the emergence of such sparse symbolic interactions. Empirical evidence confirms that the two criteria hold for the majority of input samples in diverse models. Furthermore, the faithfulness of these interactions is also demonstrated by their strong sample-to-sample and model-to-model transferability, as well as their ability to explain the overall generalization power of ANNs. Our theoretical analysis and extensive experiments provide a solid foundation for symbolic explanations of ANNs, and offer novel insights into the ANN's generalization power. Our findings also highlight the potential of communicative learning, a paradigm in which the inference logic of an ANN can be directly inspected and tuned at the level of symbolic patterns, thus complementing traditional end-to-end learning paradigm. Finally, the observed emergence of symbolic patterns in ANNs suggests that similar symbolic representations may also emerge in other types of black-box systems under certain conditions, because our proof does not depend on any specific ANN architecture.

title: Bridging the Gap Between Hyperdimensional Computing and Kernel Methods via the Nystr\"om Method
summary: Hyperdimensional computing (HDC) is an approach from the cognitive science literature for solving information processing tasks using data represented as high-dimensional random vectors. The technique has a rigorous mathematical backing, and is easy to implement in energy-efficient and highly parallel hardware like FPGAs and "processing-in-memory" architectures. The effectiveness of HDC in machine learning largely depends on how raw data is mapped to high-dimensional space. In this work, we propose NysHD, a new method for constructing this mapping that is based on the Nystr\"om method from the literature on kernel approximation. Our approach provides a simple recipe to turn any user-defined positive-semidefinite similarity function into an equivalent mapping in HDC. There is a vast literature on the design of such functions for learning problems. Our approach provides a mechanism to import them into the HDC setting, expanding the types of problems that can be tackled using HDC. Empirical evaluation against existing HDC encoding methods shows that NysHD can achieve, on average, 11% and 17% better classification accuracy on graph and string datasets respectively.

title: SkillAligner: Treating Retrieved Skills as Adaptable Drafts at Execution Time
summary: General-purpose skills promise reusable procedural knowledge for language agents, yet semantic relevance does not guarantee execution utility: a retrieved skill may encode assumptions that conflict with the current task, execution environment, or other retrieved skills. We formalize this problem as the skill--execution misfit. To address it, we propose SkillAligner, a training-free execution-time skill adaptation framework that treats retrieved skills as adaptable drafts rather than fixed instructions. Before execution, SkillAligner performs a one-time joint adaptation that specializes useful skill fragments to task requirements, aligns their procedural assumptions with the available execution interface, and composes the resulting guidance by resolving dependencies, conflicts, and redundancy across skills. The adapted content is consolidated into a compact execution guide and reused throughout the subsequent trajectory. Extensive experiments across diverse agent benchmarks and model backbones show that SkillAligner substantially improves task performance over existing skill-use baselines, reduces skill-induced regressions at the instance level, and lowers total inference cost.

title: Recent advances in weakly supervised learning: New supervision paradigms, assumption relaxations, and practical solutions
summary: Deep learning has achieved great success in recent years thanks to the availability of high-quality, well-annotated training data. However, this requirement is often not met in real-world applications. Weakly supervised learning aims to train an accurate model with incomplete, inexact, or inaccurate supervision. In this chapter, we will discuss recent advances in this field, including new supervision paradigms, relaxed assumptions, and practical solutions. First, we introduce a new weakly supervised binary classification problem called confidence-difference classification and propose consistent approaches to solve it. Next, we investigate complementary-label learning, a weakly supervised multi-class classification problem. Our proposed approaches are based on more relaxed assumptions about the data generation process than existing consistent approaches. Lastly, we present an evaluation framework for partial-label learning, another popular multi-class weakly supervised learning problem, in order to promote fair and realistic evaluation of algorithms in this field.

title: MiCoPro: End-to-End Mixed Precision HW/SW Co-design with HW-aware Proxy Model
summary: Quantized Neural Networks~(QNN) with low-bitwidth data have proven promising in efficient storage and computation on edge devices. To mitigate accuracy degradation while maximizing speedup, layer-wise mixed-precision quantization~(MPQ) becomes a popular solution. However, existing algorithms for exploring MPQ schemes are limited in flexibility and efficiency. Comprehending the complex impacts of different MPQ schemes on post-training quantization and quantization-aware training results is a challenge for conventional methods. Furthermore, an end-to-end framework for the optimization and deployment of MPQ models is missing in existing work. To address these challenges, we propose the MiCo framework, a holistic MPQ exploration and deployment framework for edge AI applications. The framework adopts a novel optimization algorithm to search for accuracy-optimal quantization configurations under strict latency constraints. We further extended the framework to MiCoPro, which introduces a robust Hardware-Aware Proxy (HAP) model to enhance prediction accuracy and hardware versatility. By leveraging target-specific latency modeling, MiCoPro enables rapid exploration and direct deployment from PyTorch models to bare-metal C code. We demonstrate the versatility of our framework on both the BitFusion accelerator and SIMD-extended RISC-V processors, achieving up to 40\% of latency reduction with less than 3\% of accuracy drop.

title: Walkable to Whom? Capturing Subjective Variability in Walkability Perception Using Multimodal Deep Learning
summary: Visual perception of walkability varies substantially across individuals, reflecting differences in personal characteristics, experiences, and preferences. Existing studies, however, often reduce these diverse judgements to aggregated scores, implicitly assuming uniform perception, and commonly rely on vehicle-mounted street-view imagery that does not reflect the pedestrian's visual experience. This paper introduces a dataset of 29,870 walkability ratings from 1,196 respondents, linking sidewalk-view imagery across urban, suburban, and regional Australian environments with individual rater attributes, and proposes the first user-conditioned multimodal deep learning framework for walkability perception, fusing visual features with respondent-level representations. A viewpoint-comparison study shows that sidewalk-view images receive significantly higher walkability ratings than matched street-view images, indicating that imagery source is a substantive design decision in perception surveys. The user-conditioned model improves rank agreement with observed ratings by 65% over an image-only baseline (quadratic weighted kappa 0.47 vs. 0.29), demonstrating that who is evaluating an environment carries predictive indication beyond image content alone. These findings support moving from aggregated, observer-independent walkability scores toward models that represent diverse users, enabling more inclusive assessment of pedestrian environments.

title: ELMZip: Onboard Satellite Image Compression via Extreme Learning Machines for Efficient Downlink
summary: The acquisition of multispectral imagery via small satellites (e.g., CubeSats) presents significant data downlink challenges due to high data volumes and restricted communication windows. While onboard image compression is critical to address this bottleneck, traditional methods often struggle to adapt to the nonlinear statistics of multi-band, multi-resolution data. To overcome these limitations, we propose ELMZip, a novel framework based on Extreme Learning Machines (ELM) and domain decomposition strategies for efficient, resolution-free onboard neural representation. ELMZip formulates the fitting process as a convex least-squares problem using random-feature single-layer networks, thereby eliminating the need for computationally expensive backpropagation. By adopting an asymmetric transmission protocol that sends only the compact output weights, the proposed method significantly reduces the downlink payload. Unlike previous neural representation approaches that rely on iterative optimization and require transmitting full network parameters, ELMZip achieves significant compression efficiency while maintaining high reconstruction fidelity. This capability enables immediate image reconstruction for analysis, allowing resource-constrained platforms to maximize data return and advancing real-time AI-powered Earth observation.

title: How Molecular Generative Models Organize Molecular Identity
summary: Generative models for matter are often evaluated as samplers over output representations, and their latent spaces are commonly used as proxies for navigating chemical space. Much less is known about how these models internally arrange discrete chemical identities within those representations. We study this arrangement by making molecular identity explicit and pulling it back through the generative process. Through these pullbacks we probe the regions that generate the same object, exposing the trained model's internal repertoire: a fixed partition that determines which objects (novel or not) the model can produce. Across three molecular generative architectures, we find that this repertoire is arranged into piecewise-constant regions separated by recurring coarse-to-fine boundaries. Its organization depends on the representation probed, the identity convention, decoder stochasticity, and the metric used to compare coordinates. During training, local chemical organization stabilizes while the number of distinct molecular identities represented within each neighborhood continues to change. Internal organization must therefore be characterized, rather than assumed, before a generative space can be treated as chemically navigable.

title: Beyond Foundation Models: Dimension-Aware Neural Architecture Search with Small-Data Representation Models for Cryocooler Lifetime Prediction
summary: Large-scale pretrained time-series models achieve strong results through large-scale pretraining and task-agnostic representation learning, but they rely on abundant, diverse data that industrial and scientific domains often lack. We therefore propose the FSD-RM (Family of Small-Data Representation Models) paradigm as a practical alternative for limited, domain-specific telemetry. Rather than relying on large-scale pretraining, we focus on capacity-controlled representation learning using established encoder architectures (CNN1D, LSTM, GRU, Transformer), selected for their suitability in small-data settings and interpretability. These encoders are trained unsupervised on multivariate telemetry data and integrated into a two-stage pipeline for downstream lifetime prediction. To systematically examine architectural trade-offs under data constraints, we employ \textbf{dimension-aware neural architecture search (NAS)} to jointly optimize model capacity and input dimensionality. Experiments on cryocooler telemetry show that the proposed approach achieves competitive predictive performance while reducing training cost and model complexity. The contribution lies in combining established representation learning techniques within a coherent, NAS-driven framework tailored to small-data regimes, with explicitly defined parameter settings and design choices. The results indicate that effective representation learning can be achieved without large-scale pretraining when appropriate inductive bias and capacity control are applied.

title: Every Cache Entry Earns Its Place: Global Allocation of Resolution and Coverage for KV Cache Compression
summary: As large language models (LLMs) process increasingly long contexts, KV cache storage and repeated access have become a major bottleneck. Existing KV cache compression methods rely on predefined, fixed compression rules and are typically developed around either token eviction or merging. As a result, cache resources can neither flow freely across layers, heads, and context slots, nor be jointly allocated to balance local resolution and information coverage. Therefore, we propose GraceKV, a global approach for the allocation of resolution and coverage in KV cache compression, and formulate the compression process as a global resource allocation problem under a fixed cache budget. GraceKV treats each layer-KV head-slot combination as an atomic unit and builds a prototype tree. Leaf nodes correspond to token-level KV entries, while each internal node uses a single prototype to compress the KV space covered by its children. A set of non-overlapping nodes in the tree forms the representation of an atomic unit. Adding the root of a new tree expands information coverage, whereas splitting a selected node improves local resolution. All candidate actions compete globally for a shared cache budget. Finally, the nodes retained across all trees form the compressed KV cache. This process adaptively determines the allocation of cache resources among atomic units globally and the balance between resolution and coverage. GraceKV requires no additional training, and the entire compression and inference process is performed on the GPU. Systematic experiments across diverse long-context tasks and compression ratios show that GraceKV ranks first in 24 of 32 settings and remains robust up to 128-fold compression. These results validate the effectiveness of global budget allocation in coordinating information coverage and local resolution.

title: Hyperbolic Graph Embedders for Link Prediction and Topology Reconstruction
summary: Hyperbolic embeddings provide compact geometric representations of complex networks in hyperbolic spaces, but systematic comparisons of methods developed in machine learning, network science, and algorithmics remain rare. We benchmark 13 unsupervised hyperbolic graph embedders under a unified protocol for link prediction and topology reconstruction on synthetic and empirical networks. The protocol captures both missing-link recovery and the preservation of local and global network structure. Maximum-likelihood and representation-learning-based approaches, including hybrid variants, achieve the strongest overall performance, although no method dominates across all tasks and structural regimes. Performance is more strongly associated with embedding paradigm than with disciplinary origin. We identify the network regimes in which different paradigms succeed or fail and provide practical guidance for method selection in downstream applications.

title: Accounting Graph Transformer for Short-History Multi-KPI Forecasting in Small Businesses
summary: Small businesses often have only 12-24 months of accounting history, yet planning and risk workflows require coordinated forecasts across financial statements. We study joint 12-month forecasting of 13 income-statement, balance-sheet, cash-flow, and working-capital key performance indicators (KPIs) from 71 monthly ledger series. We introduce the Accounting Graph Transformer (AGT), which represents each ledger series as a masked token, exchanges information through typed attention on a fixed accounting-relation graph, pools target-specific context, and fuses it with a gated three-month recency path. Across 11,993 forecast origins from 1,060 unseen companies, AGT achieves sample-weighted KPI-macro mean absolute error (MAE) $0.6990 \pm 0.0013$ over three independent seeds, compared with $0.7378 \pm 0.0014$ for the strongest baseline, LightGBM. At the pre-specified seed 42, a paired company-clustered bootstrap gives a LightGBM-minus-AGT difference of 0.0395 with 95% confidence interval (CI) $[0.0350,0.0439]$. AGT is best on all 13 KPIs against LightGBM, TimeMixer, and SOFTS in the matched seed-42 comparison, while final-architecture ablations show that relational attention, accounting topology, and the recency path each improve validation and test accuracy. On 7,094 additional unseen companies with origins sampled from January-May 2025, AGT obtains 0.7548 MAE versus 0.7694 for SOFTS. A single 5.3M-parameter model produces 156 aligned forecasts without company-specific fitting, providing one forecasting layer for integrated planning, liquidity, and working-capital analysis.

title: Beyond Isolation: Unlocking Reinforcement Learning Component Synergy for Sample-Efficient Continuous Control
summary: Reinforcement learning systems are significantly more complex than other machine learning paradigms due to inherent properties, causing RL system design to jointly account for many tightly coupled factors. Despite advances in individual algorithmic components, their functional interdependencies remain underexplored: do they exhibit mutual synergy or counterproductive interference? To bridge this gap, we conduct a systematic investigation and find that the efficacy of different components exhibits significant task-dependency, and naively stacking state-of-the-art techniques does not necessarily yield performance gains; instead, it often triggers emergent challenges, such as compounded non-stationarity. Building upon these findings, we distill a suite of actionable insights into the principled coordination of these components. Guided by these insights, we propose ROSER, an RL framework that coordinates three critical dimensions: Model-based Representation, Optimization Stability, and Experience Replay. Across diverse continuous-control benchmarks, ROSER consistently outperforms vanilla baselines and achieves 17.60% gains over naive stack. Our findings underscore the necessity of a holistic perspective in RL system design and paves the way for developing sample-efficient agents.

title: Synthetic LiDAR Data Generation and Deterministic Downsampling for Point Cloud Classification on the Edge
summary: Deploying three-dimensional deep learning frameworks to low-power embedded processors is bottlenecked by the unstructured nature of spatial data and the resource-intensive distance sorting algorithms often used before neural network inference. To address this gap, this paper presents a hardware-constrained workflow optimized for native execution on the Raspberry Pi 5. To account for the reality gap between noiseless, clean computer-aided design (CAD) datasets and real-world sensor data, we use physics-based simulation to construct a synthetic LiDAR dataset. Cross-dataset evaluations demonstrate a substantial drop in classification accuracy when networks trained on clean CAD data are evaluated on synthetic LiDAR sensor data, highlighting the critical need for sensor-aware training. To address the latency bottleneck of traditional geometric preprocessing on edge CPUs, we integrate an isolated, feature-driven Critical Points Layer (CPL) as a frontend filter. Our results show that the pretrained CPL deterministically compresses raw 1024-point clouds to a subset of 40 to 60 unique coordinates. When profiled on the ARM Cortex-A76 processor, the complete pipeline achieves an inference throughput of approximately 50 FPS while maintaining an instance classification accuracy of 88.36%, demonstrating the viability of deterministic real-time 3D perception at the edge.

title: Online Conformal Prediction Beyond Feedback
summary: This research explores online conformal prediction, a method for uncertainty quantification in machine learning models deployed in safety-critical applications, for arbitrary black-box classifiers and non-i.i.d. data streams.

title: Interpretable reinforcement learning with decision-tree pruning
summary: This paper presents a pruning method to improve the interpretability of reinforcement learning policies by converting trained policies into more transparent decision-tree rules.

title: TEXAS: Task-Expert-Aware Supervision for Downstream Mixture-of-Experts LLM Adaptation
summary: This research introduces TEXAS, a method for Task-Expert-Aware Supervision, to enhance the adaptation of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Large Language Models by addressing limitations in identifying task-relevant experts.

title: Separating Decision-Rule Misalignment from Readout-Coverage Limitations in Speech Language Models
summary: This paper introduces a generation-aligned diagnostic ladder to evaluate speech language models, helping to differentiate between decision-rule misalignment and readout-coverage limitations in paralinguistic tasks.

title: NTDH: Complex Reasoning for Comprehensive Affective Analysis
summary: This research proposes NTDH, a method for complex reasoning in comprehensive affective analysis, tackling challenges like heterogeneous prediction tasks and context-dependent affective meaning.

title: Recovering Lesion Parameters from Aphasic Picture Naming Error Profiles in Large Language Models
summary: This study uses lesioning methods on Large Language Models to produce error profiles similar to aphasia in picture naming, aiming to understand if internal model states causally explain observed behaviors.

title: Do AI Personas Grow? Analyzing and Benchmarking Personality Evolution in LLM Agents After Life Events
summary: This research analyzes and benchmarks personality evolution in LLM agents after life events, investigating whether AI personas can grow and remain coherent over extended interactions.

title: ConstructCIE: A Dataset for Extracting Causal Information from Construction Accident Narratives
summary: This paper introduces ConstructCIE, a manually annotated dataset designed for extracting causal information from construction accident narratives in OSHA reports, despite implicit and distributed evidence.

title: Measuring the Cross-Lingual Comprehension Gap: How the language of the evidence shapes what language models understand
summary: This research measures the cross-lingual comprehension gap in language models, assessing how the language of evidence affects their understanding when content is presented in different languages.

title: GRASP: Reinforcing Language Model Anonymizers with Group Relative Policy Optimization
summary: This paper introduces GRASP, a method that reinforces language model anonymizers with Group Relative Policy Optimization to defend against privacy risks by rewriting text to conceal sensitive personal attributes.

title: Lost in Interpolation: Why Predictive Feedback Fails in Diffusion Language Models
summary: This analysis investigates why predictive feedback fails in Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs), attributing it to linear interpolation in the raw embedding space that incorrectly treats it as Euclidean.

title: Confidence Estimation for Financial Vision-Language Models in Chart and Document Understanding
summary: This research focuses on confidence estimation for Financial Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) used in chart and document understanding, emphasizing trust in model outputs over mere accuracy due to high stakes.

title: Don't `Well, Actually' Me Unless You Know What You're Talking About: Weak Presupposition Verification Degrades General QA Performance
summary: This study examines how weak presupposition verification degrades general QA performance in LLMs, highlighting their inability to identify and correct false presuppositions in questions.

title: TradeVerse: A Longitudinal Benchmark of Political Negotiation in International Trade
summary: This paper introduces TradeVerse, a new longitudinal benchmark designed to evaluate Large Language Models on their performance in political negotiation tasks within international trade scenarios.

title: Beyond "AI Language": The case for the idiolectal nature of LLM output
summary: This chapter argues that Large Language Model (LLM) outputs possess distinct, model-specific linguistic signatures, akin to human idiolects, rather than being a collective 'AI language'.

title: Pre-Inference Routing for Cost-Efficient Document Field Extraction
summary: This research explores pre-inference routing for document field extraction, using inexpensive document-based signals to predict difficulty and choose the most cost-efficient model before extraction.

title: The Horizon Gap: Planning, Memory, Execution, Training, and Evaluation for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: This paper identifies and surveys 'The Horizon Gap,' a major challenge for Long-Horizon LLM Agents, detailing failures in planning, memory, execution, training, and evaluation for multi-hour tasks.

title: TA-RAG: Tone Awareness as a Design Imperative for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: This paper proposes TA-RAG, an approach to Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) that incorporates 'tone awareness' as a design imperative to handle varied communication styles in retrieved documents for LLMs.

title: Do Audio Language Models Use Paralinguistic Evidence? Counterfactual Audits for Response Evaluation
summary: This research uses counterfactual audits to investigate whether Audio Language Models (ALMs) actually utilize paralinguistic evidence when acting as judges for speech-to-speech systems.

title: Progressive Content Refinement with Decaying Reward Joint LinUCB
summary: This paper introduces a novel method for progressive content refinement using Decaying Reward Joint LinUCB, aiming to improve Large Language Model performance by addressing limitations of existing iterative refinement techniques.

title: Stockmark-Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-JapanDocReader: Structured Document Parsing via Capability Injection and Forgetting Control
summary: This paper introduces Stockmark-Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-JapanDocReader, a new Japanese document understanding model built from Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning-BF16. Its goal is structured document parsing through capability injection and forgetting control.

title: Multi-Perspective Triad Interaction Graph Neural Network for Cognitive Distortion Detection
summary: This paper proposes MTI-GNN, a Multi-Perspective Triad Interaction Graph Neural Network, designed for cognitive distortion detection in computational mental health. It models Beck's cognitive triad to address psychological structure in distorted thoughts.

title: FutureBridge: Token Selection Beyond Local Preference in Collaborative Decoding
summary: FutureBridge is a method that enhances collaborative decoding, allowing an LLM to assist an SLM by selecting tokens beyond local preferences when their predictions diverge. It aims to improve the interaction between language models.

title: Autonomy-of-Heads: Data-Free Sparse Attention from Frozen Query-Key Geometry
summary: Autonomy-of-Heads proposes a data-free sparse attention method derived from frozen query-key geometry to mitigate the quadratic attention computation and KV-cache costs in long-context LLM inference.

title: LLMRouter: Unified Infrastructure for Developing, Evaluating, and Deploying LLM Routers
summary: LLMRouter is a unified infrastructure designed for developing, evaluating, and deploying LLM routers, which are essential for cost-effective model deployment. It aims to streamline the comparison and extension of diverse model routing strategies.

title: Georeferencing Non-Gazetteered Place Names using Biological Specimen Records
summary: This research focuses on georeferencing non-gazetteered place names by utilizing biological specimen records from natural history institutions. It uses digitized data from the Allan Herbarium to capture temporal geographic and biodiversity information.

title: Calibrating WEAT Against Anisotropy: ZCA Whitening as a Geometric Pre-Processing Step for Embedding Association Tests
summary: This paper proposes Zero-phase Component Analysis (ZCA) whitening as a geometric pre-processing step to calibrate the Word Embedding Association Test (WEAT). It aims to improve WEAT, a widely used method for measuring bias in AI fairness research.

title: Ask-E: An Environment for Calibrated Question Generation
summary: Ask-E is an environment developed for calibrated question generation, aiming to create challenging problems that probe model limits and aid in evaluation. It supports generating questions at a precise difficulty level for model improvement.

title: Can Language Models Imagine Without Seeing? Ekphrasis: Measuring Visual Creative Ideation in Text-Only LLMs
summary: Ekphrasis is a new method designed to measure visual creative ideation specifically in text-only Large Language Models. It aims to assess whether LLMs can originate visual concepts independently of image generation, addressing limitations in current evaluations.

title: PHASE-Tree: Modeling Character-State Evolution in Long-Horizon Role-Playing Dialogue
summary: PHASE-Tree is a model designed to address character-state evolution in long-horizon role-playing dialogue, allowing characters to remain consistent while evolving with the narrative. It aims to improve upon static character profiles in AI-driven storytelling.

title: Confirming Our Biases? Evaluating the Capabilities, Risks, and Societal Impact of Large Language Models
summary: This study investigates the extent to which Large Language Models reinforce user biases stemming from prompt framing. It examines the boundary between implicit and explicit biases in LLM interactions and their societal impact.

title: GPTKB 2.0: Browsing, Querying, and Auditing a Disambiguated LLM-Derived Knowledge Base
summary: GPTKB 2.0 is a large-scale disambiguated knowledge base materialized from an LLM, containing millions of triples and entities. A web demo allows for browsing, querying, and auditing this knowledge base, which aids in AI information storage and retrieval.

title: Does More Retrieved Evidence Help Visual Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Diffusion Language Models?
summary: This research investigates whether expanding retrieved evidence in Visual Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) benefits Diffusion Language Models (DLMs). It challenges the assumption that more retrieved evidence always improves performance for DLMs.

title: An Agentic Hybrid Top-Down and Bottom-Up Approach to Knowledge Graph Generation
summary: This paper proposes an agentic hybrid approach for knowledge graph generation to address the challenge of organizing multilingual expertise declarations for HR platforms. This pipeline grounds a large language model to improve talent matching.

title: HNR-DAC: Hard-Negative Reranking and Distribution-Aligned Classification for Scientific Claim Verification
summary: HNR-DAC (Hard-Negative Reranking and Distribution-Aligned Classification) is a proposed method for scientific claim verification over cited papers. It aims to predict claim-paper relations and identify justifying paragraphs, addressing challenges like within-paper distractors.

title: Measuring Concept Content in Text from LLM Activations: ESG Evidence from Concept Vectors and Linear Probes
summary: This research presents methods for measuring concept content in text directly from LLM activations, utilizing concept vectors and linear probes. It aims to capture what an LLM 'judges' a text to be about, beyond surface-level analysis.

title: From Test-Time Scaling to Reusable Memory: Measuring Crystallization in Text-to-SQL
summary: This paper explores the concept of 'crystallization' in Text-to-SQL systems, focusing on reusable memory for retaining verified repair episodes. It examines how systems can benefit from recalling past solutions to recurring queries, rather than discarding computation.

title: Skaling: Chinchilla's Exponents Meet Kaplan's Coupling
summary: Skaling proposes a new formulation for neural scaling laws that addresses systematic under- and overestimation of loss at data-scarce and overtraining extremes. It improves upon existing assumptions about how model size and training data impact loss.

title: Stoicheia: Character-Level Masked Diffusion for Ancient Greek Textual Restoration, Parsing, and Metrical Scansion
summary: Stoicheia is a 405M-parameter character-level masked-diffusion encoder model designed for Ancient Greek textual restoration, parsing, and metrical scansion. It processes input across five independently maskable planes, including letters and linguistic features.

title: Why Knowing Both Hops Is Not Enough: Understanding Two-Hop Generalization in Language Models
summary: This research investigates why Large Language Models (LLMs) struggle with two-hop generalization despite correctly storing individual hops. It aims to understand the internal mechanisms behind these puzzling failures in combining information for multi-hop queries.

title: Gaze Behavior in Visual World Experiments Can be Modeled With Off-the-shelf Language-Vision Encoders
summary: This paper explores how off-the-shelf language-vision encoders can model gaze behavior in human language processing, investigating whether neural LMs are promising models for understanding human cognitive processes.

title: Grammar Engineering Meets LLMs: Development of Cantonese and Irish ParGram Treebanks
summary: This research details the development of Cantonese and Irish ParGram treebanks, demonstrating how grammar engineering can leverage LLMs for linguistic formalism and computational implementation while balancing cross-linguistic consistency.

title: Natural Language Processing Psychometrics
summary: This paper introduces NLP Psychometrics, a framework that treats psychological prediction from text as a psychometric problem, linking NLP model scores to interpretable linguistic features for mental health outcomes.

title: Geo-Spatial Concept Probing of Large Language Models: Abstraction, Compositionality, and Grounding
summary: This research investigates the conceptual understanding of Large Language Models (LLMs) through geo-spatial concept probing, focusing on abstraction, compositionality, and grounding. It aims to evaluate why LLMs struggle with genuine concept understanding.

title: LitTraceQA: A Benchmark for Multi-Stage Grounding and Verification in Scientific Question Answering
summary: LitTraceQA is introduced as a new benchmark designed for evaluating multi-stage grounding and verification in scientific question answering systems, including language models and Retrieval-Augmented Generation.

title: An Exploratory Evaluation of LLM-Assisted Rewriting of Moderate-Complexity Financial Sentences for DisCoCat-Based Sentiment Analysis
summary: This paper presents an exploratory evaluation of using LLM-assisted rewriting for moderate-complexity financial sentences to improve DisCoCat-based sentiment analysis, addressing practical limitations of the framework.

title: CoinRAG: Contextualized Information Nugget KV Cache Reuse for Long-Context RAG
summary: CoinRAG introduces a novel optimization technique for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) by utilizing contextualized information nugget KV cache reuse for long contexts. This method aims to improve RAG efficiency by reducing redundancy and noise.

title: CreativeInstruct: Scalably Teaching LLMs to Balance Quality, Creativity, and Diversity
summary: CreativeInstruct is a method designed to scalably teach Large Language Models (LLMs) to balance output quality, creativity, and diversity during post-training. It aims to mitigate the common issue of reduced creativity after training.

title: Multi Codec Discrete Diffusion Model for Text Guided Speech Inpainting and Editing
summary: This paper introduces a multi-codec discrete diffusion model specifically designed for text-guided speech inpainting and editing tasks. The model aims to reconstruct missing or corrupted speech segments and modify spoken content.

title: StepJack: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agent Safety Against Multi-Step Indirect Prompt Injection
summary: StepJack introduces a new benchmark to evaluate the safety of computer-use agents (CUAs) against multi-step indirect prompt injection attacks. It focuses on a novel attack class where adversarial instructions are planted in the environment.

title: Model Confidence Under Answer-Preserving Attacks: An Informativeness-Manipulability Frontier
summary: This research investigates model confidence in vision-language systems under answer-preserving white-box attacks, exploring the informativeness-manipulability frontier. It examines the robustness of confidence readouts and their relevance for AI system oversight.

title: Online Monitoring and Corrective Steering of Programming Agents
summary: This paper presents methods for online monitoring and corrective steering of programming agents, aimed at improving their efficiency and reliability in tasks like fixing GitHub issues. The research addresses challenges in long-horizon agent trajectories.

title: UAV3DCrop: Benchmarking 3D Reconstruction in Repeated Multi-Angle UAV Crop Surveys
summary: UAV3DCrop introduces a benchmark for evaluating 3D reconstruction methods specifically for repeated multi-angle UAV crop surveys in precision agriculture. It aims to provide accurate 3D crop monitoring for analysis of plant structure and growth dynamics.

title: Deep Evidential Regression for Sparse Forest Height Estimation from Multimodal Satellite Imagery
summary: This paper proposes Deep Evidential Regression for sparse forest height estimation using multimodal satellite imagery, addressing the challenge of quantifying predictive uncertainty in deep learning approaches for environmental applications.

title: TransSLR: A Lightweight Transformer for Sign Language Recognition
summary: TransSLR introduces a lightweight Transformer model designed for automated Sign Language Recognition, particularly focusing on under-represented languages like Central African Sign Language to improve accuracy in this domain.

title: Test-Time Adaptation with Online Personalized Energy-Based Cache for Fine-Grained Video Expression Recognition
summary: This research proposes a method for test-time adaptation using an online personalized energy-based cache to improve fine-grained video expression recognition. The approach aims to address challenges in identifying subtle and temporally evolving affective states.

title: Improving Low-Resolution Face Recognition under Limited Data: How Synthetic Data Generation Can Close the Domain Gap
summary: This paper explores how synthetic data generation can improve low-resolution face recognition by closing the domain gap when labeled native-LR data is limited. It addresses the challenges of face recognition systems in surveillance settings.

title: SLED: Scalable Location Encoding via Distillation
summary: SLED introduces a method for scalable location encoding via distillation, aimed at learning high-quality representations from vast amounts of geospatial data and Earth Observations. This technique addresses challenges posed by the size and diverse modalities of environmental data.

title: Do 3D Medical Foundation Models See Through MRI Artifacts? A Controlled Study of Representation Robustness
summary: This paper presents a controlled study evaluating the representation robustness of self-supervised 3D medical foundation models against MRI artifacts. It aims to understand the sensitivity of these general-purpose feature extractors to imaging discrepancies.

title: When Semantics Saturate or Emerge: Adaptation-Conditional Semantic Utility in Source-Free Cross-Domain Few-Shot Learning
summary: This paper investigates the validity of language description rankings in source-free cross-domain few-shot learning after target-domain visual adaptation, specifically with vision-language models. It examines how semantic utility changes during adaptation under a paired protocol.

title: Corrupting Attention: Evasion-Based Adversarial Attacks on Encoder Attention in Detection Transformers
summary: This research explores evasion-based adversarial attacks targeting encoder attention mechanisms in detection transformers, highlighting vulnerabilities in object detection models. The paper addresses concerns about the safe deployment and robustness of neural networks against such attacks.

title: CoDAT: Collaborative Dual-Attention Transformer with Low-Cost Temporal Modeling for Efficient Edge Action Recognition
summary: This paper introduces CoDAT, a collaborative dual-attention transformer designed for low-cost temporal modeling, enabling efficient real-time human action recognition. The model is optimized for deployment on Internet-of-Things (IoT) edge devices with strict resource constraints.

title: WaveFreqAnchor: Wave-Structural Anchoring and Frequency Correction Diffusion for Training-Free Face Restoration
summary: This paper introduces WaveFreqAnchor, a training-free method for face restoration using diffusion models that employs wave-structural anchoring and frequency correction. It addresses issues of structural drift and degraded fidelity in existing diffusion-based face restoration under severe conditions.

title: Beyond Starry Night: Shortcut-Aware Control-State Planning for Artist-Grounded Text to Image Generation
summary: This research presents a method for 'shortcut-aware control-state planning' to improve artist-grounded text-to-image generation, moving beyond models' reliance on generic artist-specific shortcuts. The goal is to generate images that better preserve the user's intended scene and artistic style.

title: Explore or Converge? Stage-Guided Per-Step Optimization for Diffusion Models
summary: This paper explores 'stage-guided per-step optimization' for diffusion models, utilizing reinforcement learning to align their generative capabilities with specific user preferences. The method aims to overcome the limitations of maximum likelihood training in achieving desired outcomes.

title: GraphVerse: A Comprehensive Visual Graph Reasoning Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces GraphVerse, a new comprehensive visual graph reasoning benchmark designed to evaluate the ability of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to reason over structured visual information. It aims to address the limitations of existing evaluations in assessing true reasoning capabilities.

title: UniCycleFlow: Bidirectional Unpaired Image Translation with a Shared Rectified Flow
summary: This paper proposes UniCycleFlow, a new method for bidirectional unpaired image translation that utilizes a shared rectified flow to preserve source-specific structures. It aims to learn coherent transformations in both directions without requiring paired supervision, improving upon existing approaches.

title: PAST: Prompt-Adaptive Sampling Termination for Efficient Diffusion Model
summary: This paper introduces PAST (Prompt-Adaptive Sampling Termination), a method to improve the efficiency of diffusion models for text-to-image tasks. It aims to optimize downstream objectives and address the low efficiency of existing fine-tuning methods using reinforcement learning.

title: AdvTiles: Physical Adversarial Camouflage Clothing against Person Detectors via Learnable Tiles
summary: This research introduces AdvTiles, a method for generating physical adversarial camouflage clothing using learnable tiles to effectively attack person detectors. It addresses the challenge of achieving both visual naturalness and strong attack effectiveness in physical adversarial attacks.

title: Bend the Basics: Degradation-Aware Deformable Tokenization for All-in-One Image Restoration
summary: This paper proposes 'Degradation-Aware Deformable Tokenization' for all-in-one image restoration, aiming to develop a single model capable of recovering images degraded by diverse corruptions. The method addresses limitations of fixed patch partitioning in unified Transformer models.

title: GOPI: Generation-Oriented 3D Pose Inference for Furniture Insertion from Single-View RGB-D Indoor Scenes
summary: This paper presents GOPI, a generation-oriented method for 3D pose inference, enabling the insertion of new furniture into indoor scene images from single-view RGB-D inputs. The approach addresses the challenge of physically grounded furniture placement when scale is underdetermined.

title: RegionDet: A Benchmark for Region Detection Beyond Object Instances
summary: This paper introduces RegionDet, a new benchmark for region detection designed to evaluate computer vision models' ability to localize visual targets beyond discrete object instances. It focuses on detecting regions defined by visual states or scene characteristics.

title: Multi-Agent Forensic Reasoning for Generalizable Deepfake Video Detection
summary: This research proposes a 'Multi-Agent Forensic Reasoning' approach for generalizable deepfake video detection, aiming to counter the malicious use of generative AI. The method addresses limitations in existing deepfake benchmarks and enhances detection reliability.

title: DAEP: Difficulty-Aware Evidence Planning for Medical Video Corpus Temporal Answer Grounding
summary: This paper describes DAEP, a 'Difficulty-Aware Evidence Planning' method developed for medical video corpus temporal answer grounding as part of a shared task. The system retrieves target videos and localizes answer-supporting spans by ranking videos using subtitle and visual cues.

title: FedVAR: Prototype-Aligned Federated Framework for Video Anomaly Recognition
summary: This paper introduces FedVAR, a prototype-aligned federated framework designed for video anomaly recognition (VAR) in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS). The framework utilizes federated learning for decentralized intelligence to enhance safety and maintain digital twins.

title: ControlRef: Efficient Layout-Guided Multi-Instance Generation via Anchored 4D-RoPE
summary: This paper proposes ControlRef, an efficient method for layout-guided multi-instance generation in Multi-Modal Diffusion Transformers (MM-DiTs) using anchored 4D-RoPE. It aims to improve controllable image synthesis by addressing challenges in integrating this capability into unified architectures.

title: HazeSpikeMamba: Coupling Spiking-Inspired and State-Space Features for Self-Supervised Real-World Dehazing
summary: This paper introduces HazeSpikeMamba, a novel model for self-supervised real-world dehazing that couples spiking-inspired and state-space features. The model addresses the performance drop of dehazing networks when applied to real photographs compared to synthetic data.

title: Prune Once: Retraining-Free Task-Agnostic Pruning for Vision-Language Models
summary: This paper introduces 'Prune Once,' a retraining-free and task-agnostic pruning method designed to reduce the computational and memory requirements of Vision-Language Models (VLMs). The technique aims to facilitate the deployment of VLMs in constrained environments by improving their efficiency.

title: MuST-VAD: Mutual Structured Learning for Video Anomaly Detection
summary: This paper proposes MuST-VAD, a mutual structured learning framework for weakly supervised video anomaly detection (VAD), where an anomaly detector and a large vision-language model (LVLM) exchange knowledge. The framework aims to improve anomaly score learning from features in VAD.

title: Vernata: Self-Supervised Learning of LiDAR Point Representations
summary: This research introduces Vernata, a self-supervised learning method for LiDAR point representations, addressing the scarcity of labeled 3D data for deep learning models used by outdoor robots.

title: MaskFlow: Precise, Consistent and Seamless Regional Image Editing
summary: MaskFlow is presented as a new method for precise, consistent, and seamless regional image editing, overcoming challenges in localized and natural edits despite strong semantic alignment.

title: AVCap: Reinforcing Audio-Video Joint Caption with Detail-Aware Reward
summary: AVCap proposes a new method for reinforcing audio-video joint captioning with detail-aware reward, essential for multimodal video understanding and generation, by addressing dataset scarcity and limitations of prior reinforcement learning.

title: Debias in Text, Believe Your Eyes: Text-Anchored Cross-Modal Transfer for Visual Counter-Commonsense Reasoning
summary: This research explores enhancing visual counter-commonsense reasoning in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) by leveraging text-anchored cross-modal transfer, focusing on reasoning beyond common assumptions.

title: Degradation-Aware Prompt Learning with Cross-Modal Compensation for Adverse Weather Removal
summary: This paper introduces degradation-aware prompt learning with cross-modal compensation to improve the removal of adverse weather effects in images, addressing the limitations of existing all-in-one restoration models.

title: Dual-Space Modality Consistency Learning for Universal Cross-Modal Re-Identification
summary: This research proposes a dual-space modality consistency learning method for universal cross-modal re-identification, aiming to retrieve identities across heterogeneous imaging modalities like visible-infrared person and cross-modal ship ReID.

title: Summarize First, Download Later: Onboard VLMs for Bandwidth-Efficient Earth Observation
summary: This research investigates the use of onboard Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for bandwidth-efficient Earth observation, allowing satellites to summarize data before download to overcome downlink capacity bottlenecks.

title: Generative Embedding Benchmark: How Much Information Survives in a Dense Embedding?
summary: This work introduces a Generative Embedding Benchmark to assess the amount of information retained in dense embeddings, moving beyond discriminative tasks and geometric criteria for evaluation.

title: When One Modality Is Not Enough: Multimodal Sex and Life-Stage Classification of Red Deer from Aerial RGB-Thermal Video
summary: This research demonstrates a multimodal AI approach for classifying the sex and life-stage of red deer from aerial RGB-thermal video, improving wildlife population estimation beyond simple counting.

title: Local Epistemic Uncertainty Guided Active Sampling for Plug-and-play Diffusive Image Restoration
summary: This paper presents a method using local epistemic uncertainty-guided active sampling to improve plug-and-play diffusive image restoration, optimizing diffusion model performance in restoration tasks.

title: HRDiT: Training-Free High-Resolution Image Generation with Off-the-Shelf Diffusion Transformer Models
summary: HRDiT introduces a training-free method for high-resolution image generation by adapting off-the-shelf Diffusion Transformer models, extending capabilities beyond U-Net-based approaches.

title: Stable Curves, Unstable Items: Item-Level Scaling Heterogeneity in Video LLMs
summary: This research uncovers item-level scaling heterogeneity in Video LLMs, showing that aggregate scaling curves can obscure large, opposing changes in model performance for individual items.

title: Understand Before Detect: Vision--Language Learning for Omni-Domain Infrared Small Target Detection
summary: This research proposes a vision-language learning approach for omni-domain infrared small target detection, aiming to improve performance in challenging conditions with heterogeneous imaging domains.

title: YOLO-PEFT: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning on YOLO Family
summary: YOLO-PEFT is introduced as a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method specifically designed for the YOLO family of real-time detectors, addressing limitations of generic PEFT methods on their heterogeneous operators.

title: Explanation Stability of Test-Time Adaptation in Computational Pathology: A Large-Scale Benchmark
summary: This work presents a large-scale benchmark for evaluating the explanation stability of test-time adaptation methods in computational pathology, complementing accuracy assessments in a clinically relevant setting.

title: RoRA: Role-Oriented Regional Allocation for Visual Token Pruning in MLLMs
summary: RoRA introduces a role-oriented regional allocation method for visual token pruning in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), aiming to reduce the computational cost of processing long visual token sequences.

title: International Transfer of Stochastic Cortical Self-Reconstruction
summary: This research explores the international transfer of Stochastic Cortical Self-Reconstruction (SCSR), a method for personalized mapping of gray matter atrophy in neurodegenerative disorders like Alzheimer's disease.

title: Geometry-Aware Camera Localization for Bronchoscopy
summary: This research focuses on geometry-aware camera localization for bronchoscopy, addressing the need for millimeter-level precision and real-time guidance in medical procedures within confined anatomical structures.

title: Beyond Fluency: A Clinical Benchmark and Anomaly-Enhanced Baseline for Spine MRI Report Generation
summary: This paper introduces a clinical benchmark and an anomaly-enhanced baseline for automated spine MRI report generation, evaluating state-of-the-art Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for diagnostic accuracy in radiology.

title: Human-AI Perceptual Alignment by Playing Hues and Cues
summary: This work proposes a novel gamified evaluation framework called 'Hues and Cues' to assess human-AI perceptual alignment in Contrastive Vision-Language Models (CVLMs), moving beyond traditional benchmarks.

title: InstanceSplat: Instance-Aware Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting for Scene Understanding
summary: This paper introduces InstanceSplat, a feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting method for instance-aware 3D reconstruction and scene understanding, addressing limitations in existing category-oriented approaches.

title: Representation-driven Endoscopic Visual Embedding Alignment for Latent Generation
summary: This research explores representation alignment to improve the efficiency of developing foundation generative models, such as Diffusion Transformers, for endoscopic visual embedding and latent generation.

title: Flow-Corrected Shape Optimization: Taming Manifold Drift in High-Dimensional 3D Models
summary: This paper introduces Flow-Corrected Shape Optimization to address manifold drift, a critical failure mode encountered when optimizing 3D shapes within the latent spaces of deep generative models.

title: CANIS: Generation-Assisted 3D Canonicalization via an Image-Semantic Bridge
summary: CANIS is proposed as a category-agnostic, generation-assisted method for 3D object canonicalization, using an image-semantic bridge to achieve semantically meaningful orientations.

title: Fast and Accurate: An Adaptive VLA Inference Framework through Environment-aware Model Selection
summary: This paper presents an adaptive VLA inference framework that uses environment-aware model selection to balance inference speed and task success rate for embodied intelligence, combining fast reactive control with slow deliberative reasoning.

title: SyncSBC: Decentralized Swarm Behavior Prediction for Synchronized Autonomous Control
summary: SyncSBC is a method for decentralized swarm behavior prediction, enabling robot swarms to infer complex emergent behaviors from purely local perception for synchronized autonomous control.

title: SoRoMoX: Fast, Differentiable, and Parallelizable Soft Robot Models
summary: SoRoMoX provides fast, differentiable, and GPU-parallel soft robot models based on Cosserat-rod theory, designed to support advanced control-oriented workflows.

title: CrossTracer: Cross-Embodiment Navigation via VLA Model Reasoning and Trace Residuals Adapting
summary: CrossTracer is a hierarchical framework that enables cross-embodiment robot navigation by adapting VLA model reasoning to embodiment-specific mobility constraints using trace residuals.

title: AtlasVLA: Persistent World-Ego State Modeling for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: AtlasVLA introduces persistent world-ego state modeling for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, addressing the limitation of perception forgetting in embodied AI tasks, especially with single-camera setups.

title: Is Forward Prediction Enough? Physical State Grounding for JEPA World Models
summary: This research investigates whether forward prediction is sufficient for JEPA-based world models, proposing physical state grounding to enhance their learning of structured and control-relevant latent representations.

title: R2S-EGO: Dual-Proxy Refinement for Sparse-Capture Real-to-Sim
summary: R2S-EGO introduces dual-proxy refinement for sparse-capture real-to-sim, improving scene representations to generate observations along robot ego trajectories efficiently for simulation.

title: When Coordination Becomes a Threat: Communication Attacks in LLM-Controlled Multi-Robot Systems
summary: This paper examines the security risks of communication attacks in LLM-controlled multi-robot systems, highlighting vulnerabilities when Large Language Models are used as high-level planners for embodied robots.

title: Unordered Landmark Visual Navigation
summary: This research addresses image-goal navigation for embodied AI by developing a method for unordered landmark visual navigation, overcoming limitations of temporally ordered video streams or auxiliary sensors.

title: How Should I Pick a Foundation Model for My Robot? In Favor of a Community Evaluation Framework for Social Robots
summary: This paper advocates for a community evaluation framework for social robots to guide the selection of foundation models, arguing that current public leaderboards do not adequately assess real-time, embodied social interaction.

title: Spatiotemporal Agility: Time-Constrained Reinforcement Learning for Vision-Guided Dynamic Quadrupedal Interception
summary: This research develops spatiotemporal agility for legged robots using time-constrained reinforcement learning, enabling vision-guided quadrupedal interception in dynamic environments with strict temporal constraints.

title: Cross-View Action Consistency for Camera-Robust Vision-Language-Action Policies
summary: This paper explores cross-view action consistency to enhance scene-camera viewpoint robustness in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies, improving their reliability for embodied AI tasks using only RGB images, language, and proprioception.

title: Decoupling Intention from Trajectory: A Representational Deduction Framework for World Action Models
summary: This paper proposes a Representational Deduction Framework for World Action Models (WAMs) to decouple intention from trajectory, enhancing their ability to understand world state evolution and guide generative motion planning.

title: Automated Terminal-to-Housing Assembly System for Flat Ribbon Cable Harness
summary: This paper presents a sensor-minimal automated assembly system designed for bidirectional single-row flat ribbon cable harnesses, addressing the challenges of mechanically coupled multi-terminal insertion.

title: A Haptic Robot Finger Designed for Guqin Instrument Playing
summary: This research introduces a haptic robot finger designed for playing the Guqin instrument, aiming to enable more nuanced and interactive musical performance beyond conventional open-loop positional control in humanoid robotics.

title: Benchmarking and Reasoning Distillation of Large Language Models for Feedback Controller Design in Complex Dynamical Systems
summary: This paper focuses on benchmarking and reasoning distillation of Large Language Models for feedback controller design in complex dynamical systems, highlighting the need for evaluation beyond simple linear systems.

title: Real-time Whole-Body Motion Planning for Mobile Manipulators Carrying Arbitrarily Shaped Payloads via Kinematically-Coupled SVSDF
summary: This research focuses on real-time whole-body motion planning for mobile manipulators that carry complex payloads in cluttered environments, addressing issues with payload geometry and kinematic coupling.

title: C2Dex: Contact-Consistent Reconstruction and Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Monocular Video
summary: This paper introduces C2Dex, a method for contact-consistent reconstruction and retargeting of dexterous manipulation from monocular human videos to robots, addressing the challenge of transferring diverse manipulation behaviors.

title: Detection and Ranging of Transient Extrinsic Contacts Based on 6D Dynamic Tactile Sensing
summary: This research focuses on detecting and ranging transient extrinsic contacts during delicate manipulation using 6D dynamic tactile sensing, aiming to improve robotic systems' ability to localize subtle collisions.

title: LifelongCrossNav: Persistent 3D Semantic Memory for Cross-Floor Multi-Object Navigation
summary: LifelongCrossNav is a framework for sequential multi-object navigation in unknown environments, focusing on persistent 3D semantic memory to enable cross-floor navigation for object-goal tasks.

title: Representation Handoffs for OpenArm-Based Laboratory Mobile Manipulation
summary: This field report presents an OpenArm-based mobile manipulation prototype designed for laboratory automation, addressing the need for reliable alignment from language instructions and observations to safe actions in embodied AI.

title: TEMPO: Semantic-Action Decoupled RL Post-Training for Vision-Language-Action Models

title: What happens when medical students rely on AI – and never develop their own judgment? | Simar Bajaj and Joseph Sakran
summary: AI’s danger isn’t just in experts losing the ability to reason. It’s that trainees may never learn how to do so in the first place In healthcare, there’s growing concern over doctors becoming less clinically adept as they increasingly rely on AI tools. But what about the trainees – medical students, residents and fellows – who are using these tools before they have built their own clinical judgment? The idea of deskilling implies that someone possessed an ability and then lost it. Here, the danger is not just deskilling but never-skilling. Although a doctor who has forgotten how to reason is recoverable, one who never learned how may not be. OpenEvidence, essentially an AI chatbot for clinicians, has given this concern its most concrete form. About two-thirds of US doctors actively use OpenEvidence, asking about puzzling symptoms, drug interactions and clinical guidelines, getting responses within seconds, anchored in the latest research. Trainees, unsurprisingly, have also begun to use this AI tool in many of the same ways – but at a far more formative stage. Continue reading...

title: On Democratizing ASI to Preserve Civil Liberties
summary: I continue to believe we should pause frontier AI development. Any discussion of alternative strategies should be thought of as planning for contingencies. A unifying driver behind many post-alignment risks —catastrophic risks that remain even if we solve the alignment problem—is that by strong default, ASI would end liberal democracy . Liberalism—in which people have individual rights, autonomy, and the ability to choose their own destiny—is an important force protecting human welfare. [1] When people are free, we are reasonably good at making our lives better of our own volition. Many post-alignment risks have a certain flavor. AI-empowered terrorism; coups; permanent dictatorships; concentration of power. Those risks already exist today (and existed 20 years ago), but they're mitigated by the fact that power is relatively evenly distributed across people. The most powerful person in the world doesn't have an extraordinary advantage over the 10th-most-powerful person. ASI could change that. If people still have civil liberties post-ASI, that will only be because the controllers of ASI allow us to have them. [2] One way of thinking goes: AI will be extremely powerful. If everyone had their own personal AI, we could each use it to protect our own interests, and things will turn out okay for us. But how do you get there? It's not going to happen automatically, but it may be possible to set up a gradual process to keep power balanced. Cross-posted from my website . Democratizing AI vs. putting a democratic government in charge of AI The "democra" words (democracy, democratize) are overloaded with meanings, so I want to be clear about which meaning I'm referring to. By "democratizing AI", I'm talking about ensuring that many people have access to AI. One could also speak of a singleton AI that's controlled by a democratic government, or a singleton AI that's democratically controlled (people vote on what the AI should do). As Andy Masley writes , "homogenizing democracy" (as he calls it) entails forcing everyone to do what the majority wants. That's not good. That's why the title of this article speaks of "preserving civil liberties", rather than "preserving democracy". (To be fair, I do wish we would get to vote on whether AI companies should be allowed to build unsafe recursively self-improving superintelligence, rather than them getting to unilaterally build it and put all our lives at risk.) A sketch of how we might democratize AI To be clear: democratizing AI is not a great plan. But it's less bad than a lot of other plans. To be clear x2: for "democratizing AI" to be a "less bad plan", it has to be implemented with particular care. Otherwise, it's just a bad plan. The obvious way of democratizing ASI doesn't work: Someone has to build it and then voluntarily give it to everyone. What if they decide not to do that? Offense/defense balance issues: if attacking is easier than defending, then bad actors can use their personal ASI to do catastrophic damage. I doubt that it helps with the second problem, but a gradualist approach has some chance of sidestepping the first. (By which I mean it has maybe a 1–10% chance of working.) Here's the plan: Step 1. Give everyone their own personal smart-but-not-superintelligent AI assistant. Step 2. Make a marginal improvement to AI capabilities, so that the next-gen AI isn't enough of an improvement to defeat all the previous-gen AIs combined. Step 3. Give everyone the new and improved AI. Repeat. The idea is that if the leading AI developer decides not to do Step 3 (instead keeping the new AI for themselves), then they are risking a conflict with the rest of the world, and they can't win that conflict. There are many ways this plan could go badly, which are left as an exercise for the reader. What we should really do is pause AI development . Specifically, major countries should sign an international treaty agreeing not to build dangerous AI. The plan to "democratize AI" is riskier, but at the same time, it doesn't seem easier ? In order to preserve the balance of power, you need AI capabilities to advance slowly, and you need some way to enforce that. In short, you still need an international binding agreement not to build AI [except under certain narrow conditions], and not to use recursive self-improvement. You still need enforcement mechanisms like transparency and GPU monitoring; you still need a way for counterparties to shut down AI development if one party goes rogue (something like a remote kill switch on all the data centers). Two non-obvious issues with democratizing AI Democratizing AI has many issues. I will make note of two particular under-discussed problems. Liberalism only protects those inside it Even if we somehow succeed at preserving personal liberties by democratizing AI, and we succeed at making sure the AI is actually good for people, that still doesn't get us a good outcome. Most sentient beings alive today are non-human animals. Today's liberalism has failed to help them; almost all animals live lives much worse than humans' . Democratizing AI would not straightforwardly improve on the status quo. There is no realistic scenario where (e.g.) every factory-farmed chicken has her own superintelligent AI assistant. If we preserve liberalism-for-humans, that does not clearly flow into good outcomes for non-human animals, digital minds, and whatever other sentient beings may exist in the future. Beings who cannot assert their rights do not automatically benefit; other measures are required to ensure their well-being. AI proliferation increases catastrophic risks from competition Having many ASI agents with different goals could cause tremendous suffering via retributivism, war, unfortunate decision theory , or agents threatening torture (and making good on those threats) to incentivize other agents to do what they want. Center on Long-Term Risk and Center for Reducing Suffering have discussed this concern in more detail. For example, see Safe Pareto Improvements Research Agenda and Agential s-risks . And the lack of liberalism for animals has a lot to do with why life is so miserable for them. ↩︎ I read a version of this statement in a LessWrong comment, but I couldn't find the original source. ↩︎ Discuss

title: CMU-Drive and V2V-VLA: Cooperative Multi-agent Unified Driving with Reasoning Benchmark and Vehicle-to-Vehicle Vision-Language-Action Models
