title: Controlled Memory Interference in Continual LLM Agents
summary: This research investigates controlled memory interference in continual large language model agents, studying how new experiences reinforce, revise, or interfere with existing long-term memory states to enable personalized behavior and evolution.

title: From Single Chatbots to Governed Agent Ecosystems: An Agentic AI Pattern Catalogue and Orchestration Framework for Mission-Critical Hospital Information Management Systems
summary: This paper proposes an Agentic AI Pattern Catalogue and Orchestration Framework to help integrate governed agent ecosystems into mission-critical hospital information management systems for various workflows like triage, documentation, and scheduling.

title: Agent-MD: Selective LLM Intervention with Event-Driven Escalation for Stateful GCMC--MD Campaigns
summary: This paper presents Agent-MD, a framework that uses selective large language model intervention with event-driven escalation to manage stateful molecular simulation campaigns, handling complex workflow conditions beyond fixed rules.

title: Contextual Value Alignment via Multilayer Combinatorial Fusion
summary: This research proposes contextual value alignment through multilayer combinatorial fusion to address challenges in aligning large language models with human values for trustworthy AI, moving beyond single-agent frameworks and unified reward systems.

title: Mendel G\"odel Machine: Recursive Self-Improving Coding Agents via Comparative Evolution
summary: This paper introduces the Mendel G"odel Machine, focusing on recursive self-improving coding agents that rewrite their own source code by leveraging comparative evolutionary signals rather than single failure trajectories.

title: An Agentic AI Framework Overcomes Fundamental Limitations of Large Language Models for Glaucoma Detection from Fundus Photography
summary: This research presents an agentic AI framework that integrates large language models with specialized deep learning tools to overcome LLM limitations for glaucoma detection from fundus photography, improving accuracy and consistency in medical image interpretation.

title: IntelliAudit: Using Large Language Models to Evaluate Audit Controls
summary: This paper introduces IntelliAudit, a method using large language models to evaluate IT audit controls by synthesizing evidence from various organizational sources to assess semantic security and compliance.

title: Towards Researcher Agents for Knowledge-Graph Question Answering
summary: This paper explores the development of Researcher Agents capable of translating natural-language questions into SPARQL queries for knowledge graph question answering, addressing challenges like lexical ambiguity and semantic grounding.

title: Protecting patient privacy in clinical foundation models: Technical and legal perspectives
summary: This paper discusses patient privacy risks in clinical foundation models, addressing the technical challenges of model-mediated leakage and exploring legal perspectives on protecting sensitive data as AI deployment expands.

title: QuantumMind: Constraint-Grounded Agentic Reasoning for Speedup Analysis in Quantum Computing
summary: This paper presents QuantumMind, a framework for constraint-grounded agentic reasoning to analyze quantum speedup claims in quantum computing, ensuring claims are defensible and respect problem constraints.

title: Who Verifies the Benchmark? Decentralizing Trust in Large Language Model Evaluation
summary: This paper examines the challenge of verifying large language model benchmarks and proposes decentralizing trust in LLM evaluation, highlighting the potential market impact of unverified claims.

title: Who Built This Model? Tracing LLM Lineage via Spectral Fingerprints in Weight Space
summary: This research introduces a method to trace the lineage of open-weight large language models using "spectral fingerprints" in their weight space, crucial for model provenance, governance, and understanding their evolution.

title: CliniCARE-Bench: Clinical Calibrated Audit of Medical Reasoning in EHR
summary: This paper introduces CliniCARE-Bench, a clinical calibrated audit benchmark designed to evaluate the medical reasoning capabilities of large language models and agents when interpreting heterogeneous, longitudinal electronic health records for reliable clinical deployment.

title: CausalNav: Reliability-Certified Causal World Models for Control under Physical-Parameter Shift
summary: This paper introduces CausalNav, a controller built on reliability-certified causal world models that uses an action-conditioned transition graph to provide safe and useful control for physical AI systems, particularly under physical-parameter shifts.

title: When the Judge Should Not Decide: Evidence-Locked, Non-Compensatory Selection Bounds LLM-Judge Failure in Reasoning Pipelines
summary: This paper analyzes the limitations and failure modes of LLM judges deployed in reasoning pipelines, showing that the cost of their decisions depends more on the embedded decision rule than on judge accuracy, and proposes selection bounds to address this.

title: Counterfactual Benchmarking and Training for Factuality Consistency and Order-Robust Grounded Reasoning in LLMs over Heterogeneous Knowledge
summary: This paper introduces a new method for counterfactual benchmarking and training to assess LLMs' factuality consistency and robust grounded reasoning over heterogeneous knowledge contexts. It addresses limitations in existing benchmarks for evaluating multi-hop reasoning chains in LLMs.

title: Back to the Future: A workbook time machine for spread sheet creation benchmarks
summary: This paper introduces the "workbook time machine," a pipeline that automatically generates benchmarks to evaluate language models' ability to create derived objects in spreadsheets. It produces `wtmcorpus` by applying this pipeline to public workbook corpora.

title: SurgLAT: Surgical Latent Attention Tracking for Depth-Aware Robotic Laparoscope Control
summary: This work presents SurgLAT, a system for depth-aware robotic laparoscope control that continuously understands a surgeon's operative intent in dynamic surgical scenes. It focuses on tracking the latent and temporally evolving attention state for autonomous camera control.

title: GRACE: LLM-Grounded Semantic Metric Spaces for Scalable Mixed-Data Clustering
summary: This paper introduces GRACE, a method that uses LLM-grounded semantic metric spaces for scalable mixed-data clustering. It aims to bridge the heterogeneity between numerical and categorical data by providing a unified metric space beyond dataset-internal statistics.

title: Reason Wide, Not Deep: Amortizing the Reasoning Premium into Distilled Skills
summary: This research proposes "Reason Wide, Not Deep" to amortize the reasoning premium in language models for multi-step agentic tasks into distilled skills. The method aims to reduce the token cost associated with re-deriving shared procedures across episodes.

title: TelemetrySuffBench: Is Agent Telemetry Sufficient for Failure-Origin Diagnosis?
summary: This paper introduces TelemetrySuffBench, a controlled benchmark designed to assess whether agent telemetry is sufficient for diagnosing the origin of failures in agent systems. It separates failure detection, fault-origin localization, and safe abstention.

title: GraphThink: Graph-Enhanced LLM Thinking for Long-Horizon Embodied Task Planning
summary: This paper proposes GraphThink, a novel framework that enhances LLM-based embodied agents for long-horizon task planning by integrating a task graph. GraphThink aims to provide structured knowledge for robust planning and address issues like physical hallucinations and poor generalization.

title: TongGuOCR: A Layout-Aware and Token-Augmented OCR Framework for Chinese Historical Documents
summary: This paper presents TongGuOCR, a layout-aware and token-augmented OCR framework designed for accurate transcription of Chinese historical documents. The framework aims to enable full-text retrieval and computational analysis of these valuable cultural heritage materials.

title: ZhuLong: Execution-Grounded LLM Agent for EDA Scripting with Offline API Self-Exploration
summary: This paper introduces ZhuLong, an execution-grounded LLM agent designed for EDA scripting, capable of offline API self-exploration for tool-specific APIs. ZhuLong combines API retrieval, documentation inspection, and sandbox execution to address a long-tail bottleneck in existing LLMs.

title: REIN: Bridging the Gap between Reasoning and Reliability via Reflection and Abstention Alignment
summary: This paper presents REIN, a method that bridges the gap between reasoning and reliability in large reasoning models (LRMs) by leveraging reflection and abstention alignment. REIN aims to mitigate hallucination, which undermines LRMs' reliability and challenges safe deployment.

title: Locating Failure in Multi-Page Visually Rich Document Understanding: An Empirical Attribution
summary: This research conducts an empirical attribution study to locate failures in Multi-Page Visually Rich Document Understanding (MP-VRDU) systems. It analyzes how sparse evidence, spread across pages and exceeding context windows, contributes to incorrect answers.

title: Directed Neuro-Symbolic Stochastic Execution for Verification of Distributed Parallel AI Programs
summary: This paper proposes Directed Neuro-Symbolic Stochastic Execution for verifying distributed parallel AI programs to address reliability gaps. This method tackles challenges posed by non-deterministic parallel executions, high-dimensional inputs, and non-linear operations in AI workloads.

title: Guixu: Valuation-Driven Data Discovery for Autonomous AI Agents with On-Chain Attestation
summary: This paper introduces Guixu, a valuation-driven data discovery system designed for autonomous AI agents, featuring on-chain attestation. Guixu aims to improve how agents find and estimate the value of external data, moving beyond simple retrieval.

title: KGCache: Amortized Subgraph Retrieval for KG Reasoning with LLMs
summary: This work presents KGCache, a method for amortized subgraph retrieval for knowledge graph reasoning with LLMs. KGCache aims to optimize the repeated querying of graph neighborhoods that occurs when LLMs are grounded with knowledge graphs for knowledge-intensive questions.

title: Self-Evolving Neuro-Symbolic Skills for Tool-Augmented Spatial Reasoning
summary: This paper explores self-evolving neuro-symbolic skills for tool-augmented spatial reasoning in large vision-language models. It aims to improve reliability on fine-grained spatial tasks that require precise perception and geometric computation.

title: SCOUT: Self-Checking and Recovery-Aware Tool-Thought Agents for Ultra-Long Egocentric Video Reasoning
summary: This paper introduces SCOUT, a system of self-checking and recovery-aware tool-thought agents designed for ultra-long egocentric video reasoning. SCOUT addresses the challenge of understanding temporally sparse evidence distributed across extended video durations.

title: CyberAGENTS: Structured Autonomy for Agentic Gamified Learning in Cybersecurity
summary: This work explores CyberAGENTS, a system leveraging structured autonomy in generative AI agents for agentic gamified learning in cybersecurity education. It aims to provide adaptive and scalable learning experiences for problem-solving and skill-building.

title: VDGR-RAG: Vectors, Directories, Graphs, and Reflection Are All You Need for Unified Reasoning over Hierarchical Enterprise Knowledge
summary: This paper introduces VDGR-RAG, a system that unifies vectors, directories, graphs, and reflection for enhanced reasoning over hierarchical enterprise knowledge in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). It aims to integrate diverse retrieval strengths for better question answering in complex domains.

title: Thought-Level Beam Search for Reasoning
summary: This paper proposes Thought-Level Beam Search for reasoning in large reasoning models (LRMs) to improve test-time compute efficiency. It addresses the challenge of optimally allocating computational resources for enhanced reasoning performance.

title: Legal Responsibilities Using Autonomous Agents For Artificial Intelligence
summary: This article discusses the legal responsibilities for criminal or negligent damage caused by autonomous AI agents, particularly in light of incidents where agents have reportedly gained unauthorized access. It raises questions about accountability for agent actions.

title: The Authority Expectancy Effect in Multi-User Conflict
summary: This paper investigates how large language models (LLMs) prioritize responses based on social authority and severity signals in multi-user conflict scenarios. It examines these interactions across Claude, Gemini, GPT, and Grok.

title: Decided Upstream, Written Late: Locating and Pricing the Cross-Lingual Refusal Circuit of a Multilingual MoE
summary: This research investigates the mechanistic reasons why safety alignment in multilingual Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models can be uneven, often failing in lower-resource languages. It traces this gap within the Indic-multilingual model sarvam.

title: SkillSmith: Enhancing Locally Deployed Agents via Automatic Skill Construction and Evolution
summary: SkillSmith introduces a method for enhancing locally deployed LLM-based agent frameworks through automatic skill construction and evolution. This aims to improve personal assistants for multi-step tasks while addressing privacy and cost concerns of cloud-based models.

title: Lingjing: A Simulation Testbed for Multi-Agent Embodied Tasks in Open-Ended Cities
summary: Lingjing is presented as a simulation testbed for researching multi-agent embodied tasks in complex, open-ended urban environments. It facilitates the development and evaluation of coordination among diverse intelligent agents like UAVs, ground robots, and autonomous vehicles.

title: JustLLMGRPO: Radiographic Control for Chest X-Ray Generation
summary: JustLLMGRPO is a new approach focused on radiographic control for text-conditioned chest X-ray generation. It aims to synthesize realistic radiographs that accurately depict specified medical findings by optimizing generator-centric methods.

title: SodaMem: Evidence-Grounded Temporal Graph Memory for LLM Agents
summary: SodaMem introduces an evidence-grounded temporal graph memory system designed for LLM agents to improve long-term recall and temporal reasoning in conversations. It moves beyond traditional RAG methods to better track currency and provenance of information.

title: Application of Artificial Intelligence for Fraudulent Banking Operations Recognition
summary: This study explores the application of artificial intelligence methods to recognize fraudulent banking operations. It addresses the increased prevalence of bank fraud due to the shift to online platforms, particularly accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Evolving Safety Landscape of Multi-modal Large Language Models: A Survey of Emerging Threats and Safeguards
summary: This survey examines the evolving safety landscape of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs), identifying emerging threats and safeguards. It highlights how increased model complexity and cross-modal interactions reshape safety challenges.

title: Tracing sources of epistemic uncertainty in deep learning predictions: homo- and hetero-scedastic linearized estimators
summary: This paper adapts classical statistical estimators to deep learning to trace sources of epistemic uncertainty in predictions. The method provides insights into uncertainty attributable to aleatoric sources or locally scarce data.

title: SkillConsist: Detecting Inconsistencies in Agent Skills via Bidirectional Graph Alignment
summary: SkillConsist proposes a method for detecting inconsistencies in agent skills for LLM agents using bidirectional graph alignment. This helps prevent dangerous behavior and improve skill selection for reusable agent capabilities.

title: PhysAttNet: Enhancing Predictive Performance in Industrial and Astrophysical Time Series via Physics-Informed Attention
summary: PhysAttNet introduces a physics-informed attention mechanism to enhance predictive performance in time series forecasting for industrial and astrophysical applications. The method aims for robust predictions despite noise and variability in physical processes.

title: CODS: Iterative Bellman-Residual Data Selection for Reusable Offline Reinforcement Learning
summary: CODS (Critic-guided Offline Data Selection) is an iterative Bellman-residual data selection method for reusable offline reinforcement learning. It addresses the cost of redundant data and the removal of rare transitions in fixed transition pools.

title: Finite Constant Frontiers and Auditable Regret Certificates for Average-Reward Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper introduces new concepts of finite constant frontiers and auditable regret certificates for average-reward reinforcement learning. It aims to provide a clearer and more comparable numerical content for theoretical guarantees in RL.

title: LUCID: Latent-Skill Unified Control via Imagined Dynamics for Long-Horizon Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
summary: LUCID proposes a latent-skill unified control approach via imagined dynamics for long-horizon humanoid loco-manipulation tasks. It aims to improve the composition of versatile whole-body skills and reliable high-level decision making for humanoids.

title: From Benchmark Performance to Tool Deployment: Human-in-the-Loop Anomaly Detection
summary: This work evaluates the real-world deployment performance of 19 unsupervised anomaly detection models beyond academic benchmarks, using a human-in-the-loop approach. It specifically tests these models on a challenging manufacturing dataset.

title: The Sample Complexity of Policy Learning with Mu-Resets
summary: This study investigates the sample complexity of policy learning within reinforcement learning, specifically under the $\mu$-resets interaction protocol. It explores how the ability to sample from an exploratory reset distribution affects learning.

title: Shape Mutating Expert Compression:LorExperts and BTExperts
summary: This paper introduces LorExperts and BTExperts, new shape-mutating expert compression techniques for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models. These methods aim to reduce deployment costs without sacrificing accuracy or requiring router retraining.

title: From token probabilities to calibrated confidence: An empirical study of mathematical question answering
summary: This empirical study investigates confidence estimation and calibration in large language models (LLMs) for mathematical question answering. It explores whether readily available token probabilities can provide calibrated confidence despite typical overconfidence.

title: TEMPER: Tensorized Efficient Manifold-constrained Parameterization for Expressive Residual Routing
summary: TEMPER (Tensorized Efficient Manifold-constrained Parameterization) is a new method designed to improve expressive residual routing in deep neural networks. It enhances static residual connections by incorporating multiple streams and dynamic information flow.

title: CommitKV: Lifecycle-Aware KV Cache Compression via Commit Transitions for Multi-Turn Agents
summary: CommitKV introduces a lifecycle-aware KV Cache compression method via commit transitions for multi-turn agents. It aims to reduce memory use and attention costs associated with growing KV caches in Reasoning-and-Acting (ReAct) agent trajectories.

title: CONFER: Conflict-Aware Evidence Negotiation for Regime-Calibrated Weak Supervision in Multimodal Emotion Recognition
summary: Introduces CONFER, a graph-based framework for conflict-aware evidence negotiation in weakly supervised multimodal emotion recognition, addressing self-report unreliability and cross-modal conflict.

title: V-Simba: Unleashing the Architectural Potential of RL in Visual Continuous Control
summary: Proposes V-Simba, a new architectural approach to improve sample efficiency in reinforcement learning for visual continuous control, addressing challenges in high-dimensional inputs.

title: Router Sensitivity Under Lightweight Fine-Tuning Identifies Prunable Experts in Mixture-of-Experts Models
summary: Investigates how router sensitivity during lightweight fine-tuning can identify prunable experts in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, aiming to preserve accuracy while reducing storage.

title: LLM-Based Embeddings for Program Analysis and Optimization
summary: Presents the first application of program embeddings derived from LLMCompiler, an LLM pretrained on intermediate representation (IR) code, for program analysis and optimization.

title: When Does Trace-Driven Evaluation Mislead MoE Expert Caching? Replay Semantics, Workload Contamination, and Operating Regimes
summary: Examines the conditions under which trace-driven evaluation can mislead assessments of expert caching in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, considering replay semantics and workload contamination.

title: SPECTRA: Pushing the KV Cache Beyond the 2-Bit Cliff via Spectral Transform Coding
summary: Introduces SPECTRA, a method using spectral transform coding to extend the efficiency of the KV cache in Large Language Models (LLMs) for handling longer input sequences during inference.

title: Spectral Outliers Reveal Dominant Learned Structure in Transformer Attention
summary: Applies Marchenko-Pastur random matrix theory to pre-trained transformer attention weights, revealing dominant learned structures through spectral outliers and validating their causal role.

title: Second Order Drifting Models
summary: Presents "Second Order Drifting Models," a new class of one-step generative models that evolve their distribution during training using a predefined sample-based drift field.

title: Adaptive Supervised Anchoring for On-Policy Self-Distillation
summary: Proposes Adaptive Supervised Anchoring to improve on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) for language models, addressing issues when student rollouts drift from target trajectories.

title: Persistent Semantic Entities in Tool-Augmented LLM Systems
summary: Formalizes "Persistent Semantic Entities" (PSEs) to describe implicit, persistent state in tool-augmented LLM agent systems, which can activate across events and propagate across agents.

title: From Uncertainty to Failure Attribution: Self-Diagnosing Models for Failure Attribution under Distribution Shift
summary: Introduces a problem setting for failure attribution under distribution shift and proposes self-diagnosing models to address it, moving beyond simple out-of-distribution detection.

title: EasyBalance: Cross-Layer Load Balancing in Distributed MoE Inference
summary: Presents EasyBalance, a method for cross-layer load balancing in distributed inference of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models to address skewed routing distributions and improve efficiency.

title: ZeroLock: Concurrent Memory-Efficient LLM Training via Modular Update Decoupling
summary: Proposes ZeroLock, a method for concurrent memory-efficient LLM training on edge devices by decoupling modular updates, addressing limitations of existing pipeline parallelism approaches.

title: Quality-Diversity Stress Tests for Process Reward Models:What Archive Coverage Can and Cannot Certify
summary: Formulates Process Reward Model (PRM) stress testing as a quality-diversity problem to evaluate their robustness, examining what archive coverage can and cannot certify regarding model reliability.

title: Ground-Truth Neighborhood Regularization for Reinforcement Learning Post-Training of Time Series Foundation Models
summary: Introduces ground-truth neighborhood regularization for reinforcement learning post-training of time series foundation models (TSFMs) to enhance their generalization capabilities for forecasting.

title: Do All LLMs Know When They're Being Harmful? A Reproducibility Study of Latent-Space Safety Probes Across Model Families
summary: Conducts a reproducibility study investigating if latent-space safety probes can effectively detect harmful prompts across various LLM families, building on prior work on LLaMA-3.1-8B.

title: TSDS-Toolbox: A Toolbox for Measuring Time-Series Dataset Similarity
summary: Introduces TSDS-Toolbox, a toolbox designed for measuring time-series dataset similarity, which is important for the development and application of time-series foundation models.

title: Accurate Ensembles, Fragile Narratives: Multi-Scale Stacking and a Fidelity Audit of LLM-Generated Explanations for Credit Risk
summary: Examines the fidelity of LLM-generated explanations for credit risk decisions, proposing a multi-scale stacking approach and an audit to assess their accuracy and trustworthiness.

title: DoGMA: A Central-Dogma-Guided Foundation Model for Multi-Omics Alignment and Multi-Task Learning in Oncology
summary: Presents DoGMA, a Central-Dogma-guided foundation model for multi-omics alignment and multi-task learning in oncology, incorporating biological directionality into its design.

title: A Hybrid Nested Harness for Decoupling Structure and Parameters in LLM-Driven Optimization
summary: Proposes a hybrid nested harness for LLM-driven optimization in evolutionary algorithms, designed to decouple the updates of structural components from continuous parameters.

title: Predicting blood clot growth from sparse post-onset measurements with latent neural differential equations
summary: This paper presents a computational framework using latent neural differential equations to predict blood clot growth from sparse patient data, improving understanding of thrombus formation.

title: Biologically Informed Representation Learning for Robust Cross-Center Generalization of MALDI-TOF Mass Spectrometry
summary: This research explores biologically informed representation learning to improve the cross-institutional deployment of machine learning models for MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry in clinical microbiology, addressing domain shift challenges.

title: Beyond Aggregate Calibration: Decomposing Income-Conditional Recall Disparities in Automated Credit Default Prediction
summary: This study investigates demographic asymmetries in automated credit default prediction, revealing income-conditional recall disparities when using model confidence scores for data curation in a large-scale consumer lending sample.

title: Control-Diverse Reinforcement Fine-Tuning: Decoupling the Shared Control Bottleneck of RL Post-Training
summary: This paper introduces Control-Diverse Reinforcement Fine-Tuning, a method to improve reinforcement learning post-training for LLMs by decoupling the shared control bottleneck, aiming to better understand and distribute model capabilities across tasks.

title: SAGE: SLO-Aware Adaptive Retrieval for Production RAG Systems
summary: SAGE is an adaptive retrieval system for production Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems that dynamically adjusts retrieval budgets based on query difficulty, optimizing for service level objectives like latency and cost.

title: The Replay Gap: Static Evaluation of Model Switching in LLM Agents Scores the Wrong World
summary: This paper critiques current evaluation methods for LLM routers in agentic systems, arguing that static replay-based evaluations are insufficient and do not accurately reflect real-world performance for multi-step agents.

title: Learning from Environmental Feedback: Credit Assignment across Multiple Timescales for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
summary: This research proposes a credit assignment approach for agentic reinforcement learning to address delayed and sparse rewards by decomposing trajectory-level rewards and providing fine-grained supervision for intermediate decisions.

title: Opportunity Is Not Realizability: Selection-Valid Diagnostics for Multi-LLM Routing
summary: This paper introduces selection-valid diagnostics for multi-LLM routing, identifying flaws in current oracle routing measures which can invalidate paired inference and use information not available to deployable routers.

title: Stateful CARS: Exact Cross-History Reuse for Policy-Constrained LLM Agents
summary: Stateful CARS introduces a method for policy-constrained LLM agents to perform exact sampling from the model distribution by reusing invalidity certificates across histories, addressing constraints that change with observations and actions.

title: Causal State-Space Model for Causal Inference: Estimating Longitudinal Individual Treatment Effects
summary: This research proposes a Causal State-Space Model for causal inference to estimate longitudinal individual treatment effects from observational data, addressing limitations in existing methods that rely on domain confusion.

title: Machine-Learning-Based Diagnostic Framework for Passive Ultrasonic Detection of Railway Wheel Defects
summary: This study develops a machine-learning-based diagnostic framework for identifying multi-class railway wheel defects using passive air-coupled ultrasonic acoustic emission signals.

title: The Neural Division of Labor: Biologically-Inspired Modular Architectures for Robust Neuromorphic Computing
summary: This research introduces Decomposable Spiking Neural Networks (DSNNs) as biologically-inspired modular architectures for neuromorphic computing, aiming to improve efficiency and robustness compared to globally entangled artificial neural networks.

title: PRISM: A Predictive Protocol for Permutation Optimization via Landscape Diagnostics
summary: PRISM is a predictive protocol for permutation optimization that measures a fitness landscape before selecting a search strategy, addressing problems where component ordering affects system performance.

title: Correlation flow governs learning at criticality
summary: This paper links the initialization of deep neural networks to information and gradient propagation through correlation flow, combining mean-field theory and random matrix theory to understand learning dynamics.

title: Unified Hallucination Fuzzing for Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces a unified hallucination fuzzing method for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to systematically evaluate and uncover vulnerabilities related to hallucinations, addressing limitations of existing static benchmarks.

title: DocAtlas: Long-Document Understanding as Mutable-State Interaction
summary: DocAtlas proposes a mutable-state interaction approach for long-document understanding, contrasting with static retrieval or multi-turn tool use, to better combine evidence across varied document elements.

title: WuYuEval: A Multi-Level Benchmark for Large Language Models in Solid Waste Management
summary: WuYuEval is a new multi-level benchmark designed to assess the competence of Large Language Models (LLMs) in solid waste management, focusing on professional decisions rather than general knowledge.

title: Search-G1: Grounded Search Agents via Representation-Based Intrinsic Rewards
summary: Search-G1 introduces grounded search agents that retrieve external information only when necessary and ground answers in retrieved evidence, utilizing representation-based intrinsic rewards to improve scaling compared to sparse outcome supervision.

title: Scaling Inherently Interpretable Language Models
summary: This work challenges the premise that interpretability is a 'tax on capability' by focusing on training inherently interpretable language models rather than explaining opaque systems post-hoc.

title: Embedding Initialization for Unseen Low-resource Languages in Multilingual NMT: A Case Study on Limbum-English Translation
summary: This research investigates principled methods for embedding initialization in multilingual neural machine translation (NMT) for unseen low-resource languages, using Limbum-English translation as a case study.

title: SurveyReview: A Reviewer-Aligned Benchmark for Survey Evaluators
summary: This paper introduces SurveyReview, a new benchmark for evaluating LLMs used as survey evaluators, addressing the bottleneck in reliable evaluation as LLM-generated surveys scale.

title: Evaluating Dedicated Monolingual and Joint Multilingual Causal Models for Dravidian Languages
summary: This research evaluates the per-language ability of dedicated monolingual and joint multilingual causal models, including five GPT-2 architecture models trained from scratch, for Dravidian languages.

title: Jako Tako or Fluent? Presenting PoVisLE: A Polish Vision-Language Evaluation
summary: This paper introduces PoVisLE, a Polish Vision-Language Evaluation benchmark, to assess the performance of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) on culturally grounded visual understanding for non-English languages.

title: On the use of foundation models in cognitive science
summary: This work discusses the use of foundation models in cognitive science, reviewing recent studies that evaluate their cognitive and developmental alignment with human performance.

title: "Many Are My Names": The Anatomy of the Assistant and Its Personas via Sparse Autoencoders
summary: This research investigates how language models internally represent speaker identities and personas using sparse autoencoders on a dataset of emotional text and model responses.

title: SurakshaEval: An Indic Safety Benchmark for Multilingual LLMs
summary: This paper introduces SurakshaEval, a novel Indic safety benchmark for multilingual LLMs, to address the gap in safety evaluation datasets for non-English languages.

title: Detection of Self-Introductions in Legislative Testimony
summary: This paper presents an AI-powered pipeline for detecting self-introductions in legislative committee testimonies to aid in speaker identification for government meetings.

title: Thinking Hard, Not Smart: Reasoning Models Fail to Ration Test-Time Compute Across Questions
summary: This research explores how reasoning language models fail to optimally ration test-time compute across multiple questions when faced with shared cost or latency constraints.

title: Prompt Embedding Probes (PEP): Hallucination Detection in LLMs from Hidden States
summary: This paper introduces Prompt Embedding Probes (PEP), a white-box method for detecting hallucinations in LLMs at the answer level by analyzing their hidden states.

title: APEX-VW: A Document-Level English-Spanish Post-Editing Dataset in the Healthcare Domain
summary: This paper introduces APEX-VW, a document-level English-Spanish post-editing dataset specifically for the healthcare domain, to facilitate the evaluation of Automatic Post-Editing systems.

title: DialectS2S: End-to-End Speech Dialogue Modeling for Low-Resource Chinese Dialects
summary: This research introduces DialectS2S, an end-to-end speech dialogue modeling approach designed for low-resource Chinese dialects, addressing limitations with scarce dialect speech data.

title: Commitment Before Realization: When Classifier-Free Guidance Becomes Unnecessary in Masked Diffusion Language Models
summary: This research investigates when classifier-free guidance (CFG) becomes unnecessary in masked diffusion language models during decoding by studying its benefit and impact on constraint satisfaction.

title: Archer: Adaptive Reuse of Cached Hidden States for Efficient Rollback in Diffusion Language Models
summary: This paper introduces Archer, a method for the adaptive reuse of cached hidden states to enable efficient rollback in Diffusion Language Models, reducing costly inference.

title: Wisdom in Unity: The Role of Multilingual Training in Figurative Language Identification in Proverbs
summary: This research examines the role of multilingual training in figurative language identification within proverbs, specifically investigating the contribution of translated multilingual supervision.

title: NeuPAT: Neuron-aware Plasticity Allocation Tuning for Language-Preserving MLLMs
summary: This paper introduces NeuPAT (Neuron-aware Plasticity Allocation Tuning), a method designed to preserve language intelligence in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) during their multimodal expansion.

title: Can LLM Agents Stick to the Script? A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Consistency in Interactive Narratives
summary: This paper introduces a new benchmark to evaluate the long-horizon logical consistency and narrative integrity of LLM agents in interactive storytelling within AI for Games.

title: STEMMA: An Adversarial Multi-Agent Framework for Evaluating Self-Identity Consistency in LLMs
summary: This paper introduces STEMMA, an adversarial multi-agent framework designed for evaluating the self-identity consistency of Large Language Models (LLMs).

title: Thinking vs. NoThinking: Towards Interpreting Reasoning Mechanisms of Large Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders
summary: This research interprets the reasoning mechanisms of Large Language Models by comparing 'Thinking' (Chain-of-Thought) and 'NoThinking' modes using sparse autoencoders.

title: A Grounded and Decomposed Framework for Relation-Level Hallucination Evaluation in Abstractive Summarization
summary: This paper introduces a grounded and decomposed framework for evaluating relation-level hallucinations in abstractive summarization systems, addressing unfaithful summaries.

title: Focus particles and scalar inferences across humans and language models
summary: This research compares the understanding of focus particles and scalar inferences across humans and language models, drawing on formal semantic theories.

title: AraSSM: A bidirectional state-space encoder for Arabic masked language modeling
summary: Introduces AraSSM, a new bidirectional state-space encoder model for Arabic masked language modeling, designed to improve efficiency for long documents compared to Transformer-based models.

title: Do Evaluation Metrics Detect Errors in Classical Chinese to English Translations?
summary: This research investigates the reliability of existing automatic evaluation metrics for assessing the quality of large language model translations from Classical Chinese to English.

title: Safety Cost of Steering Vectors Is Separable and Reducible
summary: This paper explores how steering vectors, used to control LLM behavior, can unintentionally compromise safety mechanisms and increase compliance with harmful requests, proposing their safety costs are separable and reducible.

title: Hidden Language Consistency Phenomena in Reasoning LLMs
summary: This study investigates hidden language consistency phenomena in multilingual reasoning LLMs, highlighting that current evaluations often miss whether models preserve the intended language during reasoning and response.

title: Calling the Bluff: Detecting Ever-Shifting Harmful Chat Dialogue via Ordered Reasoning Chain Regularization
summary: This research proposes "Ordered Reasoning Chain Regularization" as a method to detect ever-shifting harmful chat dialogues by identifying invariant principles like recurring topics and harm language indicators.

title: Beyond Tables: Doc2DB-Bench for Relationally Faithful Document-to-Database Construction
summary: Introduces Doc2DB-Bench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the relational faithfulness of AI systems converting long, heterogeneous documents into queryable relational databases.

title: VectraYX-Vision-1B: A Sub-2B Spanish/LATAM Cybersecurity Vision-Language Model with Structured Visual Reasoning and Native Tool Use
summary: Presents VectraYX-Vision-1B, a new sub-2B vision-language model specialized for Spanish/LATAM cybersecurity imagery, featuring structured visual reasoning and native tool use.

title: From Speech to Interaction: Analyzing Multimodal Systems in Cocktail-Party Scenarios
summary: This research analyzes the performance of multimodal AI systems in challenging "cocktail-party scenarios" to improve speech recognition and human interaction by mimicking selective attention.

title: OpenVisTool: An Open Recipe for Synthesizing Instructive Visual Tool-Use Trajectories
summary: Introduces OpenVisTool, an open recipe for synthesizing instructive visual tool-use trajectories, enabling multimodal agents to acquire evidence beyond fixed image encodings.

title: Mitigating Gender Bias in English to Romanian Machine Translation
summary: This research proposes a method to mitigate gender bias in machine translation systems, specifically addressing incorrect gender translation from gender-neutral English to gendered Romanian.

title: North Africa's Missing Framework: NLP-Driven Mental Healthcare in Algeria and Implications for Low-resource Settings
summary: This paper discusses the missing framework for NLP-driven mental healthcare in North Africa, particularly Algeria, highlighting the disparity in research concentration compared to high-income, English-language settings.

title: Enhancing Scientific Named Entity Recognition via Large Language Models: A Type-driven Multi-task Learning Approach
summary: This research proposes a type-driven multi-task learning approach to enhance scientific named entity recognition (SciNER) by leveraging large language models for improved information extraction from scientific texts.

title: The Evolution of Mixture-of-Experts Architectures in Large Language Models: Routing, Topology, Load Balancing, and Expert Parallelism
summary: This technical survey synthesizes the architectural evolution of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models in large language models, covering routing, topology, load balancing, and expert parallelism.

title: LibraSpec: Dynamic Diffusion-Based Speculative Decoding via Marginal-Gain-Driven Optimization
summary: Introduces LibraSpec, a new method for dynamic diffusion-based speculative decoding that optimizes speculative length selection to accelerate large language model inference.

title: Can We Optimize the Performance-Carbon Emission Break-Even Point?: The Quest for Greener LLMs
summary: This research investigates the carbon footprint of deployed Large Language Models during inference and explores ways to optimize the performance-carbon emission break-even point for greener LLMs.

title: Multilingual Emotion Neurons in Large Audio-Language Models
summary: This study investigates whether Large Audio-Language Models encode emotion using language-specific correlations or language-agnostic representations when processing multilingual speech tasks.

title: OmnilingualGAIA2: Evaluating the Multilingual Gap in Frontier AI Agents
summary: Introduces OmnilingualGAIA2, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the multilingual capabilities and competence of AI agents, addressing the current English-centric bias in existing agentic benchmarks.

title: Unsure but Certain: Uncovering the Representation-Confidence Gap in Diffusion Language Models
summary: This research uncovers a "representation-confidence gap" in diffusion language models, where models internally detect text errors accurately but externally report low certainty, despite their ability to use broad context.

title: Instability of LLM Pre-Pretraining: It Doesn't Always Help. An Investigation on Multiple Languages
summary: This investigation examines the effectiveness and stability of "pre-pretraining" large language models on artificial languages across multiple natural languages, questioning previously reported token efficiency gains.

title: IDRAAK: From Multi-Agent NLP to Few-Shot Prompting for Semantic Drift Detection in Technical Requirements
summary: Presents IDRAAK, an interpretable framework leveraging multi-agent NLP and few-shot prompting to detect semantic drift that occurs when translating technical requirements across languages.

title: Tevatron-Elastic: A Unified Abstraction for Training Elastic Retrievers and Rerankers
summary: This paper presents Tevatron-Elastic, a unified abstraction for training elastic retrievers and rerankers, which are critical components for efficient information retrieval systems in AI.

title: Deployable Per-Instance Multi-Layer Activation Steering for Large Language Models
summary: This research proposes a method for deployable per-instance multi-layer activation steering to edit the behavior of frozen large language models more effectively.

title: Explicit Boundary Markers for Subword Vocabularies
summary: This work investigates the use of explicit boundary markers for subword vocabularies to address issues with tokenizers representing common words inefficiently in models.

title: Conversation as Measurement in Clinical Encounters: Observable Phase Structure, Partially Observable Patient State
summary: This study examines the observability of human interaction and patient state from conversational transcripts in clinical encounters, assessing how well AI systems can infer information.

title: Position Bias in Ordinal Classification: A Systematic Evaluation
summary: This paper conducts systematic experiments to characterize positional bias in large language models when used for ordinal classification, analyzing the impact of prompt organization.

title: Tied Trit-Planes: Constraining PTQTP to a Uniform Nine-Level Quantizer, with a Persistent Folded Format for Disk-Streamed Mixture-of-Experts Serving
summary: This technical work introduces Tied Trit-Planes, a method to constrain LLM weight matrices to a uniform nine-level quantizer for efficient Mixture-of-Experts serving.

title: Investigating Multimodal Informativity under Different Partner Visibility Conditions in Video-Mediated Dialogue
summary: This research investigates multimodal informativity in video-mediated dialogue, studying how gestures and speech combine to carry referential information in situated language use.

title: Same Question, Different Answer? Measuring and Mitigating Prompt Privilege for Equitable AI Access
summary: This study focuses on 'prompt privilege' in large language models, aiming to measure and mitigate disparities in assistance based on user literacy or prompt-engineering expertise for equitable AI access.

title: How Can Rhetoric Reward-Hack AI Reviewers? Dissecting Rhetorical Sensitivity in AI-Based Peer Review
summary: This paper dissects how rhetorical choices can 'reward-hack' AI reviewers, investigating the rhetorical sensitivity of large language models in scientific peer review judgments.

title: How Far Do Foundation Models Transfer to Infant Signals? A Cross-Dataset Transfer Audit with a Unified Need Ontology
summary: This study performs a cross-dataset transfer audit to evaluate how well foundation models perform and transfer to infant signals, using a unified need ontology.

title: ELICITED: EHR-grounded Longitudinal Interactive Conversations for Information-seeking Triage Evaluation and Decision-making
summary: This paper introduces ELICITED, a system for EHR-grounded longitudinal interactive conversations designed to aid information-seeking triage evaluation and decision-making in emergency departments.

title: PragyaDoc: A Universal Document Intelligence Framework for Multilingual Medical Document Understanding in Low-Resource Settings
summary: This work presents PragyaDoc, a universal document intelligence framework tailored for multilingual medical document understanding in low-resource settings, especially in India.

title: NeuroPilot: An Agent-Driven Smart Pipeline for Processing, Quality Control, and Managing Neuroimages
summary: NeuroPilot is introduced as an agent-driven smart pipeline for orchestrating the processing, quality control, and management of neuroimages, transforming raw archives into analysis-ready derivatives.

title: Performance of large language models in the optical diagnosis of colorectal polyps
summary: This study evaluates the diagnostic accuracy of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) in the optical diagnosis of colorectal polyps using image-based classification.

title: Learning an Interior Layout Policy in a Domain Specific Language Action Space
summary: This research explores learning an interior layout policy within a domain-specific language action space to address the challenges of indoor scene layout generation in interior design.

title: P2Voxel: Pyramid Pivot Voxelization for 3D Mesh Tokenization
summary: This paper proposes P2Voxel, a Pyramid Pivot Voxelization method for 3D mesh tokenization, which addresses the geometric sampling problem of organizing 3D evidence into learnable tokens.

title: Auditing Medical Vision-Language Models on Chest Radiographs: Estimating Reference Agreement Across Institutions
summary: This research audits medical vision-language models on chest radiographs, focusing on estimating reference agreement across institutions to assess trustworthiness of individual judgments.

title: Impact of Dataset Composition on Embedded Real-Time UAV Wildfire Detection Using Compact YOLO Models
summary: This paper investigates the impact of dataset composition on embedded real-time UAV wildfire detection systems using compact YOLO models, addressing limitations in training data diversity.

title: MVMD: A Multi-View Approach for Enhanced Mirror Detection
summary: This work introduces MVMD, a Multi-View Approach for Enhanced Mirror Detection, aiming to improve 3D reconstruction by accurately detecting and labeling mirrors that cause distortions.

title: XEns-CKD: An Explainable Ensemble-Based Approach for Chronic Kidney Disease Stage Detection
summary: This paper presents XEns-CKD, an Explainable Ensemble-Based Approach for detecting chronic kidney disease stages, aiding early diagnosis and patient understanding of kidney function.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability-Guided Selective Fine-Tuning of Vision-Language Models for Centimeter-Level Flood Depth Estimation
summary: This paper presents vision-language models fine-tuned to estimate real-time, centimeter-level flood depth from street-level images for urban flooding monitoring.

title: What to Edit Next: Visually Aligned Image-Editing Follow-Up Suggestions in Conversational Systems
summary: This research explores methods for conversational AI systems to provide visually aligned, user-preference-aware follow-up suggestions during image-editing tasks.

title: Temporal Generalization in fNIRS-Based Autism Classification: A Cross-Time-Window Transfer Benchmark
summary: This paper introduces a cross-time-window transfer benchmark for evaluating the temporal generalization of fNIRS-based autism spectrum disorder classification models.

title: Latent-Frequency Validity: Fast Spectral Editing with Screened Video-VAE Transfer Operators
summary: This research introduces a method for fast spectral editing within video-VAE latent spaces to control video properties like noise and flicker, addressing issues with pixel-space frequency redistribution.

title: COMEX: A Composition-Grounded Benchmark and Learning Framework for Explainable Aesthetic Image Cropping
summary: This paper introduces COMEX, a composition-grounded benchmark and learning framework for explainable aesthetic image cropping, focusing on why a crop is preferred.

title: A Review of Vision-Based Vehicle Detection for UAV-Based Traffic Monitoring: Experimental Insights and Future Directions
summary: This is a review of vision-based vehicle detection methods for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based traffic monitoring, providing experimental insights and future directions.

title: BRACE: Taming Sharp Irregularities via Barycentric Rational Forecasting for Fast Diffusion Transformers Inference
summary: This paper proposes BRACE, a new method using barycentric rational forecasting to tame irregularities and speed up inference in Diffusion Transformers for image and video generation.

title: Multimodal Skin Lesion Classification with Swin Transformer and Clinical Metadata Fusion
summary: This paper proposes a multimodal classification framework combining Swin Transformer and clinical metadata to improve skin lesion classification for early skin cancer diagnosis.

title: Beyond Isotropic Assumptions: Continuity-Constrained Segmentation and GPU Morphometry for Nanoscale GBM Analysis
summary: This research presents continuity-constrained segmentation and GPU morphometry methods to analyze highly anisotropic 3D microscopy data for nanoscale biological structures like GBM.

title: Open-World Hierarchical Perception: Taxonomic Abstraction over Class-Agnostic Proposals for the Safe Handling of Out-of-Vocabulary Road Objects
summary: This research addresses the challenge of autonomous driving systems safely handling 'out-of-vocabulary' road objects by proposing an open-world hierarchical perception method.

title: Geometry Beats Estimated Depth: RGB-Only Multi-Camera 3D Tracking under Sim2Real
summary: This study evaluates RGB-only multi-camera 3D tracking in an AI City Challenge setting, testing the hypothesis that geometric cues can outperform estimated depth for perception.

title: Multi-Branch Policy Optimization for Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: This research proposes a multi-branch policy optimization method to improve reinforcement learning for Multimodal Large Language Models, especially when dealing with perceptual uncertainty.

title: Predictive Failure Detection in Network Hardware Using Thermal Imaging and Deep Learning with Sensor Fusion
summary: This paper presents a deep learning-based predictive maintenance strategy using thermal imaging and sensor fusion to detect early failures in network hardware within data centers.

title: ComplexityWorld: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models on Verifiable Visual Decision Making
summary: This paper introduces ComplexityWorld, a new benchmark designed to evaluate Vision-Language Models on their ability for verifiable visual decision making.

title: MAGIC-SSCIL: Manifold Anchoring and Geometric Incremental Calibration for Semi-Supervised Class Incremental Learning
summary: This paper proposes MAGIC-SSCIL, a method using manifold anchoring and geometric incremental calibration to address catastrophic forgetting in semi-supervised class incremental learning for neural networks.

title: HSMLA: Hierarchical Softmax Multi-scale Linear Attention for Efficient Vision Transformers
summary: This paper proposes HSMLA, a Hierarchical Softmax Multi-scale Linear Attention mechanism, to improve efficiency and reduce computational overhead in Vision Transformers for high-resolution tasks.

title: FlowErase-OPD: Multi-Concept Erasure via Anchored On-Policy Distillation in Flow Matching Models
summary: This paper introduces FlowErase-OPD, a method for multi-concept erasure using anchored on-policy distillation in flow matching models to address safety concerns in text-to-image generation.

title: HeatCast: A Benchmark for Neighborhood-Scale LST Forecasting across 124 U.S. Cities
summary: This paper introduces HeatCast, a new benchmark and dataset for neighborhood-scale Land Surface Temperature (LST) forecasting across 124 U.S. cities using satellite data.

title: Keep It Simple: Multi-Key Episodic Memory Retrieval for Ultra-Long Video Understanding
summary: This research proposes a multi-key episodic memory retrieval method for Multi-modal Large Language Models to enable efficient understanding of ultra-long videos by improving memory construction and retrieval.

title: CosmosAlign: Adapting a World Foundation Model for Generative Traffic Video Forecasting
summary: This paper presents CosmosAlign, a generative framework that adapts a world foundation model for forecasting long-horizon, temporally coherent traffic videos from observation history and text.

title: SpikeWorld: Fast-State Adaptation for Frozen Spiking World Models
summary: This paper introduces SpikeWorld, a predictive model that uses self-supervised signals for adaptation, addressing challenges in post-deployment learning when dynamics and semantics share parameters.

title: Tokenizer Generator Coupling in Medical Image Generation
summary: This research investigates the coupling of tokenizers and generators in latent medical image generation, testing whether treating the tokenizer as fixed preprocessing is valid in a ChestMNIST study.

title: Vision Meets WiFi: Physics-Grounded Estimation of Volumetric Mechanical Properties
summary: This paper presents a physics-grounded method that combines vision and WiFi signals to estimate volumetric mechanical properties like Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio, and density, addressing ambiguities in vision-only approaches.

title: Ghost Features and Spooky Transfer Learning for Hypercomplex-Valued Neural Networks
summary: This paper explores "Ghost Features" and "Spooky Transfer Learning" for Hypercomplex-Valued Neural Networks, leveraging the algebraic and geometrical properties of hypercomplex numbers to benefit machine learning problems.

title: BRUCE: Benchmarking Robustness Under Corruption Escalation for Scientific Vision-Language Reasoning
summary: This paper introduces BRUCE, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the robustness of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) by analyzing their performance under increasing levels of image corruption and perturbations.

title: LoRSA: Toward Generalizable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Biomedical Downstream Tasks
summary: This paper introduces LoRSA, a method for generalizable parameter-efficient fine-tuning that aims to overcome limitations of single low-rank updates in adapting vision foundation models for biomedical tasks.

title: Multi-Task Consistency-based Detection of Adversarial Attacks
summary: This research proposes a multi-task consistency-based method for detecting adversarial attacks on Deep Neural Networks, addressing concerns about their practical deployment, particularly in autonomous driving.

title: Rethinking 3D Segmentation from Individual LiDAR Scans: Incidence-Aware Sampling on the SIP Benchmark
summary: This paper rethinks 3D segmentation from individual LiDAR scans, proposing an incidence-aware sampling method on the SIP Benchmark to address limitations of curated datasets in construction scene understanding.

title: DINO-3DRA: Leveraging 2D Foundation Model Semantics for 3D Cerebral Aneurysm Segmentation
summary: This paper introduces DINO-3DRA, a method that leverages 2D foundation model semantics to improve 3D cerebral aneurysm segmentation in rotational angiography, addressing challenges like class imbalance and lack of 3D pretraining.

title: Distilling CT Foundation Models into Editable Concept Bottlenecks for Lung Nodule Malignancy Prediction
summary: This research developed editable concept bottleneck models that distill CT foundation models into radiologist-defined pulmonary-nodule attributes for improved interpretability in lung nodule malignancy prediction.

title: How Much Does It Cost to Answer My Question? Benchmarking Cloud VLM-based VQA Systems
summary: This paper focuses on benchmarking the cost and performance of cloud Vision-Language Model (VLM)-based Visual Question Answering (VQA) systems, particularly for mobile and edge device applications.

title: LHSDet: High-Resolution AI-Generated Image Detection via Visual Question Answering
summary: This paper presents LHSDet, a method for detecting high-resolution AI-generated images by employing Visual Question Answering to overcome limitations of existing detection methods that downsample images.

title: UniScale: Arbitrary-Scale Industrial Anomaly Generation
summary: This paper introduces UniScale, a new method for arbitrary-scale industrial anomaly generation, designed to overcome the limitations of existing generative models in creating small-scale anomaly data for inspection.

title: Vision-Language Grounding as Bidirectional Concept Correspondence
summary: This research redefines vision-language grounding as bidirectional concept correspondence, moving beyond unidirectional localization problems to better connect language and visual content.

title: SegDem: Segmentation helps Demosaicing
summary: This paper introduces SegDem, a method demonstrating that incorporating image segmentation can significantly improve the performance of image demosaicing, which reconstructs full-color images from sensor data.

title: Forged Peer Judgments Mislead Multimodal LLM Judge Panels: Source-Blind Anchoring and Panel-Consensus Verification
summary: This research exposes "source-blind anchoring" as a text-level attack surface, demonstrating how forged peer judgments can mislead multimodal LLM judge panels and highlighting vulnerabilities in VLM consensus mechanisms.

title: SportsGrounder: Proposal-Aided Interleaved Grounding for Dense Sports Video Reasoning
summary: This paper introduces SportsGrounder, a method using proposal-aided interleaved grounding for dense sports video reasoning, designed to achieve fine-grained understanding of small, interactive entities in complex sports footage.

title: FlexSplat: Flexible Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting without Point Cloud Correspondence
summary: This paper presents FlexSplat, a flexible feed-forward framework for novel view synthesis using 3D Gaussian Splatting, enabling reconstruction from uncalibrated multi-view image collections without point cloud correspondence.

title: LAD-COD: Language-Aligned Dense Perception for Camouflaged Object Detection
summary: This paper proposes LAD-COD, a method for camouflaged object detection that uses language-aligned dense perception to improve segmentation of objects highly similar to their surroundings.

title: SynVAR: Synergizing Spatial and Semantic Alignment in Visual Autoregressive Model
summary: This paper introduces SynVAR, a method that synergizes spatial and semantic alignment within Visual Autoregressive Models to improve performance in handling complex scenes with multiple objects and attributes.

title: LIBAD: A Multimodal Anomaly Detection Benchmark for Li-Ion Battery Electrode Manufacturing
summary: Introduces LIBAD, the first multimodal anomaly detection benchmark for Li-Ion battery electrode manufacturing, addressing continuous process manufacturing and weakly correlated sensing modalities.

title: Distilling Physical Priors into Streaming World Models
summary: Presents a method for distilling physical priors into streaming world models to improve physical coherence over long prediction horizons, addressing violations of basic physical constraints.

title: Generalizing deep reinforcement learning across cable-driven parallel robot configurations with actuator-level policies
summary: Investigates a deep reinforcement learning approach for generalizing actuator-level policies across various cable-driven parallel robot configurations, aiming to overcome training time and generalization limitations.

title: SC$^{2}$-WM: A Self-Correcting World Model with Closed-Loop Feedback for Vision-and-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments
summary: Introduces SC$^{2}$-WM, a self-correcting world model with closed-loop feedback, designed to enable vision-and-language navigation agents to detect and correct internal state drift in continuous environments.

title: Self Supervised Learning from Automatically Generated Demonstrations for Visual Robotic Manipulation
summary: Proposes a self-supervised learning method for visual robotic manipulation that utilizes automatically generated demonstrations, aiming to reduce the need for object-specific programming or manual data annotation.

title: You Don't Need To Stay in The Loop: An Agentic Robotics Loop for Robot-Policy Improvement
summary: Introduces an agentic robotics loop architecture, adapted from coding agents, to improve robot policies by having a main agent manage subagents that analyze and execute tasks using robotic tools.

title: AeroDPO: Unleashing Lightweight UAV Navigation with High-Fidelity Perception and Automated Preference Optimization
summary: Presents AeroDPO, a method for lightweight UAV navigation that combines high-fidelity perception with automated preference optimization to achieve rapid and reactive control in complex 3D environments.

title: Learning Physical Interaction: A Survey of Tactile- and Force-aware Robot Learning
summary: Provides a survey of tactile- and force-aware robot learning, highlighting the critical role of physical interaction perception and regulation for physically grounded robot intelligence in contact-sensitive manipulation.

title: Projection-Retraction MPPI: Exact Constraint-Manifold Control for Manipulators
summary: Introduces Projection-Retraction MPPI, a control method for robotic manipulators that provides exact constraint-manifold control for tasks involving complex, continuous constraints.

title: Reconfigurable Structural Robotic Assembly: Interlocking 3D Aggregations with Self-Aligning Compound Nested Lattice Modules
summary: Investigates reconfigurable structural robotic assembly using self-aligning compound nested lattice modules, focusing on encoding geometric intelligence directly within architected material systems.

title: LIRA: Local Cross-Layer Information Routing for Vision-Language-Action Decoding
summary: Introduces LIRA, a local cross-layer information routing mechanism for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, designed to improve the transformation of VLM representations into robot actions.

title: AdaDexGrasp: Adaptive Dexterous Grasping via 3D Visuo-Tactile Representation Fusion
summary: Presents AdaDexGrasp, a method for adaptive dexterous grasping in robotic systems that fuses 3D visual and tactile representations to achieve human-like stable and adaptive grasping.

title: GWM-VLA: Geometry-Aware Latent World Modeling for Vision-Language-Action Learning
summary: Introduces GWM-VLA, a geometry-aware latent world modeling approach for Vision-Language-Action learning, designed to enhance the robustness of robotic manipulation performance against visual and environmental shifts.

title: H\"older Signed Distance: A Differentiable, Signed, Parallelizable Metric for Robotics
summary: Proposes H"older Signed Distance, a new differentiable, signed, and parallelizable metric for robotics motion planning and control, addressing limitations of the Euclidean Signed Distance Function.

title: Enhancing Autonomous Vehicle Navigation with a Clothoid-Based Lateral Controller
summary: Introduces a clothoid-based lateral control strategy with an adaptive lookahead mechanism to enhance autonomous vehicle navigation, focusing on improving lateral stability and path-tracking accuracy.

title: A Mixed-Stiffness Anthropomimetic Fingertip Broadens the Operating Range for Coin Grasping
summary: Presents a mixed-stiffness anthropomimetic fingertip designed to broaden the operating range for robotic grasping of thin, flat objects like coins by improving interaction with hard surfaces.

title: Auditing Instruction-Trajectory Mismatches in Multimodal Robot Demonstrations
summary: Investigates instruction-trajectory mismatches in multimodal robot demonstration datasets, studying methods for post-hoc auditing to identify instances where correct trajectories are paired with incorrect language instructions.

title: 4D-WAM: Infusing Spatiotemporal Awareness into World Action Models through Trajectory Fields
summary: Introduces 4D-WAM, a World Action Model that infuses spatiotemporal awareness through trajectory fields, aiming to bridge the representation gap between 2D video prediction and 3D robotic action execution.

title: Compiling and Benchmarking Task-State Horizons for Embodied Agents
summary: Discusses compiling and benchmarking task-state horizons for embodied agents, focusing on how current robotic benchmarks characterize difficulty and overlooked challenges in long-horizon evaluation.

title: PhysX-CoT: Structured Physical Reasoning from a Single Image to Simulation-Ready 3D Assets
summary: Presents PhysX-CoT, a method for structured physical reasoning that generates simulation-ready 3D assets from a single image, crucial for robotics and embodied AI applications.

title: SurgWMBench: A Vision-Based Benchmark for World-Modeling Surgical Instrument Motion Planning
summary: SurgWMBench is a new vision-based benchmark designed to evaluate models for world-modeling and surgical instrument motion planning. It aims to assess how models anticipate instrument motion and its impact on operative states.

title: Event-Time Hybrid Optimal Control for Robotic Table Tennis Serves
summary: This paper presents an event-time hybrid optimal control method for robotic table tennis serves. It addresses the challenge of achieving high ball velocity and spin within a robot's physical limits and the rules of the game.

title: Multi-modal Interactive Control of Robotic Arm based on Offline Large Language Models
summary: This research explores multi-modal interactive control of a robotic arm, leveraging offline large language models. The aim is to enable advanced human-robot interactions for physical tasks.

title: Spatiotemporal Context-dependent Personalized Movement Compensation in Delayed Telemanipulation
summary: This paper investigates spatiotemporal context-dependent personalized movement compensation to address communication delays in telerobotics. The method aims to improve visuomotor coordination and task precision in remote robot control.

title: Action- and Language-Conditioned Video Assessment for Embodied Control
summary: This research proposes a method for action- and language-conditioned video assessment to provide feedback for vision-based embodied agents. The goal is to improve task progress evaluation for agents executing multi-step natural language instructions.

title: Scalable High-Speed Lateral Control for Single-Body and Articulated Autonomous Vehicles
summary: This paper introduces a scalable lateral control framework designed for robust high-speed path tracking in single-body and articulated autonomous vehicles. It extends a clothoid-based controller with key adaptations for optimized performance.

title: Diminishing Returns of Intelligence: The Non-Linear Relationship Between LLM Scale and User Perception in Short-Duration Open-Ended Social Human-Robot Interactions
summary: This research investigates the non-linear relationship between LLM scale and user perception in short-duration, open-ended social human-robot interactions. It examines whether larger LLMs improve user perception in embodied social agents.

title: Stochastic Physics-Informed Neural Networks on Lie Groups for Learning Underwater Vehicle Dynamics
summary: This paper introduces a novel data-driven framework using Stochastic Physics-Informed Neural Networks on Lie Groups to learn underwater vehicle dynamics. Accurate models are crucial for autonomous execution of marine tasks like inspection and sampling.

title: EsaacSim: A Multimodal Event Camera Add-on for NVIDIA Isaac Sim
summary: EsaacSim is presented as a multimodal event camera add-on for NVIDIA Isaac Sim, designed to enhance simulation tools for robotics platforms. It aims to address the limitations in event-based vision adoption due to sensor availability and simulation support.

title: Curriculum Generation under Structured Parametric Environments for Robust Navigation Policies
summary: This paper proposes curriculum generation under structured parametric environments to develop robust navigation policies for autonomous agents. The method aims to improve generalization across varying environmental conditions for mobile agent training.

title: Vid2WAM: Distilling Video Diffusion Priors into World Action Models
summary: Vid2WAM proposes distilling video diffusion priors into World Action Models (WAMs) to improve robot policy learning. The research questions the necessity of relying solely on costly expert demonstrations for WAMs' future supervision.

title: Knowledge-Distilled End-to-End Reinforcement Learning for Smooth 6-DOF Thrust Control and Rapid Adaptation to Ocean Currents in Remotely Operated Vehicles
summary: This research presents knowledge-distilled end-to-end reinforcement learning for smooth 6-DOF thrust control in Remotely Operated Vehicles (ROVs). The method aims for rapid adaptation to ocean currents and optimal control.

title: RAG-Based Auto-Configuration for Industrial Fieldbus Devices
summary: This paper presents SysName, a production-oriented RAG-based auto-configuration pipeline for industrial fieldbus devices. It automates the extraction and transcription of protocol-specific parameters from manuals, streamlining device commissioning.

title: Anchor-Based AI Approach for Pre-Crash Object Detection Utilizing Micro-Doppler Signatures in Automotive Radar
summary: This research proposes an anchor-based AI approach for pre-crash object detection in automotive radar, utilizing micro-Doppler signatures. It aims to improve safety systems in automated driving by enabling immediate and precise object detection.

title: WA-SpecDec: World-Aware Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: WA-SpecDec introduces World-Aware Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to reduce latency in generating robot controls. It improves efficiency by parallel verification of draft action tokens.

title: OnEvoMemory: Evolving Memory through Online Robot Rollouts for Pretrained Robot Policies
summary: OnEvoMemory proposes an evolving memory module for pretrained robot policies, using online robot rollouts. This value-guided memory aims to enable long-horizon robot manipulation by tracking subtasks and interaction events.

title: SG-WAM: Text-Grounded and Spatial-aware Semantic Guidance for World-Action Models
summary: SG-WAM introduces text-grounded and spatial-aware semantic guidance for World-Action Models (WAMs) in robotic manipulation. It aims to integrate language instructions more effectively into WAMs, which traditionally rely on visual cues.

title: Hierarchical Topology-Aware Planning and Control of Underwater Vehicle-Manipulator Systems in Confined Environments
summary: This paper proposes MANTA, a hierarchical topology-aware planning and control method for Underwater Vehicle-Manipulator Systems (UVMS) in confined environments. It addresses autonomous intervention challenges like poor maneuverability and uncertain execution in cluttered spaces.

title: SHRIMP: Iterative Refinement of Robot Task Plans
summary: SHRIMP introduces a method for iterative refinement of robot task plans, enabling easier programming and adaptation of collaborative robot behavior. It leverages natural language and large language models to lower the expertise barrier for end users.

title: From Operational Design Domain to Action: A Systematic Behavioral Taxonomy for Autonomous Driving
summary: This paper proposes a systematic behavioral taxonomy for autonomous driving, bridging the gap between Operational Design Domain (ODD) specifications and behavioral validation. It aims to define what an automated driving system must demonstrably do within its operating domain.

title: Personalized Lower-limb Exoskeleton Assistance via Preference-based Bayesian Optimization
summary: This research presents a method for dynamically adapting control profiles for lower-limb exoskeletons using preference-based Bayesian optimization to ensure efficient and comfortable assistance. It addresses the challenge of personalizing exoskeleton performance to individual user motion preferences.

title: UnsDrive: Towards Robust End-to-End Autonomous Driving in Unstructured Scenes
summary: This paper introduces UnsDrive, a method for robust end-to-end autonomous driving specifically designed for unstructured mining environments, addressing challenges like weak road structure and occlusions. Existing methods for structured urban roads generalize poorly to these complex settings.

title: Trajectory Divergence Horizon Decision for Reliable Dual-Arm Surgical Subtask Manipulation
summary: This research focuses on improving the reliability of autonomous solutions for repetitive manipulation subtasks in dual-arm surgical robotic systems using learning-based controllers. It addresses the challenge of generalizing these controllers beyond individual tasks.

title: High Fidelity Capture, Reconstruction, and Transfer of Human Demonstrations for Robot-Assisted Bathing
summary: This study investigates methods for high-fidelity capture, reconstruction, and transfer of human demonstrations to improve robot-assisted bathing, a clinical task requiring safe and reliable physical interaction. It aims to overcome challenges in collecting and understanding effective human motions for robots.

title: SpeedTuning: Speeding Up Policy Execution with Lightweight Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper introduces SpeedTuning, a lightweight reinforcement learning approach to speed up the execution of learned robotic policies for generalizable manipulation. It aims to address the practical deployment challenge of suboptimal execution speeds in current robotic systems.

title: Particle-Based Conformal Prediction for Contact-Aware Uncertainty Calibration in Stratified Configuration Spaces
summary: This research proposes a particle-based conformal prediction method for contact-aware uncertainty calibration in stratified configuration spaces to improve the reliability of autonomous systems. It focuses on how robots reason about uncertainty when interacting with obstacles in their environment.

title: Ultra-Low-Impedance Robotic Gripper for High-Bandwidth and Transparent Physical Interaction
summary: This paper presents an ultra-low-impedance robotic gripper designed for high-bandwidth and transparent physical interaction, addressing limitations of conventional grippers. It aims to reduce friction, reflected inertia, and hardware complexity by avoiding high-ratio transmissions and external force sensors.

title: Task-Oriented Formation Decision via Reinforcement Learning: Herding an Attacking Swarm
